summary: Target-level plan for completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility over Q and its definite-quaternionic and patched variants. R31.1 specialises CompletedCohomologyPartII’s completed tower to modular curves (imported CC.8 identification), proves the degree-zero, degree-two and compact-support facts and the non-Eisenstein injectivity and freeness of Emerton §5.3, and constructs the completed modules of quaternionic Shimura curves and of definite quaternion algebras over totally real fields. R31.2 identifies locally algebraic vectors with classical cohomology (Emerton’s Theorem 7.4.2 with its degree and vanishing inputs), proves density of classical vectors, compares with newforms, recovers classical cohomology from completed homology with coefficients (Nakamura), and gives the quaternionic classical comparisons and type-specialised modules. R31.3 constructs the completed Hecke algebra T(K^p) and T_{ρ̄,Σ} from CC.8, the Hecke-valued determinant and representation, the deformation-to-Hecke surjection, the Galois factorisation Ĥ^1 ≅ ρ^m ⊗ U, Zariski density of classical points, the definite quaternionic big Hecke algebra and Pan’s pro-modular primes. R31.4 builds the local Langlands families over T, the multiplicity module X(θ), and proves Emerton’s refined local–global compatibility (Theorem 6.2.13), his Theorem 1.2.1 with both residual hypotheses, the mod p Theorem 1.2.6, Nakamura’s dual form for completed homology, Dospinescu–Le Bras’s local–global compatibility for a definite quaternion algebra, Pan’s semisimple local–global compatibility, and (conditionally on Scholze’s functor) the CDN comparison. R31.5 constructs the CEGGPS patched module for GL_n(F) and the quaternionic patched completed homology, with type-specialised modules, Emerton–Paškūnas support, Tung’s full support at odd p and at p = 2, and Pan’s patching at nice primes and in the residually irreducible case. R31.6 states promodularity and its Fontaine–Mazur and Kisin consequences, Böckle’s R = T, the global proof of Emerton’s Theorem 3.3.22, Dospinescu–Le Bras’s quaternionic globalisation, the globalisation-dependence audit and the export table (inputs CC1–CC5 of GL2ModularityLifting). The local p-adic Langlands inputs are requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.2–R30.6, which has no plan yet; Scholze’s functor is a recorded gap.

nodes.title: Completed cohomology of the modular tower
nodes.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite with integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k, and let G = GL_2(Q_p). For a compact open K_f ⊂ GL_2(A_f) let Y(K_f) be the modular curve GL_2(Q)∖((C∖R) × GL_2(A_f)/K_f) with its canonical model over Q. For A ∈ {O, O/ϖ^s, E} and a tame level K^p ⊂ GL_2(A_f^p) put H^1(K^p)_A = colim_{K_p} H^1_ét(Y(K_pK^p)_{Q̄}, A), the colimit over compact open K_p ⊂ G, and likewise H^1_c(K^p)_A with compact supports and H^0(K^p)_A. The completed cohomology at tame level K^p is the ϖ-adic completion Ĥ^1(K^p)_O = lim_s H^1(K^p)_O/ϖ^s, and Ĥ^1(K^p)_E = E ⊗_O Ĥ^1(K^p)_O, an E-Banach space with unit ball Ĥ^1(K^p)_O; the same recipe gives Ĥ^1_c(K^p) and Ĥ^0(K^p). Taking the locally convex (O-linear) inductive limit over tame levels gives Ĥ^1_A = colim_{K^p} Ĥ^1(K^p)_A for A = O, E. For a finite set Σ_0 of primes not containing p, Σ = Σ_0 ∪ {p} and an open K_{Σ_0} ⊂ G_{Σ_0} = ∏_{ℓ∈Σ_0} GL_2(Q_ℓ), put Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_A = Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ)_A with K_0^Σ = ∏_{ℓ∉Σ} GL_2(Z_ℓ), and Ĥ^1_{A,Σ} = colim_{K_{Σ_0}} Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_A. These carry commuting continuous actions of G_Q, of G, of the tame group (GL_2(A_f^p), resp. G_{Σ_0}) and of the Hecke operators T_ℓ, S_ℓ for ℓ ∉ Σ(K^p). The carrier is the CompletedCohomologyPartII coefficient-limit object H̃^1(K^p, O) of the modular tower transported along CC.8's modular realisation; no second completed-cohomology carrier is defined. The object of Emerton’s Conjecture 1.1.1 is the multiplicity space Hom_{E[G_Q]}(V, Ĥ^1_E) of a two-dimensional E-representation V of G_Q, with its GL_2(A_f)-action.
hypotheses: E/Q_p finite, O its integers, ϖ a uniformizer, k = O/ϖ.
Group actions follow Emerton lg §2: the G- and GL_2(A_f)-actions are those of Carayol twisted by g ↦ (g^{-1})^t (lg p. 45, footnote 11); this convention is fixed for the whole roadmap.
Ĥ^1_E is a colimit of Banach spaces with the locally convex inductive-limit topology; it is not itself ϖ-adically complete, and the tame colimit is taken after completion.
proofSteps: Identify the finite-level étale cohomology groups with the CC.0/CC.1 modular tower through CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/arithmetic-tower-realisation (modular family, with ModularCurvesPartII R14.3 supplying the finite étale/Betti comparison); the p-level colimit at fixed s is CC.1's fixed-exponent object and the s-limit is CC.2's coefficient-limit completion.

Emerton’s isomorphism (5.1.1), H^1(K^p)_O/ϖ^s ≅ H^1(K^p)_{O/ϖ^s}, is torsion-freeness of H^1(K^p)_O plus vanishing of the ϖ-torsion of the degree-two groups in the colimit (EM-PAMQ Lemma 7.2.1); it identifies Ĥ^1(K^p)_O with lim_s colim_{K_p} H^1(Y(K_pK^p), O/ϖ^s), which is CC.2's object (EM-PAMQ Corollary 7.2.4).
Transport the G_Q- and Hecke actions with CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/transported-arithmetic-actions; the G-action is CC.1's smooth action through conjugated levels, extended by continuity.

Form the tame colimit with CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.1/tame-level-variation; the transition maps are closed embeddings (EM06 Proposition 2.2.13), so the O-linear inductive-limit topology of lg p. 45, footnote 10, is Hausdorff.

sources.match: Defines H^1(K^p)_A as the p-level colimit of étale cohomology of the modular curves, Ĥ^1(K^p)_O as its ϖ-adic completion with the reduction isomorphisms (5.1.1)–(5.1.2), the Banach space Ĥ^1(K^p)_E, the tame colimit Ĥ^1_A with its inductive-limit topology, the fixed-away-from-Σ variants Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0}) and Ĥ^1_{A,Σ}, and the compactly supported and degree-zero analogues.

The local–global conjecture is a statement about the multiplicity space of V in Ĥ^1_E; Remark 1.1.2 records the case (V|G_{Q_p} a twist of an extension of the cyclotomic character by the trivial character) in which it is expected to fail as stated.
Torsion-freeness and separatedness of H^1_*(K^p)_O, the Banach completion Ĥ^1_*(K^p)_E, and its identification with lim_s colim_{K_p} of the mod ϖ^s cohomology, for ordinary and compact supports.
Nakamura recalls the same objects Ĥ^i(K^p), Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0}) and Ĥ^1_Σ with the inductive-limit topology, which his zeta morphisms consume.

For a fixed tower the survey defines Ĥ as the p-adic completion of the direct limit and H̃ as lim_s lim_r H(X_r, Z/p^s); for the modular tower in degree one these agree at each tame level by (5.1.1) of EM11.

acceptance: Ĥ^1(K^p)_O/ϖ ≅ colim_{K_p} H^1(Y(K_pK^p), k), G_Q × G-equivariantly (EM11 (5.1.2) with s = 1).
For K^{p′} ⊂ K^p the pullback Ĥ^1(K^p)_E → Ĥ^1(K^{p′})_E is a closed G-equivariant embedding, and the K^p-invariants of Ĥ^1_E are Ĥ^1(K^p)_E (the theorem R31.1/arithmetic-actions-and-admissibility).

uses.how: The multiplicity space Hom_{E[G_Q]}(V, Ĥ^1_E) is the target of the local–global maps.
Localising at a residual maximal ideal gives the ρ̄-part Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}, a direct summand.
Its Pontryagin–Schikhof dual is completed Borel–Moore homology, the source of the zeta morphisms.
Pan identifies H̃^1(K^p, Z_p) with perfectoid cohomology; the request to R31.1 asks for this carrier with its admissible actions.
Odd-prime lifting through local–global compatibility uses this carrier.

tests.statement: Ĥ^0_E is isomorphic to the space of functions on Q_{>0}∖A_f^× that are continuous in the p-adic variable and smooth away from p, with G_Q acting through class field theory and GL_2(A_f) through det (EM-PAMQ (60)); a wrong definition that completes before taking π_0 of the tower fails this.

nodes.title: Admissibility, tame-level control and the arithmetic actions
nodes.statement: For every tame level K^p: (a) Ĥ^1(K^p)_E with the G-action is an admissible unitary E-Banach representation of G = GL_2(Q_p), and Ĥ^1(K^p)_O is ϖ-adically admissible: Ĥ^1(K^p)_O/ϖ is an admissible smooth k-representation of G; the same holds for compact supports. (b) The natural map Ĥ^1(K^p)_E → (Ĥ^1_E)^{K^p} is a G-equivariant isomorphism, under which T_ℓ (resp. S_ℓ) corresponds to the double coset K^p diag(ℓ,1) K^p (resp. K^p diag(ℓ,ℓ) K^p) for ℓ ≠ p unramified in K^p. (c) For K^{p′} ⊂ K^p the pullback Ĥ^1(K^p)_E → Ĥ^1(K^{p′})_E is a closed embedding, equivariant for G and for the Hecke operators at primes unramified in both levels. (d) The G_Q-action on Ĥ^1(K^p)_O is continuous, unramified outside Σ(K^p) = {p} ∪ {ℓ : K^p ramified at ℓ}, and commutes with G and the Hecke operators; on Ĥ^1_E the G_Q-action commutes with GL_2(A_f).
hypotheses: Tame levels are compact open subgroups of GL_2(A_f^p); (b) is stated for the E-Banach spaces; the integral analogue needs neatness or the localisation of R31.1/non-eisenstein-boundary-and-injectivity.
Admissibility is in the sense of Schneider–Teitelbaum: the Schikhof dual of a G-stable unit ball is finitely generated over O[[H]] for one, hence every, compact open H ⊂ G.
proofSteps: Each modular curve Y(K_f) is homotopic to a finite one-dimensional simplicial complex; this verifies the finite-cell hypothesis of CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.5/banach-admissibility, and the local group is the compact p-adic analytic GL_2(Z_p), so CC.5 gives (a) (EM06 Theorem 2.2.11, EM-PAMQ Lemma 7.2.5).

(b) is the averaging argument over K^{p′} ⊂ K^p normal, made integral by the transfer of CC.1 and passing to completions; it is EM06 Theorem 2.2.16(ii); the Hecke statement is EM-PAMQ Lemma 7.2.8 (which cites a proposition of the published version of EM06 whose number does not match the 2006 draft read here).
(c) is EM06 Proposition 2.2.13: the pullback is split, after inverting p, by the normalised trace, so its image is closed.

(d) is the transport of R31.1/the-object-the-conjecture-is-about’s G_Q-action; unramifiedness outside Σ(K^p) follows from good reduction of Y(K_pK^p) at ℓ ∉ Σ(K^p) for K_p fixed and is preserved by the colimit and completion (EM-PAMQ 7.2.9).

sources.locator: Theorem 2.2.11, p. 31; Proposition 2.2.13, p. 32; Theorem 2.2.16, p. 33
sources.match: Admissibility of the completed cohomology of arithmetic quotients as Banach G-representations, closedness of the tame-level pullbacks, and recovery of a fixed tame level as invariants.
The modular-curve statements: admissible unitary Banach representation, closed tame-level embeddings, invariants and Hecke double cosets, and the G_Q-action commuting with G and Hecke.
Emerton records that the G-action makes Ĥ^1(K^p)_O ϖ-adically admissible in the sense of his Definition 3.1.1.

acceptance: The proof of (a) applies CC.5 only after the finite-cell and compact p-adic analytic hypotheses are verified for the modular tower.
Concrete instance: for K^p = K_1(N)^p and a weight-two newform f of level N prime to p, the f-isotypic part of H^1(Y_1(N), E) embeds in (Ĥ^1_E)^{K^p} by (b).

nodes.title: Degree zero, vanishing in degree two and compact supports
nodes.statement: For the modular tower: (a) Ĥ^0_E ≅ C(Q_{>0}∖A_f^×, E), the space of functions continuous in the p-adic variable and locally constant away from p, with G_Q acting through G_Q^{ab} ≅ Q_{>0}∖A_f^× (class field theory) and GL_2(A_f) through det; at tame level K^p, Ĥ^0(K^p) restricted to a small compact open H ⊂ Z(Q_p) is a direct sum of copies of C(Z_p^×, E). (b) Ĥ^2_c = 0, and Ĥ^n = Ĥ^n_c = 0 for n ≥ 3; the p-adically completed H^2 (without supports) vanishes as well, because each Y(K_f) is a non-compact curve. (c) The forget-supports maps Ĥ^1_c(K^p)_O → Ĥ^1(K^p)_O and Ĥ^1_{c,E} → Ĥ^1_E are surjective. (d) Cup product defines continuous pairings Ĥ^0_E ⊗ Ĥ^1_{*,E} → Ĥ^1_{*,E} for * ∈ {∅, c}, and cupping with the class of a continuous character ψ of Q_{>0}∖A_f^× twists T_ℓ to ψ(ℓ)T_ℓ and S_ℓ to ψ(ℓ)^2 S_ℓ.
hypotheses: The degree-zero description uses the determinant π_0(Y(K_f)) ≅ Q_{>0}∖A_f^×/det K_f; continuity is in the p-adic variable only.
(b) and (c) are statements about the completed objects; finite-level H^2_c is nonzero.
proofSteps: (a): H^0 of each Y(K_f) is the space of functions on π_0(Y(K_f)) = Q_{>0}∖A_f^×/det K_f; the colimit over K_p and ϖ-adic completion give continuous functions in the p-adic direction (EM-PAMQ (60)); the restriction to a small H ⊂ Z(Q_p) follows since H acts through det on the components (EM06 proof of Proposition 4.3.1).

(b): for K_p fixed choose K_p′ ⊂ K_p with [K_pSL_2(Q_p) : K_p′SL_2(Q_p)] divisible by p^r; the pullback on H^2_c multiplies by a multiple of p^r on each component, so colim_{K_p} H^2_c is p-divisible and its p-adic completion vanishes (EM06 Proposition 4.3.6). Non-compact curves have no H^2 and no cohomology above degree 2.

(c): compare H^1_c with parabolic cohomology H^1(X(K_f)) of the compactified curves and show that the cokernel of H^1_c → H^1, the boundary cohomology, becomes p-divisible in the colimit for the same index reason (EM06 Proposition 4.3.9; EM-PAMQ 7.2.10); the boundary sequence is CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.7/boundary-long-exact-sequences-and-the-borel-serre-tower applied to the modular tower.
(d): CompletedCohomologyPartII cup products on the tower, with the twisting formula of EM-PAMQ Lemma 7.3.19.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.3.1 and its proof, p. 52; Proposition 4.3.6, p. 53; Proposition 4.3.9, p. 54
sources.match: Ĥ^0 restricted to a small central subgroup is a sum of C(Z_p^×, E); Ĥ^2_c vanishes by the p-divisibility of the colimit of H^2_c; Ĥ^1_c → Ĥ^1 is surjective.
Surjectivity of forgetting supports, the explicit description of Ĥ^0_E, the cup product with Ĥ^0, and the twist of Hecke operators by cupping with a character.
Nakamura uses the vanishing of Ĥ^2_c to identify completed Borel–Moore homology with the dual of Ĥ^1_c.

acceptance: Ĥ^2_c = 0 although H^2_c(Y(K_f), O) ≅ O^{π_0(Y(K_f))} is nonzero at every finite level.
The twist by the cyclotomic character ψ = ε: cupping with c_ε carries the eigensystem (T_ℓ, S_ℓ) of a form f to (ℓT_ℓ, ℓ^2S_ℓ).

nodes.title: Non-Eisenstein localisation: boundary, injectivity and freeness
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) be continuous and absolutely irreducible, unramified outside Σ = Σ_0 ∪ {p}, and let m be a residual maximal ideal of the completed Hecke algebra of the modular tower (CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/completed-hecke-algebra at tame level K_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ) with T_ℓ ≡ tr ρ̄(Frob_ℓ), ℓS_ℓ ≡ det ρ̄(Frob_ℓ) for ℓ ∉ Σ. Write M_m for the closed summand cut out by the residual projector of CC.8. Then: (a) Ĥ^1_c(K_{Σ_0})_{O,m} → Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,m} is an isomorphism, and replacing the open curves by their compactifications does not change the m-parts. (b) If K_p is compact open and K_f = K_pK_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ is neat, then H^1(K_f)_{O,m} → (Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,m})^{K_p} and H^1(K_f)_{O/ϖ^s,m} → (H^1_{O/ϖ^s,m,Σ})^{K_pK_{Σ_0}} are isomorphisms; for non-neat K_f the same holds unless ρ̄ is induced from a character of G_{Q(√−1)} or G_{Q(√−3)}. (c) For K_f neat and each s, H^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O/ϖ^s,m} is an injective smooth K_p-representation over O/ϖ^s; equivalently Hom_{K_p}(−, H^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O/ϖ^s,m}) is exact. (d) If moreover K_p is pro-p, there is r ≥ 0 with Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,m} ≅ C(K_p, O)^r as ϖ-adically admissible K_p-representations; dually its Schikhof dual is free of rank r over O[[K_p]].
hypotheses: ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible; this is what makes H^0 terms vanish after localisation and makes the boundary Eisenstein-free (an absolutely irreducible ρ̄ has a non-Eisenstein eigensystem by Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt, which is the eigenvalue form of non-Eisenstein used by ModularCurvesPartII R14.3).

ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/boundary-non-eisenstein is stated in weight two and residue characteristic at least 3; for p = 2 the Eisenstein property of the Hecke action on the cusp boundary (Hecke operators act on H^0 of the cusps through T_ℓ ↦ 1 + ℓ up to characters) is the same computation and is recorded as a remaining item of R31.1.
Neatness of K_f (no fixed points of GL_2(Q) on (C∖R) × GL_2(A_f)/K_f) is required in (b)–(d); Carayol’s lemma replaces it in (b) for ρ̄ not induced from Q(√−1) or Q(√−3).
The localisation is CC.8's residual summand; its identification with Emerton’s T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ ⊗ (−) is made in R31.3/completed-hecke-algebra-of-the-modular-tower and is not used here.
proofSteps: (a): the Hecke action on the boundary cohomology of the modular curves is Eisenstein (ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/boundary-non-eisenstein), so the boundary terms of the CC.7 support triangle vanish after applying the residual projector, which commutes with the triangle by CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/localisation-limit-support-dual-compatibility.

(b): for normal K_p′ ⊂ K_p and K_{Σ_0}′ ⊂ K_{Σ_0} the Hochschild–Serre sequence for the free action of K_f/K_f′ on Y(K_f′) has its H^1(K_f/K_f′, H^0) term killed by localising at m, giving H^1(K_f)_{O/ϖ^s,m} ≅ (H^1(K_f′)_{O/ϖ^s,m})^{K_f}; pass to the limits (EM11 Lemma 5.3.8 and (5.3.9)). The non-neat case is Carayol’s lemma (EM11 Remark 5.3.10).

(c): for a finitely generated smooth K_p-module M, Hom_{K_p}(M, H^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O/ϖ^s}) is identified, after localising at m, with H^1 of the local system M^∨ on Y(K_f) (EM11 (5.3.16)–(5.3.17)); a short exact sequence of such M gives a long exact sequence of cohomology whose H^0 terms vanish at m, so the Hom functor is exact on the right (EM11 Proposition 5.3.15; the method of Remark 5.3.18).
(d): (O/ϖ^s)[[K_p]] is local for K_p pro-p, so an injective admissible smooth K_p-module is C(K_p, O/ϖ^s)^r with r independent of s; pass to the limit in s (EM11 Corollary 5.3.19).

sources.match: Neat levels; recovery of finite-level ρ̄-localised cohomology as K_p- and K_{Σ_0}-invariants of the completed objects; Carayol’s replacement of neatness.

Exactness of H^1 after localising at a non-Eisenstein ideal, expressed as injectivity of the localised mod ϖ^s cohomology as a smooth K_p-representation, and the resulting isomorphism with C(K_p, O)^r for pro-p K_p.
For absolutely irreducible ρ̄ the compactly supported and ordinary completed cohomology agree after localisation (Ĥ^1_{c,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ Ĥ^1_{ρ̄,Σ}).

acceptance: For ρ̄ the reduction of the Galois representation of the weight-two newform of level 11 at p = 3 (absolutely irreducible), (a) gives Ĥ^1_{c,m} = Ĥ^1_m at tame level K_0(11)^p.
Non-example: for an Eisenstein maximal ideal (ρ̄ = 1 ⊕ ε̄) the boundary contributes and (a) fails; the hypothesis cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Completed cohomology of quaternionic Shimura curves
nodes.statement: Let E_0 be a totally real field in which p splits completely, 𝔭 | p a place (so E_{0,𝔭} = Q_p) and ∞_0 a real place; let D be a quaternion algebra over E_0 split at ∞_0, ramified at the other real places and at 𝔭 (D_𝔭 the quaternion division algebra over Q_p), and D_0 the definite algebra obtained by exchanging the invariants at 𝔭 and ∞_0. For a tame level U^p ⊂ (D ⊗ A_f^p)^× and open V in the 𝔭-part of the level, let Sh_{VU^p} be the Shimura curve over E_0. For a continuous character ψ of A_f^×/E_0^× and a continuous representation λ of the level at the places above p other than 𝔭 on a finite free O-module, define Ĥ^1(U^p, O/ϖ^n) = colim_V H^1_ét(Sh_{VU^p, Ē_0}, O/ϖ^n), its ψ-isotypic part Ĥ^1_ψ, the λ-typical part Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O/ϖ^n) = Hom(λ, Ĥ^1_ψ(U^p, O/ϖ^n)), and, after localising at a residual maximal ideal m of the abstract Hecke algebra T_S^{univ} = O[T_v, S_v]_{v∉S}, Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m} = colim_n Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O/ϖ^n)_m and Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O)_m = lim_n Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O/ϖ^n)_m with the p-adic topology. They carry commuting actions of G_{E_0,S}, T_S^{univ} and D_𝔭^× (and of A_f^×). This is CompletedCohomologyPartII’s completed cohomology of the quaternionic Shimura-curve tower (CC.8 Hilbert/quaternionic adapter), with the 𝔭-level colimit taken over D_𝔭^×-levels.
hypotheses: D is split at exactly one real place and at all finite places above p other than 𝔭; D_𝔭 is division. The tower is in the 𝔭-direction of D_𝔭^×, a compact-mod-centre group, so finite-level H^1 of the tower is not admissible over GL_2(Q_p).
ψ is the central character on A_f^×; λ has central character compatible with ψ on the intersection with A_f^×.
proofSteps: Take the canonical-model tower and finite étale–Betti comparison from CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/hilbert-finite-local-system-input and CC.8/arithmetic-tower-realisation (Hilbert/quaternionic family, quaternion algebras split at exactly one real place).
Retain the central-quotient comparison of CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/arithmetic-shimura-central-quotient when passing from the arithmetic quotient to Sh_{VU^p}.

Isotypic and λ-typical parts are taken at each finite n before the limits; localisation at m uses the finite-level Hecke images (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.4/finite-cohomology) and CC.8's residual projectors, which commute with colim_n and lim_n by CC.8/localisation-limit-support-dual-compatibility.
The Pontryagin dual (Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m})^∨ is identified with the Schikhof dual of Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O)_m (CDN after Proposition 4.11).

sources.match: The quaternionic data D_0 (definite, split at all finite places) and D (invariants exchanged at 𝔭 and ∞_0), the Shimura curves Sh_{VU^p}, and the completed cohomology Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m} with its integral version and duality.
The globalisation setting: E_0 totally real of even degree in which p splits completely, with a cuspidal automorphic π whose residual representation restricts to a given r̄ at every place above p.

acceptance: Taking E_0 = Q is excluded by the requirement that D split at exactly one real place while being ramified at 𝔭; the construction needs [E_0 : Q] even when D_0 is unramified at all finite places.
Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m} is a smooth D_𝔭^×-module; its D_𝔭^×-invariants at a fixed level are finite-level H^1 of one Shimura curve.

uses.how: Its m-part is identified with Scholze’s functor applied to the definite quaternionic module S_{ψ,λ,m}.
It factors as ρ_m ⊗ N with ρ_m the Hecke-valued Galois representation.
The comparison theorem is stated on this carrier.

api.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.torsion
api.statement: Ĥ^1(U^p, O/ϖ^n) = colim_V H^1_ét(Sh_{VU^p, Ē_0}, O/ϖ^n) with its G_{E_0,S} × T_S^{univ} × D_𝔭^× × A_f^×-action.

api.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.isotypic
api.statement: The ψ-isotypic and λ-typical parts Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O/ϖ^n) = Hom(λ, Ĥ^1_ψ(U^p, O/ϖ^n)).

api.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.localized
api.statement: Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m} = colim_n Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O/ϖ^n)_m and its integral version lim_n.

api.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.dualEquiv
api.statement: (Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m})^∨ ≅ Hom^cont_O(Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O)_m, O) as compact T_S^{univ}[G_{Q_p} × D_𝔭^×]-modules.

api.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.invariants

api.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.equivCC

tests.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.trivial_lambda
tests.statement: For λ the trivial one-dimensional representation, Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ} is the space of vectors of Ĥ^1_ψ invariant under the level at the places above p other than 𝔭.

tests.name: TauCeti.ShimuraCurveCompleted.not_GL2_admissible
tests.statement: Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m} is a D_𝔭^×-module, not a GL_2(Q_p)-module: a definition that takes the colimit over GL_2(Q_p)-levels would describe the modular-curve object of R31.1/the-object-the-conjecture-is-about instead.

nodes.title: Completed module of a definite quaternion algebra
nodes.statement: Let F be a totally real field in which p splits completely and D a quaternion algebra over F ramified at every infinite place and unramified at every place above p, with fixed isomorphisms D ⊗_F F_v ≅ M_2(F_v) at the places where D is unramified; put K_p = ∏_{v|p} GL_2(O_{F_v}) ⊂ D_p^× = ∏_{v|p} GL_2(F_v). For a tame level U^p ⊂ (D ⊗_F A_F^{∞,p})^× let X(U^p) = D^×∖(D ⊗_F A_F^∞)^×/U^p, a profinite space with a continuous right action of D_p^×, and X(U^pU_p) = X(U^p)/U_p (a finite set) for U_p ⊂ K_p open. For a topological O-module M the space C(X(U^p), M) of continuous functions carries the right-translation action of D_p^× and of the centre (A_F^∞)^×; for a continuous character ψ: (A_F^∞)^×/F^×_{≫0} → O^× trivial on U^p ∩ (A_F^∞)^×, S_ψ(U^p, M) ⊂ C(X(U^p), M) is the closed subspace of ψ-equivariant functions f(gz) = ψ(z)f(g). Put S_ψ(U^p, A) = colim_{U_p} S_ψ(U^pU_p, A) for a discrete torsion O-module A (locally constant functions), the completed cohomology S_ψ(U^p) = Hom_O(E/O, S_ψ(U^p, E/O)) ≅ lim_n S_ψ(U^p, O/ϖ^n) with the p-adic topology, S_ψ(U^p)_E = E ⊗_O S_ψ(U^p), and the completed homology M_ψ(U^p) = S_ψ(U^p, E/O)^∨ (Pontryagin dual, compact-open topology); then S_ψ(U^p) ≅ Hom^cont_O(M_ψ(U^p), O). For F = Q and no central character fixed, C^0(X) = C(X(K^p), L) is Dospinescu–Le Bras’s space of p-adic automorphic forms on B̄^*.
hypotheses: D is definite (ramified at all infinite places) and split at every place above p; p splits completely in F so that each F_v = Q_p.
The quaternionic tower is degree-zero: its cohomology is functions on finite sets; nonzero higher stabiliser cohomology at non-neat levels is not claimed to vanish.
Pan’s §3.7 variant with a smooth character ξ of U^p (functions with f(guz) = ψ(z)ξ(u^p)f(g)) is the same construction applied to the kernel of ξ, followed by the ξ-isotypic part.
proofSteps: The finite double coset sets X(U^pU_p) and their stabilisers are HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3/definite-class-set; X(U^p) = lim_{U_p} X(U^pU_p) is profinite.

S_ψ(U^p, A) for discrete torsion A is the CC.1 fixed-exponent colimit of the degree-zero tower; S_ψ(U^p) is its CC.2 coefficient limit; these are the CompletedCohomologyPartII carriers of the finite discrete arithmetic tower, as for the definite unitary groups in CC.8/definite-unitary-degree-zero.

The identifications S_ψ(U^p) ≅ lim_n S_ψ(U^p, O/ϖ^n) ≅ Hom^cont(M_ψ(U^p), O) and M_ψ(U^p) ≅ Hom_O(S_ψ(U^p), O) are Pontryagin and Schikhof duality (CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.3/continuous-dual-conventions, Pan Remark 3.2.3). HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3/definite-class-set states the finite class set in Khare–Wintenberger’s setting (F of even degree, D split at the finite places considered, quotient by the centre); the same finiteness for Pan’s D (any definite D split above p, no central quotient) is the compactness of D^×∖(D ⊗ A_F^∞)^× modulo the centre for an anisotropic group, with the centre handled by the finiteness of F^×∖(A_F^∞)^×/(U ∩ (A_F^∞)^×) times its connected component.
The ψ-isotypic part is a closed subspace since (A_F^∞)^× acts continuously; twisting by θ∘N_{D/F} gives S_ψ(U^p) ≅ S_{ψθ^2}(U^p) (Pan 3.2.7).

sources.match: The definite quaternion algebra over a totally real field in which p splits completely, the spaces S_{τ,ψ}(U, A) of continuous functions with central character, the completed cohomology S_ψ(U^p) and completed homology M_ψ(U^p) with their dualities, and twisting by characters of the reduced norm.
The variant S_{ψ,ξ} with a smooth character ξ of the tame level, deduced from the untwisted case through the kernel of ξ.

For B̄ over Q split at p and ramified at ∞: X = B̄^*(Q)∖B̄^*(A_f)/K^p is the projective limit of the finite sets X(K_p), with a right action of G = GL_2(Q_p), and C^0(X) is the space of p-adic automorphic forms.
Tung uses the same S_ψ(U^p, E/O) and M_ψ(U^p) for a definite quaternion algebra over a totally real field in which 2 splits completely.

acceptance: For D = B̄ over Q and K^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} K_ℓ with one K_{ℓ_0} torsion-free, the right G-action on X has finitely many GL_2(Z_p)-orbits (R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure).
The U_p-invariants of S_ψ(U^p, A) are S_ψ(U^pU_p, A) (Pan Remark 3.2.3).

uses.how: M_ψ(U^p)_m is the global object whose block component is compared with Paškūnas’s projective envelope.
C^0(X)[𝔭] ≅ Π(𝔭)^{⊕r} is the zero-dimensional local–global compatibility.
M_ψ(U^p)_m is patched into M̃_∞.
Scholze’s functor is applied to S_{ψ,λ,m}.
Tung’s dyadic and Pan’s residually reducible arguments work on this module.

api.statement: M_ψ(U^p) = S_ψ(U^p, E/O)^∨ as a compact O[[K_p]]-module with central character ψ^{-1}.

api.statement: For a continuous character θ of (A_F^∞)^×/N(U^p)F^×_{≫0}, f ↦ (θ∘N_{D/F})·f is an isomorphism S_ψ(U^p) ≅ S_{ψθ^2}(U^p) intertwining T_v with θ(Frob_v)T_v.

api.name: TauCeti.DefiniteQuaternionCompleted.equivCC

tests.name: TauCeti.DefiniteQuaternionCompleted.finiteLevel_computation

planet.name: Completed module of a definite quaternion algebra

nodes.title: Structure of the definite quaternionic tower
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module: (a) X(U^p)/K_p^{(1)} is finite, where K_p^{(1)} is any open subgroup of D_p^×; writing (D ⊗ A_F^{∞,p})^×/U^p = ⊔_{i=1}^r D^× y_i with stabilisers Γ_i ⊂ D^× viewed in D_p^×, each Γ_i is discrete and cocompact modulo centre in D_p^× and X(U^p) ≅ ⊔_i Γ_i∖D_p^× as topological D_p^×-spaces; X(U^p) is a compact p-adic analytic manifold with a locally analytic action. (b) For F = Q and K^p with K_{ℓ_0} torsion-free for some ℓ_0, GL_2(Z_p) acts freely on X with finitely many orbits, so C(X, M) ≅ C(GL_2(Z_p), M)^{⊕s} as GL_2(Z_p)-representations for every topological Z_p-module M. (c) If U^pK_p is sufficiently small and ψ is trivial on N_{D/F}(U^p), then S_ψ(U^p, E/O) is an injective object of the category of smooth K_p-representations over O with central character ψ; dually M_ψ(U^p) is projective among profinite O[[K_p]]-modules with central character ψ^{-1} and finitely generated over O[[K_p]], and S_ψ(U^p)_E is a topological direct summand of C_ψ(K_p, E)^{⊕d}. (d) S_ψ(U^p, E/O) is an admissible smooth D_p^×-representation, and after localising at a maximal ideal m of the Hecke algebra S_ψ(U^p, E/O)_m is admissible and injective in the smooth K_p-representations with the central character induced by ψ.
hypotheses: R18.3/definite-class-set is stated in Khare–Wintenberger’s even-degree setting modulo the centre; (a) uses only the finiteness argument, which holds for every definite D (see R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module).
(b) needs a torsion-free component of the tame level; (c) needs U^pK_p sufficiently small (all the groups (t_i^{-1}D^×t_i ∩ U(A_F^∞)^×)/F^× trivial) and ψ trivial on N_{D/F}(U^p).
Finiteness of X(U^p)/K_p uses strong approximation for the reduced-norm-one group and finiteness of the class set; no claim is made for an indefinite quaternion algebra.
proofSteps: (a): finiteness of D^×∖(D ⊗ A_F^{∞,p})^×/U^p is the finiteness of the class set (R18.3/definite-class-set); the stabilisers are discrete since D^× is discrete in (D ⊗ A_F^∞)^×, and cocompact modulo centre since D is definite (DLB Lemma 4.4).

(b): a nontrivial stabiliser of a point of X in GL_2(Z_p) would be a finite-order element of D^× lying in a conjugate of K_{ℓ_0}, which is torsion-free; finitely many orbits by (a); choose a section on each orbit (DLB Lemma 13.1).

(c): for a finite torsion smooth K_p-module M, S_{M,ψ}(U^pK_p, O) ≅ Hom_{O[K_p]}(M^∨, S_ψ(U^p, E/O)) (Pan Lemma 3.2.5); the left side is exact in M at sufficiently small level by Pan Corollary 3.1.3, giving injectivity on finite modules, and Mittag-Leffler gives it in general (Pan Proposition 3.2.4); dualise and use admissibility for finite generation and the direct-summand statement (Pan Corollary 3.2.6; Tung-2 Corollary 4.2.2).

(d): (S_ψ(U^p, E/O))^{U_p} = S_ψ(U^pU_p, E/O) is cofinitely generated, giving admissibility; localisation is a direct summand, and injectivity passes to summands (CDN Proposition 4.7(a), citing Paškūnas).

sources.match: X is a finite disjoint union of Γ_i∖G with Γ_i discrete cocompact, a compact p-adic analytic manifold; GL_2(Z_p) acts freely with finitely many orbits, so C^0(X, M) ≅ C^0(GL_2(Z_p), M)^{⊕s}.

sources.locator: Corollary 3.1.3, p. 18; Proposition 3.2.4, Lemma 3.2.5, p. 19; Corollary 3.2.6, p. 20
sources.match: Exactness of quaternionic forms at sufficiently small level, injectivity of S_ψ(U^p, E/O) among smooth K_p-modules with central character, projectivity and finite generation of M_ψ(U^p), and the direct-summand embedding of S_ψ(U^p)_E into C_ψ(K_p, E)^{⊕d}.
Local admissibility of S_ψ(U^p, E/O) and projectivity of M_ψ(U^p) in the category of pseudo-compact modules, for the 2-adic setting.
S_ψ(U^p, L/O)_m is nonzero, admissible and injective in the smooth K_p-representations with central character ψ_p.

acceptance: For F = Q, B̄ of discriminant 2 and p = 3, (b) holds with K^p maximal away from 2 and Iwahori-free at an auxiliary prime ℓ_0 ≥ 5.
Non-example: without a torsion-free component the GL_2(Z_p)-action on X can have nontrivial finite stabilisers, and C(X, M) is then only a sum of induced modules from those stabilisers.

nodes.title: Locally algebraic vectors of completed cohomology
nodes.statement: For * ∈ {∅, c} there is a natural G_Q × GL_2(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism ⊕_{k≥2, n∈Z} H^1_*(V_k)_E ⊗_E (Sym^{k−2}E^2)^∨ ⊗_E E(n) ≅ (Ĥ^1_{*,E})_{l.alg}, where (Ĥ^1_{*,E})_{l.alg} is the subspace of locally GL_2(Q_p)-algebraic vectors, H^1_*(V_k)_E = colim_{K_f} H^1_*(Y(K_f), V_k) is the cohomology of the tower with coefficients in the local system V_k attached to Sym^{k−2} of the standard representation, E(1) is the line on which G_Q × GL_2(A_f) acts by ε ⊗ (ε∘det), and GL_2(A_f) acts on (Sym^{k−2}E^2)^∨ through GL_2(Q_p). Its isotypic pieces come from the following degree statements, for an irreducible algebraic representation W of GL_2(Q_p) with dual W̌: (i) Ext^i_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^0_{la}) vanishes except for i ∈ {0, 3}, and both survivors vanish unless W is one-dimensional; (ii) H^0(V_W) ≅ Hom_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^0_{la}) and H^1(V_W) ≅ Hom_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^1_{la}), and Ext^1_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^1_{la}) ≅ Ext^3_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^0_{la}); (iii) for compact supports H^1_c(V_W) ≅ Hom_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^1_{c,la}) and H^2_c(V_W) ≅ Ext^1_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^1_{c,la}). Consequently, for a cuspidal newform f of weight k defined over E, V_f ⊗_E π(V_f) ⊗_E (Sym^{k−2}E^2)^∨ embeds G_Q × GL_2(A_f)-equivariantly into Ĥ^1_{*,E}.
hypotheses: The comparison holds only in cohomological degree one; it uses the explicit Ĥ^0, the vanishing Ĥ^n = 0 for n ≥ 2 and Ĥ^2_c = 0 (R31.1/degree-zero-two-and-compact-support). A formal interchange of invariants and inverse limits is not used.
Locally algebraic means: the orbit map of the vector is locally a polynomial in the matrix entries and det^{−1} on a compact open subgroup of GL_2(Q_p); this is stronger than locally analytic.
(Sym^{k−2}E^2 ⊗ det^n)_{k≥2,n∈Z} is a complete set of irreducible algebraic representations of GL_2 over E.
proofSteps: CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.6/hochschild-serre-descent-to-finite-level gives the continuous Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H^i_cts(U, Ĥ^j ⊗ W) ⇒ H^{i+j}(Y_U, V_W); passing to locally analytic vectors and Lie-algebra cohomology turns it into Ext^i_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^j_{la}) ⇒ H^{i+j}(V_W) (EM06 Corollary 2.2.18). CC.6/analytic-classical-comparison warns that the underived locally analytic vectors need justification: here the Ĥ^j are admissible Banach representations, on which the functor of locally analytic vectors is exact and has no higher derived functors (Schneider–Teitelbaum; Emerton’s locally analytic vectors memoir), so the underived and derived forms agree in this case.

Proposition 4.3.1 of EM06: Ĥ^0 restricted to Z(Q_p) × SL_2(Q_p) is the tensor product of its restriction to the centre with the trivial SL_2-representation; a Künneth argument and vanishing of positive z-Ext for C(Z_p^×, E) give Ext^i_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^0_{la}) ≅ Hom_z(E(χ^{-1}), Ĥ^0_{la}) ⊗ H^i(sl_2, W); Whitehead’s lemmas give (i) (EM06 Corollary 4.3.2).
Feed (i) and the vanishing of H^n(V_W) for n > 1 into the spectral sequence to get (ii) (EM06 (4.3.3)–(4.3.5)); Ĥ^2_c = 0 gives (iii) (EM06 (4.3.7)–(4.3.8)).

Sum (ii)/(iii) over the irreducible W = Sym^{k−2} ⊗ det^n and identify Hom_{gl_2}(W̌, −) ⊗ W̌ with the W̌-isotypic locally algebraic vectors; the Tate twist E(n) records det^n (EM-PAMQ Theorem 7.4.2).

For a newform f, H^1_*(V_k)_E contains V_f ⊗ π(V_f) G_Q × GL_2(A_f)-equivariantly (EM-PAMQ Theorem 2.5.1): the Galois factor is the rank-two realisation of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.1/newform-rank-two-realisation and the GL_2(A_f)-factor is identified with π(V_f) by local–global compatibility away from p (R19.4) and at p (Saito, R19.5); R14.3/relative-coefficient-system supplies V_k on the neat cofinal levels Y_1(N), N ≥ 5, which suffice for the tower. The Manin–Drinfeld splitting of H^1_c → H^1_par allows either support (EM-PAMQ Corollary 7.4.3).

sources.match: Ext groups of algebraic representations with values in the locally analytic vectors of Ĥ^0 are computed by Lie-algebra cohomology of sl_2, which kills all but degrees 0 and 3; the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence then identifies H^1 with coefficients in V_W with the W̌-equivariant locally analytic vectors in degree one, and similarly with compact supports.
The locally algebraic vectors of Ĥ^1_{*,E} are the direct sum over k ≥ 2 and n of H^1_*(V_k)_E ⊗ (Sym^{k−2})^∨ ⊗ E(n); a cuspidal newform contributes V_f ⊗ π(V_f) ⊗ (Sym^{k−2})^∨.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.3.13, p. 51; proof of Corollary 5.4.5, p. 55
sources.match: Emerton’s local–global paper uses [38, Thm. 7.4.2] (= EM-PAMQ Theorem 7.4.2) to describe the locally algebraic vectors at classical points.

acceptance: Weight two: the K_p-invariant locally algebraic vectors of algebraic weight W = 1 recover H^1(Y(K_pK^p), E), the cohomology carrying weight-two forms.

For W one-dimensional, Ext^1_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^1_{la}) ≅ Ext^3_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^0_{la}) can be nonzero, so the degree-one comparison is exact only in the Hom term; the theorem does not claim vanishing of higher Ext for trivial W.

planet.name: Locally algebraic vectors of completed cohomology

nodes.title: Density of algebraic and classical vectors
nodes.statement: (a) For every tame level K^p the GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors of Ĥ^1(K^p)_E are dense in Ĥ^1(K^p)_E; the same holds for any closed G-stable topological direct summand of Ĥ^1(K^p)_E, in particular for the summand cut out by a residual Hecke projector. (b) The E[G]-span of the GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors of such a summand is the direct sum, over the systems of Hecke eigenvalues λ attached to classical cuspidal eigenforms of weight k ≥ 2 and tame level dividing K^p, of the λ-parts of its locally algebraic vectors; hence ⊕_λ Ĥ^1(K^p)_E[λ]_{l.alg} is dense in Ĥ^1(K^p)_E. (c) In the definite quaternionic case of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module with F = Q and B̄ split at p, the GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors of any topological direct summand of C^0(X) are dense; for a general totally real F and ψ|_{O_{F_v}^×} algebraic at a place v | p, the subspace of S_ψ(U^p)_E that is GL_2(O_{F_v})-algebraic and locally algebraic at the other places above p is dense.
hypotheses: Density is for the Banach topology of Ĥ^1(K^p)_E (resp. of C^0(X), S_ψ(U^p)_E).
In (b) the eigensystems run over classical cuspidal eigenforms; Eisenstein eigensystems do not occur in Ĥ^1 after localising at a non-Eisenstein ideal but may occur without localisation.
proofSteps: Reduce to a neat level: averaging over K^p/K^{p′} projects Ĥ^1(K^{p′})_E onto Ĥ^1(K^p)_E (EM11 Remark 5.4.2).

Since Y(GL_2(Z_p)K^p) is homotopic to a finite one-dimensional complex, Ĥ^1(K^p)_E is a quotient of C(GL_2(Z_p), E)^s compatibly with algebraic vectors (EM06 Theorem 2.1.5); in the localised case R31.1/non-eisenstein-boundary-and-injectivity(d) makes it a direct summand of C(GL_2(Z_p), E)^s directly (EM11 Proposition 5.4.1).

Polynomial functions on GL_2(Z_p) are the GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors of C(GL_2(Z_p), E) and are dense by Mahler’s theorem (Tau Ceti’s PadicFunctionalAnalysis roadmap, Layer 3.2, states Mahler’s theorem on Z_p; the several-variable form on GL_2(Z_p) ⊂ Z_p^4 follows by tensor products of Mahler bases); density passes to quotients and direct summands.
(b) is R31.2/locally-algebraic-vectors-of-completed-cohomology: every locally algebraic vector lies in a finite sum of eigenspaces of classical eigenforms (EM11 proof of Corollary 5.4.5).

(c) is the same argument with R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure(b) in place of the topology of the modular curve (DLB Lemme 13.2), and in Pan’s generality through the isomorphism S_{(k,w),ψ}(U^pU_p, E) ≅ Hom_{U_p}(W^*_{(k,w)}, S_ψ(U^p)_E) (Pan Proposition 3.2.9).

sources.match: GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors are dense in Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{E,ρ̄}, and even without localising, by Mahler expansions and the realisation of Ĥ^1 as a quotient (or summand) of a finite sum of C(GL_2(Z_p), E).
The E[G]-span of the algebraic vectors is the sum over classical points of the locally algebraic parts, by EM-PAMQ Theorem 7.4.2.
GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors are dense in any topological direct factor of C^0(X), by Lemme 13.1 and Mahler’s theorem.

For a definite quaternion algebra over a totally real field, the subspace of vectors algebraic at one place v | p and locally algebraic at the others is dense, when the central character is algebraic at v.
The completed cohomology of a tower of finite complexes is computed by a finite complex of C(H, E)-modules.

acceptance: Katz’s density of classical modular forms in p-adic modular forms is the analogue (EM11 Remark 5.4.3).
Non-example: locally constant (smooth) vectors alone are not dense in Ĥ^1(K^p)_E once nonzero weights are excluded; the density needs all algebraic weights k ≥ 2.

nodes.title: Classical eigensystems and newforms in completed cohomology
nodes.statement: Let T(Σ) = O[T_ℓ, S_ℓ]_{ℓ∉Σ} be the abstract spherical Hecke algebra and λ: T(Σ) → E′ a system of Hecke eigenvalues over a finite extension E′/E. Then: (a) the λ-part of (Ĥ^1(K^p)_{E′})_{l.alg} is nonzero if and only if λ, up to the cyclotomic twist of R31.2/locally-algebraic-vectors-of-completed-cohomology, is the eigensystem of a classical eigenform of weight k ≥ 2 and tame level K^p (cuspidal or Eisenstein); (b) for a cuspidal newform f of weight k and conductor N prime to p, with λ_f its eigensystem, Ĥ^1(K_1(N)^p)_{E′}[λ_f]_{l.alg} ≅ V_f ⊗ Sym^{k−2}(E′^2)^∨ ⊗ π_p(V_f) as G_Q × GL_2(Q_p)-representations, where π_p(V_f) is the local component at p of the automorphic representation of f; (c) under the identification of weight-two cusp forms with H^1 of the modular curve (ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/weight-two-shimura-isomorphism), the Hecke operator T_ℓ on Ĥ^1 restricts to the classical T_ℓ on Mathlib’s CuspForm space at level Γ_1(N), with the normalisation of R14 (T_ℓ the double coset of diag(ℓ, 1) after Emerton’s transpose-inverse convention); (d) every eigensystem λ with Ĥ^1(K^p)_{E′}[λ] ≠ 0 is promodular in the sense of EM-PAMQ Definition 7.3.15, and attached to it is a two-dimensional odd continuous G_Q-representation over E′ unramified outside Σ, unique up to semisimplification.
hypotheses: The Hecke normalisation is that of R14 and Emerton lg §2 (the actions of [16] twisted by g ↦ (g^{-1})^t); geometric Frobenius at ℓ has characteristic polynomial X^2 − T_ℓX + ℓS_ℓ on the Galois factor.
In (b), π_p(V_f) is the generic smooth representation of GL_2(Q_p) attached to f; p ∤ N is used only to identify the K_p-type.
proofSteps: (a) and (b) are R31.2/locally-algebraic-vectors-of-completed-cohomology combined with the decomposition of H^1_*(V_k)_E into Hecke eigenspaces, and multiplicity one for newforms with Eichler–Shimura (EM-PAMQ Corollary 7.4.3, Remark 7.3.14; EM11 proof of Theorem 3.3.22 in §7.4).

(c) is the weight-two Shimura isomorphism of ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/weight-two-shimura-isomorphism and the Hecke compatibility of R14.1/analytic-comparison-of-correspondences, transported to the completed tower by R31.1/arithmetic-actions-and-admissibility(b).

(d): Remark 7.3.14 of EM-PAMQ shows eigensystems occurring in Ĥ^1 are promodular; Proposition 7.3.17 constructs the Galois representation from the pseudo-representation on the product of the T(K^p)/I_f, using that ∩_f I_f = 0 by density of H^1 in Ĥ^1; oddness follows from oddness of each V_f.

sources.locator: Definitions 7.3.1–7.3.5, Remark 7.3.14, Definition 7.3.15, Proposition 7.3.17, Remark 7.3.18, pp. 65–69
sources.match: Systems of Hecke eigenvalues, Eisenstein systems, promodularity, and the existence and oddness of the Galois representation attached to a promodular eigensystem.
A cuspidal newform contributes V_f ⊗ π(V_f) ⊗ (Sym^{k−2})^∨ to Ĥ^1.
At a classical point of conductor N, Ĥ^1(K_1^p(N))[𝔭]_{l.alg} ≅ ρ(𝔭) ⊗ Sym^{a−b−1} ⊗ det^b ⊗ π_p(V), by [38, Thm. 7.4.2].

acceptance: Worked example (the roadmap’s required check): for the weight-two newform f of level 11 and p = 5 (good ordinary), Ĥ^1(K_1(11)^p)_E[λ_f]_{l.alg} ≅ V_f ⊗ π_p(V_f) with π_p(V_f) the unramified principal series whose Satake parameters are the roots of X^2 − a_5(f)X + 5, a_5(f) = 1, and the Hecke operator T_ℓ acts on it by a_ℓ(f) for ℓ ∤ 55 in R14’s normalisation.
Non-example: an eigensystem of a weight-one form does not occur in the locally algebraic vectors, although it occurs in Ĥ^1 as a promodular eigensystem (EM-PAMQ Remark 7.3.14).

nodes.title: Completed homology with coefficients recovers classical cohomology
nodes.statement: Let H̃^{BM}_1(K^p) = lim_{K_p} H_1(Y(K_pK^p)(C), {cusps}, O) be completed Borel–Moore homology at tame level K^p, a compact O[[GL_2(Z_p)]]-module with Hecke operators T′_ℓ, S′_ℓ. (a) For every compact O[[GL_2(Z_p)]]-module M there is a canonical Hecke-equivariant isomorphism M ⊗̂_O H̃^{BM}_1(K^p) ≅ H̃^{BM}_1(K^p, 𝒱_M) of compact O[[GL_2(Z_p)]]-modules, where 𝒱_M is the induced pro-local system. (b) For an algebraic representation W of GL_2/Q_p over E, regarded as a right O[[K_p]]-module through v·g = g^{-1}v, and any open K_p ⊂ GL_2(Z_p), there is a canonical E-linear isomorphism W ⊗_{O[[K_p]]} H̃^{BM}_1(K^p) ≅ H^1(K^pK_p, 𝒱_W)(1), compatible with Hecke operators, change of K_p, coefficient change W → W′ and the trace maps. (c) For a smooth representation τ of GL_2(Z_p) on a finite free O-module and W as above, (τ ⊗ W) ⊗_{O[[K_p]]} H̃^{BM}_1(K^p) ≅ H^1(K^pK_p, 𝒱_{τ⊗W})(1) for K_p acting trivially on τ’s reduction, by Hochschild–Serre. No integral isomorphism and no integral self-duality of symmetric powers is asserted.
hypotheses: (b) and (c) are rational statements (after inverting p); the integral map exists but is not claimed to be an isomorphism.
Borel–Moore homology is relative to the cusps; H̃^{BM}_1(K^p) is dual to Ĥ^1_c(K^p) by R31.1/degree-zero-two-and-compact-support and Poincaré duality (Nakamura Lemma 2.4).
proofSteps: (a): write M = lim M_i with M_i of finite length; for K_p acting trivially on M_i, M_i ⊗ H_1(K^pK_p) ≅ H_1(K^pK_p, 𝒱_{M_i}) since H_2 vanishes for non-compact curves; pass to limits (NAK Lemma 2.9).

(b): apply (a) to a K_p-stable lattice W_0 and take K_p-coinvariants, which compute finite-level homology by CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.6/homological-hyperTor-descent in degree one (the hyper-Tor spectral sequence degenerates because H̃^{BM}_0 contributes only through the determinant and H̃_2 = 0); Poincaré duality on Y(K^pK_p) turns H_1^{BM}(𝒱_W) into H^1(𝒱_W)(1) (NAK Lemma 2.10, citing Emerton’s isomorphism (4.3.7) and Calegari–Emerton’s Theorem 2.2.17).
(c): tensor with τ and use Hochschild–Serre for the finite quotient through which GL_2(Z_p) acts on τ (NAK Lemma 2.11).

sources.match: Completed Borel–Moore homology is the dual of compactly supported completed cohomology; its completed tensor product with a compact O[[GL_2(Z_p)]]-module is homology with coefficients; with an algebraic representation W over E it recovers H^1(K^pK_p, 𝒱_W)(1), and with τ ⊗ W by Hochschild–Serre.
The compactly supported comparison H^1_c(V_W) ≅ Hom_{gl_2}(W̌, Ĥ^1_{c,la}), dual to Nakamura’s Lemma 2.10.

acceptance: For W trivial and K_p = GL_2(Z_p), (b) gives O-coinvariants of H̃^{BM}_1(K^p) ⊗ E ≅ H^1(Y(GL_2(Z_p)K^p), E)(1).
KatoEulerSystems L2 consumes (b) with W = Sym^{k−2}(Z_p^2)^* in the form Sym^{k−2}(Z_p^2)^* ⊗_{Z_p[[K_m]]} H̃^{BM}_1(K^p(N_0))(1) → H^1(Y(N), V^*_k)(2) (its request to R31.2).

nodes.title: Classical and p-adic quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module, let W be an irreducible algebraic representation of D_p^× = ∏_{v|p}GL_2(F_v) over E (a tensor product of Sym^{k_v−2} ⊗ det^{w_v} through the embeddings) and U_p ⊂ K_p open. (a) Hom_{U_p}(W^*, C(X(U^p), E)) ≅ A_{U_p}(W) := {f: X(U^p) → W continuous with f(xu) = u^{-1}f(x)}, the space of p-adic automorphic forms of weight W and level U^pU_p, by φ ↦ (x ↦ ...) with inverse f ↦ (ℓ ↦ (x ↦ ℓ(f(x)))); with central character ψ algebraic of the matching weight the same holds for S_ψ, giving S_{W,ψ}(U^pU_p, E) ≅ Hom_{U_p}(W^*, S_ψ(U^p)_E) Hecke-equivariantly. (b) For F = Q and a fixed ι: Q̄_p ≅ C, A_{K_p}(W) ⊗_{E,ι} C ≅ Hom_{B̄^*(R)}(W_∞^*, Aut(K^pK_p)), where Aut(K^pK_p) is the space of smooth functions on B̄^*(Q)∖B̄^*(A)/K^pK_p and W_∞ = W ⊗_ι C viewed as a representation of B̄^*(R). (c) Consequently Hom_{K_p}(W, C^0(X)) ⊗_{E,ι} C ≅ ⊕_π π_f^{K^pK_p}, the sum over automorphic representations π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f of B̄^*(A) with π_∞ ≅ W_∞, and G-equivariantly C^0(X)_{l.alg} ⊗_{E,ι} C ≅ ⊕_{W} ⊕_{π_∞ ≅ W_∞} W_∞ ⊗ π_f^{K^p}; the infinite-dimensional π correspond by global Jacquet–Langlands to cuspidal representations of GL_2(A) discrete series at the ramified places of B̄.
hypotheses: (b)–(c) are stated for F = Q, where DLB work; for general F the same holds with the archimedean comparison of HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3/definite-jl, which is stated in Khare–Wintenberger’s even-degree, parallel-weight setting; R18.3/quaternion-weight likewise covers parallel weights W_k = ⊗ Sym^{k−2}. Non-parallel weights ⊗_v Sym^{k_v−2} ⊗ det^{w_v} and B̄ over Q ramified at a finite prime use the same constructions; that extension is recorded as a remaining item of R31.2.

Sign and dual conventions: W versus W^* follows DLB (their Lemme 4.7 is obtained from 4.5–4.6 by replacing W with W^*). The last display of DLB Lemme 4.7 prints π_f^{K_p} where π_f^{K^pK_p} (in the K_p-algebraic form) or π_f^{K^p} (in the G-equivariant form) is meant; see sourceIssues.
proofSteps: (a): Hom_{U_p}(W^*, C(X, E)) ≅ (W ⊗ C(X, E))^{U_p} ≅ C(X, W)^{U_p}, and U_p-invariance of a W-valued function is f(xu) = u^{-1}f(x) (DLB Lemme 4.5); the central-character version is Pan’s isomorphism 3.2.10.

(b): send f ∈ A_{K_p}(W) to φ_f(ℓ)(g) = ℓ(g_∞^{-1}·(g_p·f(g^∞) ⊗ 1)); DLB give the map f ↦ φ_f explicitly and leave its bijectivity as a standard exercise: the inverse evaluates φ at adelic points with trivial archimedean component, and left B̄^*(Q)-invariance on both sides matches because B̄^*(Q) acts on W through B̄^*(Q_p) and on W_∞ through B̄^*(R) compatibly with ι (DLB Lemme 4.6, following Taylor §1).
(c): replace W by W^* in (a)–(b) and decompose Aut(K^pK_p) under B̄^*(A) (DLB Lemme 4.7); Jacquet–Langlands is GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.3/global-jl.

sources.match: p-adic automorphic forms of weight W are the K_p-homomorphisms from W^* into C^0(X); after ι they are classical automorphic forms of weight W_∞; the K_p-algebraic vectors decompose over automorphic representations with π_∞ ≅ W_∞.

sources.locator: 3.2.10, p. 22 (used in the proof of Theorem 3.5.5, pp. 29–30)
sources.match: For a definite quaternion algebra over a totally real field, S_{(k,w),ψ}(U^pU_p, E) ≅ Hom_{U_p}(W^*_{(k,w)}, S_ψ(U^p)_E), Hecke-equivariantly.

acceptance: For W trivial and π a weight-two quaternionic automorphic representation, π_f^{K^pK_p} occurs in the K_p-invariants of C^0(X)_{l.alg} ⊗ C.

Non-example: one-dimensional automorphic representations χ∘N_{B̄/Q} of B̄^*(A) occur in C^0(X) (constant functions on fibres of the norm) but have no Jacquet–Langlands partner; they are Eisenstein for the Hecke algebra.

nodes.title: Type-specialised quaternionic modules
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module, let σ be a continuous representation of K_p on a finite free O-module σ° (a locally algebraic type: σ ⊗ E = ⊗_{v|p} σ_v with each σ_v ≅ σ(λ_v, τ_v) or σ^{cr}(λ_v, τ_v), an algebraic representation of highest weight λ_v tensored with a smooth K_v-type attached to an inertial type τ_v) on which (A_F^∞)^× ∩ K_p acts through ψ. Put S_{ψ,σ}(U, A) = Hom_{U_p}(σ, S_ψ(U^p, A)) and, for a maximal ideal m of the Hecke algebra, the type-specialised module M(σ°) = σ° ⊗_{O[[K_p]]} M_ψ(U^p)_m. Then (Schikhof duality and Frobenius reciprocity) M(σ°)^d ≅ Hom^cont_{O[[K_p]]}(σ°, M_ψ(U^p)_m^d) ≅ S_{ψ,σ°}(U^pK_p, O)_m; when U^pK_p is sufficiently small M(σ°) is finite free over O, its formation is exact in σ°, and M(σ°)[1/p] is dual to the space of classical quaternionic forms of weight and type σ. The Hecke algebra T^S_{ψ,σ}(U^pK_p) acting faithfully on S_{ψ,σ}(U^pK_p, O)_m is a finite reduced O-algebra, a quotient of the big Hecke algebra of R31.3/definite-quaternionic-hecke-algebra and of the global deformation ring R^S_ψ(σ) with local conditions σ at the places above p.
hypotheses: U^pK_p sufficiently small (Pan Corollary 3.1.3) for the exactness and freeness assertions.

The identification of R^S_ψ(σ) → T^S_{ψ,σ} requires local–global compatibility at v | p at finite level (classical, through the Bernstein centre), recorded in R31.5/type-specialised-patched-modules for the patched version.
proofSteps: M(σ°)^d ≅ Hom^cont_{O[[K_p]]}(σ°, M^d) by Schikhof duality and ≅ Hom_{G_p}(c-Ind σ°, M^d) by Frobenius reciprocity (TUNG-2 §5.2.1, CEGGPS Lemma 4.14); M_ψ(U^p)^d = S_ψ(U^p), so M(σ°)^d = Hom_{K_p}(σ°, S_ψ(U^p)) = S_{ψ,σ°}(U^pK_p, O).

Exactness and freeness: S_ψ(U^p, E/O) is injective among smooth K_p-modules with central character (R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure(c)), so Hom_{K_p}(−, S_ψ(U^p, E/O)) is exact; finite level is a finite sum of copies of σ°'s invariants under trivial stabilisers.
Classicality after inverting p is R31.2/definite-quaternionic-classical-forms(a) applied to the algebraic part of σ together with the smooth type.

The Hecke algebra T^S_{ψ,σ} is finite free over O and reduced since S_{ψ,σ}(U, E) is semisimple for the Hecke action; it is a quotient of the completed Hecke algebra by restriction (R31.3/definite-quaternionic-hecke-algebra).

sources.match: Type-specialised spaces S_{ψ,σ}(U, A) = Hom_{U_p}(σ, S_ψ(U^p, A)), the module σ° ⊗_{O[[K_p]]} M with its Hecke action via Schikhof duality and Frobenius reciprocity, and condition (3): R^S_ψ(σ) finite over O with M(σ)[1/p] faithful.
For the patched module, M_∞(σ°) ≅ lim_n Hom^cont_{O[[K]]}(M_∞, (σ°/ϖ^n)^∨)^∨, the type-specialised module, and its comparison with finite-level automorphic forms of type σ.
At sufficiently small level the functor of quaternionic forms with coefficients is exact.

acceptance: For σ the trivial type and m non-Eisenstein, M(σ°)[1/p] is dual to the weight-two quaternionic forms of level U^pK_p localised at m.
CC1 (GL2ModularityLifting supplier contract): the faithful algebraic quaternionic module consumed by Tung’s Lemma 5.3.2(3) is M(σ°)[1/p] with its R^S_ψ(σ)-action.

uses.how: Condition (3), finiteness of R^S_ψ(σ) and faithfulness of M(σ)[1/p], is equivalent to the full-support condition (1).
The typed component argument identifies the nonzero fibre with the finite-level algebraic σ-space (input CC1).
Completed homology with auxiliary levels is specialised to types at Taylor–Wiles levels.

nodes.title: Completed Hecke algebra of the modular tower
nodes.statement: Fix a tame level K^p and let T(K_pK^p) be the O-subalgebra of End_{G_Q×G}(H^1(K_pK^p)_E) generated by T_ℓ, S_ℓ for ℓ ≠ p unramified in K^p; for K_p′ ⊂ K_p restriction gives surjections T(K_p′K^p) → T(K_pK^p). Put T(K^p) = lim_{K_p} T(K_pK^p) with the projective-limit topology (each T(K_pK^p) with its ϖ-adic topology). It is the modular-tower instance of CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/completed-hecke-algebra (the inverse limit of the finite Hecke images, through CC.8’s derived-to-cohomological residual comparison), and: it is topologically generated by T_ℓ, S_ℓ; it acts faithfully on Ĥ^1(K^p)_O and Ĥ^1(K^p)_E; it is reduced, commutative, compact, and the product of finitely many complete local O-algebras T(K^p)_m, in bijection with the Galois-conjugacy classes of mod-ϖ eigensystems of modular forms of tame level K^p, its topology being the product of the m-adic topologies; for K^{p′} ⊂ K^p there is a continuous map T(K^{p′}) → T(K^p) compatible with the closed embedding Ĥ^1(K^p)_E → Ĥ^1(K^{p′})_E. For ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) absolutely irreducible, modular and unramified outside Σ = Σ_0 ∪ {p}, a compact open K_{Σ_0} ⊂ G_{Σ_0} is allowable if T(K_{Σ_0}) = T(K_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ) has a maximal ideal m with residue field k and T_ℓ ≡ tr ρ̄(Frob_ℓ), ℓS_ℓ ≡ det ρ̄(Frob_ℓ) mod m (ℓ ∉ Σ); T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ = T(K_{Σ_0})_m is a direct factor; for allowable K′ ⊂ K the map T(K′)_ρ̄ → T(K)_ρ̄ is a surjection of complete local noetherian O-algebras, an isomorphism for K sufficiently small; and T_{ρ̄,Σ} = lim_{K_{Σ_0}} T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ is a complete local noetherian O-algebra with residue field k, topologically generated by the T_ℓ.
hypotheses: The Hecke algebra is generated by the operators at primes ℓ ≠ p unramified in K^p; U_ℓ at bad primes is adjoined only where a statement says so (Emerton’s T(K_{Σ_0})^*_ρ̄ in the proof of Theorem 6.2.4).

Emerton states that any sufficiently small K_{Σ_0} is allowable for modular ρ̄; with ρ̄ assumed modular this uses only that ρ̄ arises at some level divisible by primes in Σ, which for p > 2 is the weak-to-strong Serre theorem (EM11 Remark 5.2.3); the dependence on Serre’s conjecture enters only if ‘modular’ is replaced by ‘odd’.
proofSteps: Identify Emerton’s T(K^p) with CC.8’s completed Hecke algebra for the modular tower at tame level K^p: CC.8 forms the inverse limit of finite derived images on CC.4 perfect complexes; CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/derived-cohomological-residual-comparison shows the derived and cohomological images have the same residual labels and differ by a nilpotent kernel, and in degree one for the modular tower the cohomology image is Emerton’s T(K_pK^p) (EM11 Definition 5.2.1, footnote 12 for the weak-closure description).

Semilocality and the product decomposition are CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/completed-semilocal-product, which gives the finite-image inverse-limit topology; that this is the product of the m-adic topologies follows because each T(K^p)_m is noetherian — a quotient of a universal deformation ring (absolutely irreducible residual case, R31.3/deformation-to-hecke-surjection) or of a pseudo-deformation ring (in general) — and a compact noetherian local ring with this profinite topology carries its m-adic topology. Reducedness: each T(K_pK^p) is generated by operators that are normal for the Petersson product on H^1(K_pK^p)_C (ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/hecke-twisted-self-adjoint, R14.3/cup-product-petersson), so it acts semisimply on H^1(K_pK^p)_E; its integral version is ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2/integral-hecke-algebra.

Lemma 5.2.4 of EM11: surjectivity because the image is closed and contains the topological generators T_ℓ; eventual isomorphism because the prime-to-p conductor of every modular lift of ρ̄ unramified outside Σ divides a fixed N_{Σ_0} (Carayol, Livné), so both algebras are the same quotient of R_{ρ̄,Σ} (see R31.3/deformation-to-hecke-surjection).
T_{ρ̄,Σ} is complete local noetherian since the transition maps are surjective and eventually isomorphisms (EM11 Definition 5.2.5).

sources.locator: §5.2, Definition 5.2.1 and footnote 12, p. 46; Definitions 5.2.2, 5.2.5, Remark 5.2.3, Lemma 5.2.4, pp. 47–48
sources.match: The completed Hecke algebra T(K^p) and its properties (faithful, reduced, compact, a finite product of complete local algebras); allowable levels for ρ̄, the local factors T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ and their limit T_{ρ̄,Σ}, a complete local noetherian O-algebra.
Nakamura’s T(K_{Σ_0}), allowable levels and T_{ρ̄,Σ}, as consumed by the zeta morphisms.
For a pro-p level the completed Hecke algebra has the same maximal ideals as the finite-level one (Gee–Newton Lemma 2.1.14), hence is semilocal and a product of its localisations.

acceptance: For K^p = K_1(N)^p and m attached to a residually irreducible newform of level N and weight 2, T(K^p)_m surjects onto the weight-two Hecke algebra T(K_1(N))_m acting on H^1(Y_1(N), O)_m.
For ρ̄ the mod 3 representation of the newform of level 11, the level K_0(11) away from {3, 11} is allowable.

uses.how: T_{ρ̄,Σ} is the coefficient ring of ρ^m_Σ, π^m_Σ and the multiplicity module X(θ).
Pan’s big Hecke algebra T(K^p) with its Galois determinant (request to R31.3).
Nakamura’s zeta morphisms are T_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear.
Pan’s completed Hecke quotient (input CC2).

nodes.title: Hecke-valued Galois determinant and representation
nodes.statement: (a) For every tame level K^p there is a unique continuous two-dimensional determinant D_{K^p}: O[G_{Q,Σ(K^p)}] → T(K^p) (in the sense of Chenevier) with characteristic polynomial X^2 − T_ℓX + ℓS_ℓ at Frob_ℓ for ℓ ∉ Σ(K^p) (geometric Frobenius), compatible with T(K^{p′}) → T(K^p); its specialisation at λ: T(K^p) → Q̄_p is the determinant of a semisimple odd ρ_λ: G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(Q̄_p) with det ρ_λ(Frob_ℓ) = ℓλ(S_ℓ) and tr ρ_λ(Frob_ℓ) = λ(T_ℓ). (b) If ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and K_{Σ_0} is allowable, there is a unique deformation ρ(K_{Σ_0}): G_Q → GL_2(T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄) of ρ̄, unramified outside Σ, with tr ρ(K_{Σ_0})(Frob_ℓ) = T_ℓ and det ρ(K_{Σ_0})(Frob_ℓ) = ℓS_ℓ; passing to the limit gives ρ^m_Σ: G_Q → GL_2(T_{ρ̄,Σ}), which equals ρ(K_{Σ_0}) for K_{Σ_0} small. For 𝔭 ∈ Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}, ρ(𝔭)° = ρ^m_Σ/𝔭ρ^m_Σ is a G_Q-stable lattice, free of rank two over T_{ρ̄,Σ}/𝔭, and ρ(𝔭) = κ(𝔭) ⊗ ρ^m_Σ. (c) The analogous objects exist for the definite quaternionic Hecke algebra (R31.3/definite-quaternionic-hecke-algebra): a pseudo-representation T_ψ: G_{F,S} → T_ψ(U^p) with determinant ψε^{-1}, and for non-Eisenstein m a lifting ρ_m: G_{F,S} → GL_2(T_ψ(U^p)_m) with determinant ψε of the prescribed local type.
hypotheses: Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ is required in (b) and in the lifting of (c); for residually reducible ρ̄ only the determinant (pseudo-representation) exists over T, and R31.3/eisenstein-localisation-and-pro-modular-primes treats it.

Frobenius and Hecke normalisations are those of R31.2/classical-eigensystems-in-completed-cohomology; Emerton’s ρ(K_{Σ_0}) has det(Frob_ℓ) = S_ℓ in his (5.2) display after his twist conventions, which this node records as det = ℓS_ℓ in the geometric-Frobenius convention of R19.6.
proofSteps: (a): at each finite level T(K_pK^p) acts on H^1 and the geometric Hecke determinant of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6/geometric-hecke-determinant gives a determinant over T(K_pK^p) with the stated characteristic polynomials; these are compatible under restriction, so they define a determinant on the inverse limit by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/continuous-determinant (a determinant is determined by its values on a dense set of Frobenii, IHG.0/continuous-determinant-dense).

Specialisation: a determinant over a field is the determinant of a unique semisimple representation (IHG.1/algebraically-closed-reconstruction); oddness from the classical points (EM-PAMQ Proposition 7.3.17).

(b): over the local ring T(K_pK_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ with absolutely irreducible residual determinant, the determinant comes from a unique representation (Carayol; IHG.1/henselian-irreducible and GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem); pass to the limit (EM11 discussion before Lemma 5.2.4 and Definition 5.2.7; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6/determinants-and-representability-over-a-hecke-algebra).

(c): Pan 3.3.5 builds the pseudo-representation over T_ψ(U^p) from finite levels (twisting to finite-order ψ as in Pan 3.3.3); Tung-2 Proposition 4.2.5 and DLB §5.1 (Carayol’s theorem) give the lifting for non-Eisenstein m.

sources.locator: §5.2 before Lemma 5.2.4, p. 47; Definitions 5.2.7 and 5.2.9, pp. 48–49
sources.match: Construction of the deformation ρ(K_{Σ_0}) of ρ̄ over T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ as a limit of Carayol’s finite-level deformations, the representation ρ^m_Σ over T_{ρ̄,Σ}, and the specialisations ρ(𝔭)°, ρ(𝔭).
A two-dimensional pseudo-representation of G_{F,S} valued in the definite quaternionic big Hecke algebra, with determinant ψε^{-1}.
Semilocality of the quaternionic big Hecke algebra and the lifting ρ_m to GL_2(T^S_ψ(U^p)_m) for non-Eisenstein m, of the prescribed type with determinant ψε.
Representations associated with a Hecke morphism, modular residual representations, and r^m = lim r^m(K_p) over the localised quaternionic Hecke algebra A by Carayol’s theorem.
ρ̄ deforms to ρ_m over T(U^p)_m with characteristic polynomial X^2 − T_vX + N(v)S_v at Frob_v (Scholze, Proposition 5.7).

acceptance: At a classical point 𝔭 attached to a newform f, ρ(𝔭) ≅ V_f in the normalisation of R31.2/classical-eigensystems-in-completed-cohomology.
Non-example: for ρ̄ = 1 ⊕ ε̄ there is no GL_2(T_m)-valued representation with the given traces in general; only the determinant exists.

uses.how: ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_p} determines the deformation π^m_Σ of π̄ through Kisin’s equivalence, and ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_ℓ} the family π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ).
The determinant D_S over T(K^p) and the representations ρ_λ at its points (request to R31.3).
Tung’s Hecke-valued representation with determinant ψε (input CC2).
