nodes.title: The deformation-to-Hecke surjection
nodes.statement: (a) Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and modular, unramified outside Σ, and R_{ρ̄,Σ} the universal deformation ring of ρ̄ for deformations unramified outside Σ (and ∞). There is a unique local surjection φ_Σ: R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T_{ρ̄,Σ} with φ_Σ(tr ρ^u(Frob_ℓ)) = T_ℓ and φ_Σ(ℓ^{-1} det ρ^u(Frob_ℓ)) = S_ℓ for ℓ ∉ Σ; it is the limit of compatible surjections φ(K_{Σ_0}): R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄, and ρ^m_Σ is the pushforward of ρ^u. (b) For a residual pseudo-representation t̄ = 1 + χ̄ of G_{F,S} (F totally real, Pan §4.1) let R^{ps} be the universal two-dimensional pseudo-deformation ring of t̄ with determinant χ; the pseudo-representation T_m of R31.3/hecke-galois-determinant-and-representation(c) induces a surjection R^{ps} → T_m, which factors through the quotient R^{ps,{ξ_v}} imposing T_m|_{I_{F_v}} = ξ_v + ξ_v^{-1} at v ∈ S∖Σ_p.
hypotheses: R_{ρ̄,Σ} parametrises deformations over complete local noetherian O-algebras with residue field k; it exists since ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible.
In (b) the factorisation through R^{ps,{ξ_v}} uses classical local–global compatibility at v ∉ Σ_p at finite levels, after twisting to a finite-order central character.
proofSteps: (a): the deformation ρ(K_{Σ_0}) induces φ(K_{Σ_0}) by universality (GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/universal-deformation-ring); its image is closed and contains the T_ℓ, and also the S_ℓ, so it is surjective; the R_{ρ̄,Σ}-images are compatible (EM11 diagram (5.2.6)); take the limit.

(b): universality of R^{ps} (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1/universal-reductive-pseudocharacter-ring for GL_2) gives R^{ps} → T_m; it is surjective because T_m is topologically generated by the T_v, v ∉ S (Pan 4.1.3).

The factorisation through R^{ps,{ξ_v}} is classical local–global compatibility at v ∈ S∖Σ_p for quaternionic forms at finite level (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4/all-hilbert-local-global-compatibility), passed to the limit, after twisting ψ to finite order (Pan 4.1.3, referring to 3.3.3).

sources.locator: §5.2 after Remark 5.2.3, p. 47; (5.2.6) and the paragraph after Definition 5.2.5, p. 48
sources.match: The universal deformation ring R_{ρ̄,Σ} is topologically generated by traces of Frobenius; φ(K_{Σ_0}) is surjective; passing to the limit gives φ_Σ: R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T_{ρ̄,Σ}.
Nakamura records the surjection φ_Σ: R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T_{ρ̄,Σ}.

The natural pseudo-representation over T_m with determinant χ, the universal pseudo-deformation ring R^{ps}, the surjection R^{ps} → T_m and its factorisation through R^{ps,{ξ_v}} by classical local–global compatibility at v ∈ S∖Σ_p.

acceptance: Under Böckle’s hypotheses φ_Σ is an isomorphism (R31.6/boeckle-r-equals-t).
At a classical point 𝔭 of T_{ρ̄,Σ} the composite R_{ρ̄,Σ} → κ(𝔭) classifies ρ(𝔭).

nodes.title: The ρ̄-part of completed cohomology and its commuting actions
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and modular and, for A ∈ {O, E} and allowable K_{Σ_0}, Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{A,ρ̄} = T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ ⊗_{T(K_{Σ_0})} Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_A (a direct summand, equal to the m-adic completion for A = O) and Ĥ^1_{A,ρ̄,Σ} = colim_{K_{Σ_0}} Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{A,ρ̄}, a G_Q × G × G_{Σ_0}-stable direct summand of Ĥ^1_{A,Σ} on which these actions are T_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear and commute. Then: (a) Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,ρ̄}/ϖ^s ≅ H^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O/ϖ^s,ρ̄} and Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}/ϖ^s ≅ H^1_{O/ϖ^s,ρ̄,Σ}; (b) Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,ρ̄} is a ϖ-adically admissible G-representation over T_{ρ̄,Σ} (every element of Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}/ϖ^i is killed by a power of the maximal ideal); (c) Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{A,ρ̄} ≅ (Ĥ^1_{A,ρ̄,Σ})^{K_{Σ_0}}, and for K_p compact open with K_pK_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ neat (or ρ̄ not induced from Q(√−1), Q(√−3)), H^1(K_pK_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ)_{A,ρ̄} ≅ (Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{A,ρ̄})^{K_p}; (d) H^1_{O/ϖ^s,ρ̄,Σ} is an admissible smooth G × G_{Σ_0}-representation over O/ϖ^s; (e) (Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ})^{K_p} is finitely generated over E[G_{Σ_0}] and (H^1_{k,ρ̄,Σ})^{K_p} over k[G_{Σ_0}].
hypotheses: ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and modular; Σ ∋ p contains the primes where ρ̄ ramifies.
(e) uses that the prime-to-p conductors of modular lifts unramified outside Σ are bounded (Carayol, Livné) and that the p-part of the conductor is bounded by K_p.
proofSteps: The ρ̄-part is the residual summand of CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/completed-residual-localisation at the label m, identified with Emerton’s T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ ⊗ (−) by R31.3/completed-hecke-algebra-of-the-modular-tower; localisation commutes with the limits (CC.8/localisation-limit-support-dual-compatibility), giving (a) from (5.1.2) (EM11 (5.3.3)–(5.3.4)).
(b): a direct summand of a ϖ-adically admissible representation is admissible, and the m-power torsion statement follows from (a) (EM11 Lemma 5.3.5).
(c): rational part from EM06 Proposition 2.2.13 and (4.3.4) (EM11 Lemma 5.3.6); integral part is R31.1/non-eisenstein-boundary-and-injectivity(b) (EM11 Lemma 5.3.8, Remark 5.3.10).

(d) from (c) and finiteness at fixed level (EM11 Proposition 5.3.11); (e) from boundedness of conductors, finiteness of classical lifts of bounded conductor in weight two, and R31.2/locally-algebraic-vectors-of-completed-cohomology (EM11 Proposition 5.3.13, Corollary 5.3.14).

sources.locator: Definitions 5.3.1–5.3.2 and (5.3.3)–(5.3.4), p. 49; Lemmas 5.3.5–5.3.6, pp. 49–50; Proposition 5.3.11, Proposition 5.3.13, Corollary 5.3.14, pp. 51–52
sources.match: The ρ̄-part of completed cohomology at allowable levels and in the limit, its reduction mod ϖ^s, ϖ-adic admissibility over T_{ρ̄,Σ}, recovery of finite levels as invariants, admissibility of the torsion objects, and finite generation over the group ring of G_{Σ_0}.

acceptance: The G_Q × G × G_{Σ_0}-actions on Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ} commute with each other and with T_{ρ̄,Σ}.
For K_p = GL_2(Z_p), (c) recovers H^1(GL_2(Z_p)K_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ)_{O,ρ̄}, the weight-two level-prime-to-p cohomology localised at ρ̄.

nodes.title: Galois factorisation of completed cohomology
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and modular, U_Σ = Hom_{T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Q]}(ρ^m_Σ, Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}) with its G × G_{Σ_0}-action. (a) The evaluation map ρ^m_Σ ⊗_{T_{ρ̄,Σ}} U_Σ → Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ} is a T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Q × G × G_{Σ_0}]-linear isomorphism, and reducing mod ϖ and taking m-torsion gives ρ̄ ⊗_k (U_Σ/ϖ)[m] ≅ H^1_{k,ρ̄,Σ}[m]. (b) (Eichler–Shimura in families) Let ρ: G_Q → GL_2(E) be continuous, absolutely irreducible, unramified outside Σ, K_{Σ_0} ⊂ G_{Σ_0} compact open and 𝔭 the ideal of T(K_{Σ_0})[1/p] generated by T_ℓ − tr ρ(Frob_ℓ), ℓ ∉ Σ. Then Hom_{E[G_Q]}(ρ, Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_E[𝔭]) = Hom_{E[G_Q]}(ρ, Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_E); in particular if Hom_{E[G_Q]}(ρ, Ĥ^1_{E,Σ}) ≠ 0 then ρ is promodular, and for every closed point 𝔭 ∈ Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}[1/p] the inclusions Hom(ρ(𝔭), Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭]) ⊂ Hom(ρ(𝔭), Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}) ⊂ Hom(ρ(𝔭), Ĥ^1_{E,Σ}) are equalities. (c) In Pan’s formulation: for λ: T(K^p) → Q̄_p with ρ_λ irreducible, Ĥ^1(K^p, Q̄_p)[𝔭_λ] ≅ ρ_λ(−1) ⊗ Hom_{G_Q}(ρ_λ(−1), Ĥ^1(K^p, Q̄_p)), where the twist matches Pan’s normalisation of the determinant.
hypotheses: (a) needs ρ̄ absolutely irreducible; (b) needs ρ absolutely irreducible but no residual hypothesis.
The twist (−1) in (c) is the conversion between Emerton’s and Pan’s normalisations of the Galois action on H^1 (Pan II §7.1.4); no new statement is made.
proofSteps: (a): the invariants of both sides at an allowable K_{Σ_0} are the finite-level spaces (R31.3/rho-bar-part-and-commuting-actions(c)); after inverting p the map has dense image because at classical points the locally algebraic vectors are sums of copies of ρ(𝔭) (R31.2/locally-algebraic-vectors-of-completed-cohomology) and these are dense (R31.2/density-of-algebraic-vectors); both sides are admissible, so the image is closed (Schneider–Teitelbaum), hence surjective; injectivity mod ϖ on m-torsion holds since ρ̄ ⊗ Hom(ρ̄, −) → (−) is injective for absolutely irreducible ρ̄; conclude by EM11 Lemma 3.1.6 (EM11 Proposition 5.5.3, Corollary 5.5.9; the finite-level analogue is Carayol’s Theorem 4).

(b): Frob_ℓ ↦ ℓS_ℓ extends to a continuous character of G_{Q,Σ}; the Eichler–Shimura relation on H^1 gives ρ(Frob_ℓ)(v) ⊗ (T_ℓ − tr ρ(Frob_ℓ))u + v ⊗ (ℓS_ℓ − det ρ(Frob_ℓ))u = 0 on ρ ⊗ U; at non-scalar ρ(Frob_ℓ) both factors vanish, Chebotarev extends to all ℓ ∉ Σ (EM11 Proposition 6.1.12, Remark 6.1.15, Corollary 6.1.16).
(c) is (b) rewritten with Pan’s twist (LocallyAnalyticCompletedCohomology request, citing Pan I §6.1.1 and Pan II §7.1.4).

sources.match: The Galois action factors out of the ρ̄-part: Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ ρ^m_Σ ⊗ U_Σ, proved by density at classical points, closedness of images of admissible maps, and injectivity mod ϖ on m-torsion.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.1.12 and its proof, p. 68; Remark 6.1.15 and Corollary 6.1.16, p. 69
sources.match: For absolutely irreducible ρ, every G_Q-map from ρ into Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_E lands in the 𝔭-eigenspace (Eichler–Shimura relations); nonvanishing forces promodularity.

acceptance: For ρ = V_f attached to a newform f of tame level K_{Σ_0}, Hom(V_f, Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_E) is the 𝔭_f-part and is nonzero.
Non-example: for reducible ρ = ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 the Eichler–Shimura argument gives no equality, since ρ(Frob_ℓ) acts on the span of an eigenvector by a scalar.

nodes.title: Classical points and their Zariski density
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and modular. A closed point 𝔭 ∈ Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}[1/p] is classical if its eigensystem is that of a classical cuspform of weight k ≥ 2; C ⊂ Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}[1/p] is the set of classical points whose Galois representations are crystalline at p, and C(K_{Σ_0}) its analogue at level K_{Σ_0}. A closed point is allowable if it is classical and ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p} is crystabelline, absolutely irreducible and not exceptional (not a twist of a crystalline representation with non-semisimple Frobenius on its Dieudonné module). Then: (a) ⊕_{𝔭∈C(K_{Σ_0})} Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{E,ρ̄}[𝔭]_{l.alg} is dense in Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{E,ρ̄}, and ⊕_{𝔭∈C} Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭]_{l.alg} is dense in Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}; (b) C is Zariski dense in Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}; (c) the allowable points are Zariski dense in Spec T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ and in Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}; (d) for each compact open K_p, T_{ρ̄,Σ} → T(K_pK_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ)_ρ̄ is surjective and the classical points of weight two and level K_p are the closed points of Spec T(K_pK_{Σ_0})_ρ̄[1/p].
hypotheses: Absolutely irreducible modular ρ̄.
(c) uses the eigencurve to deform a non-allowable classical point to allowable ones; the identification of classical points with prime-to-p conductor and crystalline points is Saito’s theorem.
proofSteps: (a): by R31.2/density-of-algebraic-vectors the GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors are dense; their E[G]-span is the sum of the locally algebraic parts at classical points of prime-to-p conductor, which by Saito’s theorem are exactly C(K_{Σ_0}) (EM11 Corollary 5.4.5).
(b): an element t ∈ ∩_{𝔭∈C} 𝔭 kills a dense subspace, hence Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}, and T_{ρ̄,Σ} acts faithfully, so t = 0 (EM11 Corollary 5.4.6).
(c): every point of C(K_{Σ_0}) is a limit of allowable points along the eigencurve; combine with (b) and the eventual isomorphism T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ ≅ T_{ρ̄,Σ} (EM11 Definition 5.4.7, Lemma 5.4.9).
(d) is the surjectivity of R31.3/completed-hecke-algebra-of-the-modular-tower onto each finite level and R31.2/classical-eigensystems-in-completed-cohomology.

sources.match: Classical, crystalline and allowable closed points of Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}[1/p]; density of the locally algebraic eigenspaces at crystalline classical points; Zariski density of C and of the allowable points.
A representation is exceptional if it is a twist of a crystalline representation whose Frobenius on the Dieudonné module has a double root.

acceptance: The point of the weight-two newform of level 11 at p = 3 is classical and crystalline (good reduction at 3), hence in C.
Non-example: a classical point of weight 2 with Steinberg local component at p is classical but not in C.

nodes.title: Hecke algebra of the definite quaternionic tower
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module, fix a finite set S of places containing those above p, the infinite places and those where U^p or D ramify, and let T_S^{univ} = O[T_v, S_v]_{v∉S} (T_v, S_v the double cosets of diag(ϖ_v, 1) and diag(ϖ_v, ϖ_v)). The big Hecke algebra is T_ψ(U^p) = lim_{(n,U_p)} T_ψ(U^pU_p, O/ϖ^n), the limit over pairs with ψ ≡ 1 mod ϖ^n on U_p ∩ O_{F,p}^×, of the images of T_S^{univ} in End(S_ψ(U^pU_p, O/ϖ^n)); equivalently, for F = Q without central character, T̃_Σ = lim_{K_p} T̃_Σ(K_p) is the weak closure of the image of T_S^{univ} in End^cont_O(C^0(X, O)), each T̃_Σ(K_p) being finite free over O. It acts faithfully on S_ψ(U^p) and M_ψ(U^p), commuting with D_p^×; it is independent of S; for U_p pro-p the map T_ψ(U^p) → T_ψ(U^pU_p, k) is a bijection on maximal ideals, so T_ψ(U^p) ≅ ∏_{i=1}^r T_ψ(U^p)_{m_i} with each factor m_i-adically complete and separated, and S_ψ(U^p) ≅ ⊕_i S_ψ(U^p)_{m_i}. A continuous r: G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(R) is associated with a continuous φ: T̃_Σ → R if det(X − r(Frob_ℓ)) = X^2 − φ(T_ℓ)X + ℓφ(S_ℓ) for all ℓ ∉ Σ, and r̄: G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(k) is modular of tame level K^p if it is associated with T̃_Σ → T̃_Σ/m for a maximal ideal m with residue field k (DLB Définition 5.2). For m with residual representation absolutely irreducible on G_{Q_p} (DLB’s hypothesis), A = T̃_{Σ,m} is a flat local noetherian reduced O-algebra with residue field k, a direct factor of T̃_Σ, and for a T̃_Σ-module M, M_m = A ⊗_{T̃_Σ} M is a direct factor of M (DLB Définition 5.3).
hypotheses: D definite, split above p; p splits completely in F.

DLB assert the properties of A (flat, local, noetherian, reduced) without proof; noetherianity is used in R31.4 and follows from the surjection of a universal (pseudo)deformation ring onto A (R31.3/deformation-to-hecke-surjection in the quaternionic form).
proofSteps: The big Hecke algebra is the CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/completed-hecke-algebra of the finite discrete tower of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module; the finite images are commutative finite O-algebras (R18.3).

Semilocality: a maximal ideal of the Artinian ring T_ψ(U^pU_p′, O/ϖ^n) has a nonzero eigenspace on which the p-group U_p/U_p′ has a fixed vector, so it is a maximal ideal at level U_p mod ϖ; Artinian rings are products of their localisations; pass to the limit (Pan Proposition 3.3.6, Corollary 3.3.7; Gee–Newton Lemma 2.1.14; CC.8/completed-semilocal-product). The m_i-adic completeness and separatedness of each factor is Pan’s Corollary 3.3.7(1), proved from the Artinian decomposition at each finite level; CC.8 alone asserts only the finite-image topology.
Independence of S: twisting by a character reduces to finite-order ψ, where the pseudo-representation over T_ψ(U, O/ϖ^n) is classical (Pan 3.3.3).

For DLB’s A: reducedness from semisimplicity of the finite-level Hecke action on S(U, E), flatness since A ⊂ End(C^0(X, O)_m) is torsion-free, noetherianity from the surjection of the deformation ring of r̄ (absolutely irreducible) onto A.

sources.match: The definite quaternionic big Hecke algebra T_ψ(U^p) as a limit of finite-level Hecke algebras, faithful on S_ψ(U^p), with a pseudo-representation, semilocal with product decomposition.

The spherical Hecke algebras at ℓ ∉ Σ, T_Σ, T̃_Σ(K_p) free of finite type over O, T̃_Σ the weak closure in End^cont(C^0(X, O)), compact reduced commutative; A the m-adic completion, flat local noetherian reduced, a direct factor.
T^S_ψ(U^p) is profinite with finitely many maximal ideals, J-adically complete, and the product of its localisations.

acceptance: For F = Q, B̄ of discriminant 2 and p = 3, T̃_Σ(GL_2(Z_3)) is the Hecke algebra of weight-two forms on B̄^*, isomorphic under Jacquet–Langlands to the 2-new quotient of the weight-two Hecke algebra of level Γ_0(2·N).
Non-example: without the closure, the image of T_S^{univ} in End(C^0(X, O)) is not complete and does not contain the idempotents of its maximal ideals.

uses.how: T_ψ(U^p)_m acts on the block multiplicity module m and is finite over the local pseudo-deformation ring.
A acts on C^0(X)_m, and Π(𝔭) is attached to r(𝔭)|G_{Q_p} for 𝔭 ∈ MaxSpec A[1/p].
T^S_ψ(U^p)_m receives the global deformation ring and is patched.
Pan’s nice primes are primes of T_m (input CC2).

nodes.title: Eisenstein localisation and pro-modular primes
nodes.statement: Fix Pan’s §4.1 data: p odd; F totally real of even degree in which p splits completely; S ⊇ Σ_p finite with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p for v ∈ S∖Σ_p; χ: G_{F,S} → O^× totally odd, unramified outside p, with χ(Frob_v) ≡ 1 mod ϖ for v ∈ S∖Σ_p; characters ξ_v of p-power order of the tame inertia at v ∈ S∖Σ_p; ψ, U^p and a character ξ of U^p as in Pan §3.7 (the variant with p-power tame characters). Assume (Pan’s Assumption in §4.1) that T_v − (1 + χ(Frob_v)) for v ∉ S and ϖ generate a maximal ideal m of the variant Hecke algebra T = T_{ψ,ξ}(U^p) (the Eisenstein maximal ideal), and write T_m for the localisation. Then: (a) there is a natural two-dimensional pseudo-representation T_m: G_{F,S} → T_m lifting 1 + χ̄ with determinant χ and Frob_v ↦ T_v (v ∉ S); (b) the universal map R^{ps} → T_m from the universal pseudo-deformation ring of 1 + χ̄ with determinant χ is surjective and factors through R^{ps,{ξ_v}}; (c) a prime q ∈ Spec R^{ps,{ξ_v}} is pro-modular if it is the contraction of a prime of T_m, equivalently if ker(R^{ps,{ξ_v}} → T_m) ⊆ q; the pro-modular primes form the closed subset V(ker) of Spec R^{ps,{ξ_v}}, so they are closed under specialisation; (d) for q ∈ Spec T_m, ρ(q): G_{F,S} → GL_2(k(q)) denotes the semisimple representation with trace T_m mod q; (e) T_m ≠ 0, i.e. m is a proper maximal ideal, whenever the Eisenstein maximal ideal exists for the ordinary quotient (Pan Proposition 5.6.1, an input recorded as a gap). This is a different carrier from the ordinary pro-modular primes of OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.4.
hypotheses: Pan’s §4.1 standing assumptions; p = 3 needs the additional local exclusion χ̄|G_{F_v} ≠ ω^{±1} wherever Theorem 4.1.7 is used.
The definite quaternion algebra is split at all finite places when [F : Q] is even, which Pan arranges by base change.

The existence of the Eisenstein maximal ideal (Pan Proposition 5.6.1, from Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.18 and Eisenstein congruences under ord_ϖ L_p(F, −1, χ̄ω̃) > 0) is not planned here; see the gap ‘Eisenstein maximal ideal for the ordinary Hilbert Hecke algebra’.
proofSteps: (a) is R31.3/hecke-galois-determinant-and-representation(c) for the variant algebra T_{ψ,ξ}(U^p) (Pan 3.7.2 deduces the variant from the untwisted case through the kernel of ξ).
(b) is R31.3/deformation-to-hecke-surjection(b).
(c) is the definition of pro-modularity (Pan 4.1.3, last paragraph) recast as membership in the closed set V(ker(R^{ps,{ξ_v}} → T_m)); closure under specialisation is closedness.
(d): over a field, a pseudo-representation is the trace of a unique semisimple representation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1/algebraically-closed-reconstruction).

sources.match: Pan’s setup for the residually reducible case: the Eisenstein maximal ideal of the variant Hecke algebra, the pseudo-representation T_m with determinant χ, the surjection R^{ps} → T_m factoring through R^{ps,{ξ_v}}, and the definition of pro-modular primes.
The variant completed homology M_{ψ,ξ}(U^p) and Hecke algebra T_{ψ,ξ}(U^p) with p-power tame characters, needed for Taylor’s Ihara avoidance.
Existence of the Eisenstein maximal ideal of the ordinary Hecke algebra under a p-adic L-value condition, generalising Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.18.

acceptance: Pro-modularity is stable under specialisation: if q is pro-modular and q ⊆ q′ then q′ is pro-modular.

Non-example: a prime of R^{ps} not containing the kernel, e.g. a characteristic-zero point whose pseudo-representation is not congruent to an automorphic one at the level, is not pro-modular even if its residual pseudo-representation is 1 + χ̄.

uses.how: The nilpotence of the kernel at a nice prime shows the component through it is pro-modular.
Pan’s pro-modular primes as containment of the kernel, closed under specialisation (input CC2).
After solvable base change the determinant-fixed problem has a nonzero completed Hecke quotient.

nodes.title: Local Langlands families over the completed Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and modular with ρ̄_p = ρ̄|G_{Q_p} satisfying Assumption 3.3.1 (ρ̄_p is not a twist of an extension of ε̄ by the trivial character, split or not). (a) Let π̄ be the finite-length admissible smooth k-representation of G = GL_2(Q_p) attached to ρ̄_p by Colmez (MF(π̄) ≅ ρ̄_p, central character det(ρ̄_p)ε̄, no finite-dimensional subobject or quotient). There is a deformation π^m_Σ of π̄ to an admissible G-representation on an orthonormalizable T_{ρ̄,Σ}-module, unique up to isomorphism, with MF(π^m_Σ) ≅ ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_p} and central character det(ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_p})ε; for 𝔭 ∈ Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}, π(𝔭)° = π^m_Σ/𝔭 and π(𝔭) = κ(𝔭) ⊗ π^m_Σ, and at closed points π(𝔭) = B(ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p}). (b) For ℓ ∈ Σ_0 there is a unique smooth admissible T_{ρ̄,Σ}-representation π^m_ℓ of GL_2(Q_ℓ) which is T_{ρ̄,Σ}-torsion-free, co-Whittaker, and at each minimal prime a has κ(a) ⊗ π^m_ℓ ≅ π̃(ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_ℓ} ⊗ κ(a)) (the smooth contragredient of the generic local Langlands representation); π̃^m_{Σ_0} is the maximal torsion-free quotient of ⊗_{ℓ∈Σ_0} π̃^m_ℓ and π^m_{Σ_0} its contragredient, a coadmissible T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_{Σ_0}]-module; this is Emerton’s π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ), which exists, and for p > 2 satisfies (π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ)/ϖ)[m] ≅ ⊗_{ℓ∈Σ_0} π(ρ̄|G_{Q_ℓ}) (mod p local Langlands of Emerton–Helm). (c) Φ_{Σ_0}(π^m_{Σ_0}) ≅ T_{ρ̄,Σ} for the composite of the Kirillov (top derivative) functors, and End_{T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_{Σ_0}]}(M ⊗ π^m_{Σ_0}) = End(M) for every T_{ρ̄,Σ}-module M.
hypotheses: Assumption 3.3.1 on ρ̄_p is needed for Colmez’s π̄ and Kisin’s equivalence; when End(ρ̄_p) ≠ k, Def(π̄) is not representable and π^m_Σ is defined through the subfunctor Def^*(π̄) ↪ Def(ρ̄_p).
In (b) the residue characteristic of the coefficients is p ≠ ℓ; the p = 2 mod-p statement is weaker (EM11 Remark 6.1.3: an embedding, an isomorphism when ρ̄|G_{Q_ℓ} is non-scalar).
ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_p} lies in Def^{crys}(ρ̄_p) because crystalline points are Zariski dense (R31.3/classical-points-and-zariski-density); this is what makes Kisin’s equivalence applicable.
proofSteps: (a): Colmez’s Theorem (EM11 Theorem 3.3.2) gives π̄; Kisin’s Theorem (EM11 Theorem 3.3.13) gives a fully faithful Def^*(π̄) ↪ Def(ρ̄_p) restricting to an equivalence Def^{crys}(π̄) ≅ Def^{crys}(ρ̄_p); apply it to ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_p}, which is in Def^{crys} by density of crystalline points (EM11 §6.1 first paragraphs) — these local inputs are requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.3 and R30.5.
π(𝔭) = B(ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p}) at closed points is the definition of B in the deformation-theoretic correspondence (EM11 Definition 6.1.1, Remark 3.3.19).

(b): uniqueness and existence of the co-Whittaker family are Emerton–Helm (EM11 Theorem 4.4.1, Definition 4.4.2, Theorem 6.1.2; NAK §2.2 with Theorem B.11), whose integral GL_n theory is SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5 (co-Whittaker families and the conditional local-Langlands family construction); the mod p fibre for p > 2 is EM11 Theorem 6.1.2.

(c): co-Whittaker families have free rank-one top derivative over their coefficient ring, and endomorphisms after arbitrary coefficient tensoring are scalars (SR.5; NAK Lemma B.10, used in its Lemma 2.6).

sources.locator: Assumption 3.3.1, Theorem 3.3.2, p. 24; Theorem 3.3.13, p. 26; Remark 3.3.19, p. 27
sources.match: Colmez’s π̄ attached to ρ̄_p, Kisin’s deformation-theoretic equivalence between crystalline deformations of π̄ and of ρ̄_p, and the compatibility of B with the explicit correspondence.

sources.locator: §6.1 opening paragraphs, Definition 6.1.1, Theorem 6.1.2 and Remark 6.1.3, pp. 66–67
sources.match: The deformation π^m_Σ of π̄ over T_{ρ̄,Σ} with MF(π^m_Σ) ≅ ρ^m_Σ|G_{Q_p}, its fibres π(𝔭), the family π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ) and its mod ϖ m-torsion for p > 2.
Uniqueness and properties of the coadmissible family π_{Σ_0}(ρ) attached to a Galois representation over a reduced complete local ring (Emerton–Helm).

Under ρ̄_p ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε), p ≥ 3 and End(ρ̄_p) = F: the deformation π^m_p of π̄_p with MF(π^m_p) ≅ ρ^m|G_{Q_p}, the co-Whittaker π^m_ℓ, π^m_{Σ_0} as maximal torsion-free quotient, and Φ_{Σ_0}(π^m_{Σ_0}) ≅ T_{ρ̄,Σ}.

acceptance: At a closed point 𝔭 attached to a newform f with ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p} crystalline and absolutely irreducible, π(𝔭) is the universal unitary completion of π_p(f) ⊗ Sym^{k−2} (Berger–Breuil).

Non-example: for ρ̄_p a twist of a non-split extension of ε̄ by 1 (excluded by Assumption 3.3.1), the expected B(V) is longer than the Colmez correspondence predicts (EM11 Remark 6.1.23), so the family in (a) is not defined.

uses.how: ρ^m_Σ ⊗ π^m_Σ ⊗̃ π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ) is the source of the refined local–global isomorphism.
The same three families give the dual description of completed Borel–Moore homology.
θ ranges over deformations of π̄ such as π^m_Σ.

nodes.title: Fibres of the away-from-p family (Mazur’s principle in families)
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of R31.4/local-langlands-families-over-the-hecke-algebra, for every closed point 𝔭 ∈ Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}[1/p] there is an isomorphism π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ)[𝔭] ≅ π_{Σ_0}(ρ(𝔭)°), hence E ⊗_O π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ)[𝔭] ≅ ⊗_{ℓ∈Σ_0} π_ℓ(ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_ℓ}) (Emerton’s Conjecture 6.1.4, proved as his Theorem 6.2.4). Equivalently: if Σ_0^{ng} ⊂ Σ_0 is the set of ℓ at which ρ(𝔭) is a non-generic principal series and χ makes χ ⊗ ρ(𝔭) unramified on Σ_0^{ng}, then χ ⊗ ρ(𝔭) is promodular of tame level divisible only by primes in Σ_0 ∖ Σ_0^{ng}.
hypotheses: The proof removes one prime ℓ ∈ Σ_0^{ng} at a time and uses that ρ(𝔭)(Frob_ℓ) has eigenvalue ratio ℓ^{±1}, so is not scalar.
It uses the semistable model of X(K_pK_{Σ_0}K_0^Σ) at ℓ, the Néron model of its Jacobian, and the Eisenstein property of the component group (Ribet), after localising at the non-Eisenstein m.
proofSteps: Reduce to removing one ℓ with ρ(𝔭) unramified non-generic principal series at ℓ, at Iwahori level J_ℓ (EM11 Remark 6.1.5 and proof of Theorem 6.2.4).

Adjoin U_ℓ to get T(K_{Σ_0})^*_ρ̄ (finite over T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄); refine the embedding ρ(𝔭) ↪ Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{E,ρ̄}[𝔭] (from R31.4/multiplicity-module, Emerton Remark 6.4.3) to a prime 𝔭^* over 𝔭, landing in the inertia invariants.

Construct the ℓ-new/ℓ-old exact sequence of the inertia invariants, with Frob_ℓ acting by U_ℓ on the new part and the old part ≅ two copies of the level-without-ℓ cohomology, from the Néron model sequences (6.2.9)–(6.2.11): the component group Φ is Eisenstein (Ribet), so localising at m kills it, and Frob_ℓ acts on the torus part by ℓ^{-1}U_ℓ (EM11 (6.2.7)–(6.2.11)); the semistable model at ℓ is ModularCurvesPartII R13.5 and the Néron-model and character-group sequences are R14.6; the Eisenstein property of the Hecke action on Φ (Ribet 1990, Corollary on p. 140) and the action of Frob_ℓ by ℓ^{-1}U_ℓ on the torus (Ribet, Proposition 3.8) are requested from ModularCurvesPartII R14.6, whose current nodes state the sequences and the good-reduction Eichler–Shimura relation only.

Since ρ(𝔭)(Frob_ℓ) is not scalar, the embedding does not factor through the new part, so the old part at 𝔭^* is nonzero, giving promodularity at level prime to ℓ (Mazur’s principle, EM11 Remark 6.2.12).

sources.locator: Conjecture 6.1.4 and Remark 6.1.5, p. 67; Theorem 6.2.4 and its proof with (6.2.5)–(6.2.11), pp. 72–75; Remark 6.2.12, p. 75
sources.match: The fibres of π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ) at closed points are the expected local representations; the proof is a p-adic form of Mazur’s principle using the Néron model of the Jacobian at a semistable prime and the Eisenstein component group.

acceptance: For ρ(𝔭) unramified at every ℓ ∈ Σ_0 with ρ(𝔭)(Frob_ℓ) of eigenvalue ratio ≠ ℓ^{±1}, Σ_0^{ng} = ∅ and the statement reduces to the existence of the family.

Under p > 2, ρ̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible and ρ̄ p-distinguished, the theorem also follows from Theorem 1.2.3 (EM11 Remark 6.2.12), but that route uses Serre’s conjecture; the Mazur-principle proof does not.

nodes.title: The multiplicity module X(θ)
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of R31.4/local-langlands-families-over-the-hecke-algebra, let θ be a deformation of π̄ over T_{ρ̄,Σ} (an admissible G-representation on an orthonormalizable T_{ρ̄,Σ}-module) such that θ(𝔭) ≅ π(𝔭) at every allowable closed point (Emerton’s Assumption 6.3.1; θ = π^m_Σ qualifies, and θ ≅ π^m_Σ when End_G(π̄) = k). Define X(θ) = Hom_{T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Q×G]-cont}(ρ^m_Σ ⊗_{T_{ρ̄,Σ}} θ, Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}), continuity for the m-adic topology on the source and the inductive-limit topology on the target, with the T_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear action of G_{Σ_0} induced from Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}. For a coadmissible T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_{Σ_0}]-submodule Y ⊂ X(θ) the evaluation map ev_Y: ρ^m_Σ ⊗ θ ⊗̃ Y → Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ} uses Emerton’s completed tensor product ⊗̃ (Definition C.43: ⊗̃ = colim_H of ϖ-adically completed tensor products with the H-invariants, H ⊂ G_{Σ_0} open). Then X(θ) is a smooth, cofinitely generated and coadmissible representation of G_{Σ_0} over T_{ρ̄,Σ} (Definitions C.23, C.32); X(θ)_{ctf} denotes its maximal cotorsion-free quotient (Definition C.37) and closures and saturations are in the sense of Definitions C.6 and C.28. For 𝔭 closed, E ⊗ X(θ)[𝔭] ≠ 0, giving a nonzero G_Q × G-map ρ(𝔭) ⊗ π(𝔭) → Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭] (Emerton’s Remark 6.4.3).
hypotheses: θ must satisfy Assumption 6.3.1 (fibres π(𝔭) at allowable points); then θ(𝔭)^{ss} ≅ π(𝔭)^{ss} at every closed point (Emerton Lemma 6.3.3).

Coadmissibility is Emerton’s notion for smooth representations of G_{Σ_0} over the complete local ring T_{ρ̄,Σ} (Appendix C); it is not the Schneider–Teitelbaum notion for locally analytic representations.
proofSteps: Smoothness: every continuous map factors through Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,ρ̄} for some allowable K_{Σ_0}, using Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,ρ̄} = Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{E,ρ̄} ∩ Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ} and admissibility (EM11 proof of Theorem 6.3.12, from R31.3/rho-bar-part-and-commuting-actions).

Cofinite generation and coadmissibility: the K_{Σ_0}-invariants X(θ)^{K_{Σ_0}} = Hom(ρ^m ⊗ θ, Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,ρ̄}) are cofinitely generated over T_{ρ̄,Σ} because Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,ρ̄} is ϖ-adically admissible over T_{ρ̄,Σ} and θ is admissible (EM11 Theorem 6.3.12, (6.3.7)).
Nonvanishing at closed points: X(θ) satisfies condition 4 of Emerton’s Proposition 6.4.2; Proposition C.36 gives E ⊗ X(θ)[𝔭] ≠ 0 (EM11 Remark 6.4.3).

The completed tensor product, closure, saturation and cotorsion-free notions are those of EM11 Appendix C, whose algebraic background (orthonormalizable and pro-free modules, Appendix B) is CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3 (orthonormalizable coefficient modules and mixed completed tensor products).

sources.locator: Assumption 6.3.1, Remark 6.3.2, Lemma 6.3.3, Definition 6.3.4, Theorem 6.3.12 and its proof, pp. 76–78
sources.match: The multiplicity module X(θ) of continuous T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Q × G]-maps from ρ^m_Σ ⊗ θ into Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}, its smoothness and coadmissibility as a G_{Σ_0}-representation over T_{ρ̄,Σ}.
Evaluation maps from coadmissible submodules, X(θ)_{ctf}, and the nonzero map ρ(𝔭) ⊗ π(𝔭) → Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭] at every closed point.

sources.locator: Appendix C, Definitions C.6, C.23, C.28, C.32, C.37, C.43, Proposition C.36, pp. 103–115
sources.match: Saturation, coadmissible and cofinitely generated smooth representations over a complete local ring, closures, cotorsion-free quotients and the completed tensor product ⊗̃.

acceptance: For θ = π^m_Σ and Σ_0 = ∅, X(θ) is a cofinitely generated T_{ρ̄,Σ}-module and Conjecture 6.1.6 predicts X(θ)_{ctf} ≅ T_{ρ̄,Σ}.
At a closed point 𝔭, X(θ)[𝔭] ⊗ E ≅ Hom_{G_Q×G}(ρ(𝔭) ⊗ π(𝔭), Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭]) (EM11 (6.3.10)).

uses.how: The refined local–global compatibility is the statement that ev_{X(θ)_{ctf}} is an isomorphism with X(θ)_{ctf} ≅ π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ).
The nonzero map ρ(𝔭) ⊗ π(𝔭) → Ĥ^1[𝔭] at every closed point is the input of Theorem 1.2.1(1) and of the global proof of Theorem 3.3.22.
The embedding of ρ(𝔭) into Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{E,ρ̄}[𝔭] starts Mazur’s principle.

nodes.title: Emerton’s refined local–global compatibility
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) be absolutely irreducible and modular, unramified outside Σ = Σ_0 ∪ {p}, with ρ̄_p satisfying Assumption 3.3.1 and p-distinguished (ρ̄_p^{ss} is not the sum of two copies of one character). Then there is a G_Q × G × G_{Σ_0}-equivariant T_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear isomorphism ρ^m_Σ ⊗_{T_{ρ̄,Σ}} π^m_Σ ⊗̃_{T_{ρ̄,Σ}} π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ) ≅ Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ} (Emerton’s Conjecture 6.1.6, his Theorem 6.2.13); moreover X(π^m_Σ)_{ctf} ≅ π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ) and the evaluation map is an isomorphism. In Nakamura’s normalisation, under ρ̄_p ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε), p ≥ 3 and End(ρ̄_p) = k: ρ^m ⊗_T π^m_p ⊗̃_T π̃^m_{Σ_0} ≅ Ĥ^1_{ρ̄,Σ} topologically and G_Q × G_Σ-equivariantly. The weaker statement (Conjecture 6.1.9: an isomorphism with some deformation θ of π̄ with θ(𝔭) ≅ π(𝔭) at closed points) holds whenever ρ̄_p is a sum of distinct characters (Theorem 6.4.20) and suffices for Theorem 1.2.1(2).
hypotheses: p-distinguished and Assumption 3.3.1: the two hypotheses on ρ̄_p; when ρ̄_p has only scalar endomorphisms the conclusion is Theorem 6.4.16, and when ρ̄_p = χ_1 ⊕ χ_2 with χ_1χ_2^{-1} ≠ 1, ε^{±1} it is Theorem 6.4.20 (with Conjecture 6.1.9’s θ).
The converse direction of Corollary 6.4.13 (ev an isomorphism ⇒ (6.4.14)) needs ρ̄_p non-scalar (Assumption 5.7.3), which p-distinguishedness implies.
This theorem uses no globalisation by Serre’s conjecture beyond the hypothesis that ρ̄ is modular.
proofSteps: Criterion (Theorem 6.4.9): for a coadmissible Y ⊂ X(θ), ev_Y is an isomorphism iff Y is T_{ρ̄,Σ}-faithful and ev_Y(m) (reduce mod ϖ, take m-torsion) is injective; then Y = X(θ)_{ctf}. The proof uses Lemma C.46/C.52 and Theorem 6.4.7 (surjectivity of ev_E for saturated faithful Y, by density of allowable points and the fibre computation at allowable points, Proposition 6.3.15).

Trivial endomorphisms (Theorem 6.4.16): injectivity of ev(m) reduces, through absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ and Lemma 6.4.15, to injectivity of every nonzero G-map π̄ → Hom_{k[G_Q]}(ρ̄, H^1_{k,ρ̄,Σ}[m]), which holds because π̄ has irreducible socle in this case.

Distinct characters (Theorem 6.4.20, §6.5): at allowable points with κ(𝔭) = E, ρ(𝔭)° ⊗ π(𝔭)° ≅ F_{Σ_0}(M(𝔭)_O) (Proposition 6.5.2), built into a deformation θ of π̄ by gluing over allowable ideals (Definitions 6.4.4, 6.5.6; Propositions 6.5.11, 6.5.13); conclude Conjecture 6.1.9.

Corollary 6.4.13 turns ev an isomorphism into (6.4.14) with X(θ)_{ctf} ≅ π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ), using Theorem 6.4.11 (identification of X(θ)_{ctf} under Assumption 5.7.3) and R31.4/fibres-of-the-away-from-p-family; Remark 6.1.11 gives θ ≅ π^m_Σ when Def(π̄) is representable (EM11 Theorem 6.2.13).
Nakamura’s form is the same statement with π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ) written as the contragredient of the maximal torsion-free quotient of ⊗ π̃^m_ℓ (NAK Theorem 2.2).

sources.locator: Conjectures 6.1.6 and 6.1.9, Remark 6.1.11, p. 67–68; Theorem 6.2.13, p. 75
sources.match: The refined conjecture ρ^m ⊗ π^m ⊗̃ π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m) ≅ Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ}, its weaker variant with θ, and the theorem that it holds for p-distinguished ρ̄.

sources.locator: Theorems 6.4.7, 6.4.9, 6.4.11, Corollary 6.4.13, Lemma 6.4.15, Theorems 6.4.16 and 6.4.20, pp. 84–89; §6.5, Proposition 6.5.2, pp. 89–94
sources.match: The evaluation-map criterion, the identification of X(θ)_{ctf}, and the proofs in the trivial-endomorphism and distinct-character cases.
Emerton’s refined local–global compatibility in the form ρ^m ⊗ π^m_p ⊗̃ π̃^m_{Σ_0} ≅ Ĥ^1_{ρ̄,Σ}, under (a) ρ̄_p ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε), (b) p ≥ 3, (c) End(ρ̄_p) = F.

acceptance: For ρ̄_p absolutely irreducible (so End(ρ̄_p) = k and ρ̄ p-distinguished), Ĥ^1_{O,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ ρ^m ⊗ π^m ⊗̃ π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m), and at every closed point 𝔭, Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭] ≅ ρ(𝔭) ⊗ B(ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p}) ⊗ π_{Σ_0}(ρ(𝔭)).
Non-example: for ρ̄_p ≅ χ ⊗ χ (scalar) the theorem is not proved; Emerton expects a mod p multiplicity two phenomenon there (Remark 6.1.22).

nodes.title: Emerton’s local–global compatibility theorem
nodes.statement: Let V be a continuous, irreducible, promodular two-dimensional representation of G_Q over E, unramified outside a finite set of primes, with residual representation V̄. Assume (a) V̄ is absolutely irreducible and (b) V̄|G_{Q_p} ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε̄) for every k-valued character χ of G_{Q_p} (∗ zero or not). Then: (1) for some finite set Σ of primes containing p and the primes where V ramifies, there is a nonzero GL_2(Q_p) × GL_2(A_f^Σ)-equivariant map B(V|G_{Q_p}) ⊗ (⊗′_{ℓ∉Σ} π_ℓ(V)) → Hom_{E[G_Q]}(V, Ĥ^1_E), and if V|G_{Q_p} is neither the direct sum of two characters nor an extension of a character by itself, every such map is an embedding; (2) if V̄ is p-distinguished (V̄|G_{Q_p} ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 1)), there is a GL_2(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism B(V|G_{Q_p}) ⊗ (⊗′_{ℓ≠p} π_ℓ(V)) ≅ Hom_{E[G_Q]}(V, Ĥ^1_E). Here π_ℓ(V) is the modified local Langlands representation (Tate normalisation, replaced by its generic constituent ordering when the classical representation is not generic) and B is the p-adic local Langlands correspondence. In the situation of (2) the structure of the summand of Ĥ^1_E (and of its unit ball) localised at V̄ is given by R31.4/refined-local-global-compatibility.
hypotheses: V must be promodular; the theorem itself does not invoke Serre’s conjecture.
The two residual hypotheses are distinct: (b) for (1), the stronger p-distinguishedness for (2); the embedding clause of (1) has its own hypothesis on V (not V̄).
(1) is only GL_2(Q_p) × GL_2(A_f^Σ)-equivariant, for an unspecified finite Σ; only (2) gives full GL_2(A_f)-equivariance.

Emerton’s Remark 1.1.2: the unrestricted conjecture is expected to fail when V|G_{Q_p} is a twist of an extension of the cyclotomic character by the trivial character (B must then be longer, Remark 6.1.23); hypothesis (b) excludes the residual shape of that case.
proofSteps: V corresponds to a closed point 𝔭 ∈ Spec T_{ρ̄,Σ}[1/p] with ρ̄ = V̄ (promodularity and Σ large).
Nonzero map: Remark 6.4.3 (R31.4/multiplicity-module) gives ρ(𝔭) ⊗ π(𝔭) → Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭] nonzero, and π(𝔭) = B(V|G_{Q_p}) (EM11 Theorem 6.2.1).

Embedding: if V|G_{Q_p} is irreducible, B is topologically irreducible (Proposition 3.3.24, from R30.4); otherwise V|G_{Q_p} is a non-split extension of distinct characters and B is a non-split extension described in Propositions 3.4.2/3.4.5; a non-injective map factors through its parabolic-induction quotient (using R31.1’s Lemma 5.1.3: Ĥ^1_E has no one-dimensional G-subrepresentations), and the adjunction between Ind_B and Emerton’s ordinary parts plus the abelian Galois action on Ord_B(Ĥ^1)/Ord_B(Ĥ^1)^{ab,S} (Corollary 5.6.13) shows such maps vanish (EM11 Proposition 6.2.2; the ordinary-parts functor and its adjunction are requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.2).

Pass from Hom(V, Ĥ^1_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭]) to Hom(V, Ĥ^1_E) by R31.3/galois-factorisation-of-completed-cohomology(b) and add the unramified places by the argument of EM-PAMQ Proposition 7.8.7 (EM11 proof of Theorem 1.2.1, pp. 75–76).

(2): Theorem 6.2.4 (R31.4/fibres-of-the-away-from-p-family) and Theorem 6.2.13 (R31.4/refined-local-global-compatibility) give Conjectures 6.1.4 and 6.1.9, and Proposition 6.1.17 with Lemma 6.1.19 deduces Conjecture 1.1.1 for V.

sources.match: The main theorem with its two residual hypotheses, the nonzero (resp. injective) map in (1) and the isomorphism in (2) under p-distinguishedness.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2.1, Proposition 6.2.2, pp. 71–72; proof of Theorem 1.2.1, pp. 75–76; Proposition 6.1.17 and Lemma 6.1.19, pp. 69–70
sources.match: Nonzero map from Remark 6.4.3, the closed-embedding criterion via ordinary parts and Lemma 5.1.3, and the deduction of Conjecture 1.1.1 from Conjectures 6.1.4 and 6.1.9.
The expected failure of the conjecture as stated when V|G_{Q_p} is a twist of an extension of ε by 1.

acceptance: For V = V_f attached to a newform of weight k ≥ 2 and level prime to p with V̄ absolutely irreducible and V̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible, (2) gives Hom(V_f, Ĥ^1_E) ≅ B(V_f|G_{Q_p}) ⊗ ⊗′_{ℓ≠p} π_ℓ(V_f).
Non-example: if V|G_{Q_p} = χ ⊕ χ′ is a sum of two characters, (1) only gives a nonzero map; injectivity can fail because B is then a sum of two principal series whose map may kill one summand.

nodes.title: Mod p local–global compatibility and Serre’s adelic reformulation
nodes.statement: Let H^1_k = colim_{K_f} H^1_ét(Y(K_f)_{Q̄}, k) with its G_Q × GL_2(A_f)-action, and let ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) be absolutely irreducible and modular. Suppose p > 2 and ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 1) and ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε̄) for every k-valued χ. Then there is a k-linear GL_2(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism π̄ ⊗_k (⊗′_{ℓ≠p} π(ρ̄|G_{Q_ℓ})) ≅ Hom_{k[G_Q]}(ρ̄, H^1_k), where π̄ is attached to ρ̄|G_{Q_p} by the mod p local Langlands correspondence and π(ρ̄|G_{Q_ℓ}) by the mod p local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_ℓ) in families (Emerton–Helm); equivalently ρ̄ ⊗ π̄ ⊗ ⊗′_{ℓ≠p} π(ρ̄|G_{Q_ℓ}) ≅ H^1_{k,ρ̄}[m]. Taking invariants under compact open subgroups recovers classical mod p multiplicity one results; the GL_2(Z_p)-socle of π̄ recovers Serre’s weights and the conductor of the away-from-p factor Serre’s level, answering Serre’s question 3.4(2) for these ρ̄.
hypotheses: p > 2 is required: the p = 2 statement is expected but unproved because the mod 2 local Langlands correspondence in families at ℓ ≠ 2 is incompletely understood (Emerton Remarks 1.2.7, 6.1.3, 6.1.21).
The two excluded local shapes are those of Theorem 1.2.3(c); Emerton conjectures the first removable for p > 3 (Remark 1.2.9).

The hypothesis ‘modular’ is used as stated; its replacement by ‘odd’ uses the full Serre conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger, Kisin), a globalisation dependence recorded in R31.6/globalisation-dependence-audit.

Placement: this node was drafted in the decomposition under R31.3 as R31.3/mod-p-multiplicity-and-serre-s-adelic-reformulation; since it is a corollary of Theorem 6.2.13 it belongs to R31.4 and has been moved, with the decomposition reviewer’s placement note discharged.
proofSteps: Theorem 6.2.13 (R31.4/refined-local-global-compatibility) gives Conjecture 6.1.9 for every Σ_0 (p-distinguishedness is the first exclusion).

Reduce (6.1.10) mod ϖ, take m-torsion, use Lemma C.45 and the mod p fibre of π_{Σ_0}(ρ^m_Σ) for p > 2 (R31.4/local-langlands-families-over-the-hecke-algebra(b)) to get ρ̄ ⊗ π̄ ⊗ π_{Σ_0}(ρ̄) ≅ H^1_{k,ρ̄,Σ}[m]; pass to the limit over Σ_0 (EM11 Proposition 6.1.20, proof of Theorem 1.2.6).
The proof uses only the more straightforward classical multiplicity one theorems, not level lowering at p, companion forms, or the harder part of Wiles’s Theorem 2.1(ii) (EM11 Remarks 1.2.8, 6.2.15).

sources.match: The mod p local–global isomorphism for H^1_k, its expected p = 2 analogue, its relation to classical multiplicity one, and the recovery of Serre’s weight and level.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.1.20, Remarks 6.1.21–6.1.22, p. 70; proof of Theorem 1.2.6 and Remark 6.2.15, p. 76
sources.match: Derivation from Conjecture 6.1.9 by reduction mod ϖ, and the list of classical results not used.
Serre asks whether his conjecture admits a reformulation in terms of mod p representations of the adelic GL_2; the theorem answers this for the ρ̄ it covers.

acceptance: For ρ̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible, π̄ is supersingular and its GL_2(Z_p)-socle is the set of Serre weights W(ρ̄), so taking GL_2(Z_p)K^p-invariants twisted by a Serre weight σ shows Hom_{GL_2(Z_p)}(σ, H^1_{k,ρ̄}[m]) ≠ 0 exactly for σ ∈ W(ρ̄).
For ρ̄|G_{Q_p} scalar (excluded) Emerton predicts multiplicity two (Remark 6.1.22).

nodes.title: Dual local–global compatibility for completed homology
nodes.statement: Assume (a) ρ̄_p ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε), (b) p ≥ 3, (c) End_k(ρ̄_p) = k, ρ̄ odd absolutely irreducible unramified outside Σ ∪ {∞}. Let H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} be the ρ̄-part of completed Borel–Moore homology at levels K_{Σ_0} (the Pontryagin–Schikhof dual of Ĥ^1_{c,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ Ĥ^1_{ρ̄,Σ}). Then: (1) there is a T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Q × G_Σ]-linear topological isomorphism H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (π^m_p)^* ⊗_{T} (ρ^m)^* ⊗_T π^m_{Σ_0}; (2) for A complete local noetherian, deformations ρ of ρ̄_p and π of π̄_p over A and a co-Whittaker A[G_{Σ_0}]-module V, End^cont_{A[G_{Q_p}×G_Σ]}(π^* ⊗_A ρ^* ⊗_A V) = A; hence End^cont_{T[G_Q×G_Σ]}(H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ}) = End^cont_{T[G_{Q_p}×G_Σ]}(H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ}) = T_{ρ̄,Σ} and the isomorphism of (1) is unique up to T_{ρ̄,Σ}^×; (3) under the stronger (a)′ ρ̄_p ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε^{±1}), (b)′ p ≥ 5 and (c), with R_p the universal deformation ring of ρ̄_p and P̃ the projective envelope of the dual of the socle of π̄_p (R_p ≅ End(P̃)), H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (P̃ ⊗̂_{R_p} (ρ^m)^*) ⊗_T π^m_{Σ_0}.
hypotheses: Nakamura’s hypotheses (a)–(c), resp. (a)′–(b)′–(c); End(ρ̄_p) = k makes Def(π̄_p) representable and π^m_p the pullback of the universal deformation.
The duals are continuous T-linear duals; coadmissible modules (Nakamura Appendix B.2.4) are used for π^m_{Σ_0}.
proofSteps: (1): dualise R31.4/refined-local-global-compatibility in Nakamura’s form, using the identification H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (Ĥ^1_{c,ρ̄,Σ})^d ≅ (Ĥ^1_{ρ̄,Σ})^d (NAK Lemma 2.4 and §2.1.4) and Nakamura’s Lemma B.16 on duals of completed tensor products with coadmissible modules (NAK Corollary 2.5); the tame-level duality is CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.3/tame-level-borel-moore-duality.

(2): by Lemma B.10 (endomorphisms of co-Whittaker modules after coefficient tensoring, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5) reduce to End(π^* ⊗ ρ^*) = A, which follows from End(ρ̄_p) = k, End(π̄_p) = k (Emerton Remark 3.3.14) and Schikhof duality (NAK Lemma 2.6, Corollary 2.7).

(3): π^m_p = π_p ⊗_{R_p} T with π_p universal, so (π^m_p)^* ≅ π_p^* ⊗̂_{R_p} T, and π_p^* ≅ P̃ by Nakamura’s Proposition B.26 (Paškūnas’s theory, requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.5) (NAK Corollary 2.8).

sources.locator: Corollary 2.5, Lemma 2.6, p. 25; Corollary 2.7, Corollary 2.8 and its proof, p. 26
sources.match: The dual local–global isomorphism for completed Borel–Moore homology, the computation of its endomorphisms as T_{ρ̄,Σ} (so the isomorphism is unique up to units), and its description through Paškūnas’s projective envelope P̃ under the stronger hypotheses.

acceptance: Nakamura’s zeta morphisms are T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Q × G_Σ]-linear maps out of H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ}; by (2) they are determined by their values after composing with the isomorphism of (1).
Non-example: for ρ̄_p with End(ρ̄_p) ≠ k (e.g. ρ̄_p split with distinct characters), (2) fails: End(π^* ⊗ ρ^*) contains the idempotents of the two summands.

nodes.title: The multiplicity module of the definite quaternionic tower
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module for F = Q and B̄ split at p, let r̄: G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(k) be modular of tame level K^p with r̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible, m ⊂ T̃_Σ the corresponding maximal ideal and A = T̃_{Σ,m} (R31.3/definite-quaternionic-hecke-algebra). Let Π^{univ} be the orthonormalizable admissible A[G]-module with continuous G-action such that Π^{univ} ⊗_A k(𝔭) ≅ Π(𝔭) for every 𝔭 ∈ MaxSpec A[1/p] (local Langlands in families for absolutely irreducible r̄_p), and π̄ = Π^{univ}/mΠ^{univ}, a smooth irreducible k-representation. Define M = Hom^cont_{A[G]}(Π^{univ}, C^0(X, O)_m), with the m-adic topology on Π^{univ} and the subspace topology on C^0(X, O)_m, and its Schikhof dual M^* = Hom_O(M, O) with the topology of pointwise convergence. Then M is O-flat, separated and complete for the p-adic topology, M = Hom^cont_O(M^*, O); M^* is a finitely generated A-module; for 𝔭 ∈ MaxSpec A[1/p], M[𝔭][1/p] = k(𝔭) ⊗_{A/𝔭} M[𝔭] ≅ Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]) ≅ Hom^cont_{A[G]}(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)_m) is finite-dimensional, dual to M^* ⊗_A k(𝔭), and nonzero iff 𝔭 ∈ Supp M^*[1/p].
hypotheses: r̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible (DLB’s Hypothèse); this makes π̄ irreducible and Π^{univ} exist as stated.
Π^{univ} is a local object requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.5 (the deformation of π̄ over the universal deformation ring of r̄_p, base-changed to A).
proofSteps: M is O-flat and p-adically complete since C^0(X, O)_m is (closed subspace of continuous O-valued functions); Schikhof duality gives M = Hom^cont(M^*, O) (DLB Définition 13.3).
Fibres: Π^{univ} ⊗_A k(𝔭) ≅ Π(𝔭) gives Remark 13.4 directly.

Finite generation: M^* is compact, so by topological Nakayama it suffices that M^*/mM^* is finite-dimensional; its dual (M/ϖM)[m] embeds in Hom_{k[G]}(π̄, LC(X, k)_m) ⊂ LC(X(K_p), k) for K_p fixing a nonzero vector of π̄, a finite-dimensional space since X(K_p) is finite (DLB Lemme 13.6).
Finite-dimensionality and the support criterion follow from finite generation and Nakayama (DLB Lemme 13.7).

sources.locator: §13, paragraph before Définition 13.3, Définition 13.3, Remarque 13.4, p. 69; Lemmes 13.6–13.7, p. 70
sources.match: The family Π^{univ} over A, π̄ = Π^{univ}/m irreducible, the module M of continuous A[G]-maps from Π^{univ} into C^0(X, O)_m with its Schikhof dual M^*, the fibre isomorphisms, finite generation of M^* and the support criterion.

acceptance: At a classical crystalline point 𝔭 (Lemma 13.9), M[𝔭] ⊗ k(𝔭) ≠ 0.
M^* is finitely generated over A but not in general free; its support in Spec A[1/p] is closed.

uses.how: The evaluation map (Π^{univ} ⊗̂_A M)[1/p] → C^0(X)_m is shown to be an isomorphism.
Nonvanishing of M[𝔭][1/p] at every closed point is the weak local–global statement.

tests.statement: M is the quaternionic analogue of Emerton’s X(θ): Hom of the universal family into the localised completed module, with T replaced by A.

nodes.title: Local–global compatibility for a definite quaternion algebra
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.4/quaternionic-multiplicity-module (F = Q, B̄ definite and split at p, r̄ modular with r̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible): (1) for every maximal ideal 𝔭 of A[1/p], Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]) ≠ 0 (weak local–global compatibility, DLB Proposition 13.5); (2) the evaluation map (Π^{univ} ⊗̂_A M)[1/p] → C^0(X)_m (ϖ-adically completed tensor product) is an isomorphism; (3) for every maximal ideal 𝔭 of A[1/p], C^0(X)[𝔭] ≅ Π(𝔭)^{⊕r} as G-representations, for some integer r > 0 (Emerton’s local–global compatibility for B̄, DLB Theorem 5.4). The proof passes through the family C of classical crystalline points: σ automorphic on B̄^*(A), unramified outside Σ, with σ_f^{K^p} ≠ 0, σ_p^{GL_2(Z_p)} ≠ 0 and r̄_σ = r̄, giving 𝔭_σ; C is Zariski dense in Spec A[1/p], and for 𝔭 ∈ C the locally algebraic vectors LP(X)[𝔭] lie in the image of Π(𝔭) ⊗ Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]).
hypotheses: r̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible; the argument is Emerton’s, simplified by this hypothesis (DLB §5.1).

The local inputs are Berger–Breuil (for crystalline absolutely irreducible ρ with Hodge–Tate weights a < b, Π(𝔭) is the universal unitary completion of σ_p ⊗ Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a) and the existence of Π^{univ}; both are requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp (R30.4, R30.5).

Emerton’s functional-analytic lemmas on completed tensor products with admissible orthonormalizable A[G]-modules are used as DLB use them (separatedness, closed image, m-torsion of reductions, 𝔭-parts).
proofSteps: (1): by Lemma 13.7 it suffices that Supp M^*[1/p] is Zariski dense; C is Zariski dense (A[1/p] acts faithfully on C^0(X)_m, GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors are dense (R31.2/density-of-algebraic-vectors(c)) and lie in Σ_{𝔭∈C} C^0(X)_m[𝔭] by R31.2/definite-quaternionic-classical-forms) (DLB Lemme 13.8); for 𝔭 ∈ C Berger–Breuil gives Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]) = Hom_G(σ_p ⊗ W, LP(X)[𝔭]) ≠ 0 and the image statement (DLB Lemme 13.9).

(2) injectivity: Π^{univ} ⊗̂ M is ϖ-adically separated (Emerton [33] Lemma 3.1.16), so test mod ϖ; on m-torsion, Emerton’s Lemma B.6 identifies the source with (M/ϖ)[m] ⊗ π̄, which embeds in π̄ ⊗ Hom(π̄, LC(X, k)[m]) → LC(X, k)[m], injective as π̄ is smooth irreducible; every element of the reduction is killed by a power of m (DLB proof of Théorème 5.4).

(2) surjectivity: M^* finitely generated and Π^{univ} admissible orthonormalizable give a closed image (Emerton Proposition 3.1.3 with Lemma 3.1.16); the image contains LP(X)[𝔭] for 𝔭 ∈ C, whose sum is dense.
(3): take 𝔭-parts of (2) with Emerton’s Lemma 3.1.17: C^0(X)[𝔭] ≅ Hom_A(A/𝔭, M) ⊗̂ Π^{univ}[1/p] ≅ Π(𝔭) ⊗ M[𝔭][1/p], and r = dim M[𝔭][1/p] > 0 by (1).

sources.locator: §5.1, Théorème 5.4, p. 26; §13, Proposition 13.5, Lemmes 13.8–13.9, pp. 70–71; proof of Théorème 5.4, pp. 72–73
sources.match: Emerton’s local–global compatibility for the definite quaternion algebra B̄ split at p: C^0(X)[𝔭] ≅ Π(𝔭)^{⊕r}, proved through the weak statement at a Zariski-dense set of classical crystalline points, Berger–Breuil, and the evaluation isomorphism (Π^{univ} ⊗̂ M)[1/p] ≅ C^0(X)_m.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.1.3, Lemmas 3.1.16–3.1.17, pp. 14–18; Lemma B.6, p. 100
sources.match: The functional-analytic facts on admissible orthonormalizable A[G]-modules that DLB cite as [33].

acceptance: For 𝔭 = 𝔭_σ ∈ C with σ_p unramified principal series and r(𝔭)|G_{Q_p} crystalline irreducible, r ≥ dim σ_f^{K^p}.
Non-example: without r̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible, Π^{univ} as stated need not exist and C^0(X)[𝔭] can have constituents not isomorphic to Π(𝔭).

nodes.title: The block multiplicity module
nodes.statement: In Pan’s §3 setting (F totally real, p splitting completely, D definite and split above p, so D_p^× = ∏_{v|p}GL_2(Q_p)), let m be a maximal ideal of T_ψ(U^p) with residual pseudo-representation ρ̄_m, and B_m = ⊗_{v|p} B_{m,v} the block of the category C_{D_p^×,ψ}(O) of compact O[[K_p]]-modules with compatible D_p^×-action and central character ψ attached to (ρ̄_m|G_{F_v})_{v|p} (with the cyclotomic twist of Remark 3.5.3). Let P_{B_m} be a projective envelope in that category, E_{B_m} = End(P_{B_m}) and R_p^{ps,ψε^{-1}} = ⊗̂_{v|p} R_v^{ps,ψε^{-1}} the completed tensor product of the universal two-dimensional pseudo-deformation rings with determinant ψε^{-1}. Define m := Hom_{C_{D_p^×,ψ}(O)}(P_{B_m}, M_ψ(U^p)_m). It carries two actions of R_p^{ps,ψε^{-1}}: τ_Gal, through T_ψ(U^p)_m acting on M_ψ(U^p)_m and the restrictions of the Hecke pseudo-representation to the decomposition groups at v | p; and τ_Aut, through the isomorphism of the centre of E_{B_m} with R_p^{ps} (Paškūnas, Corollary 3.4.12 of Pan) acting on P_{B_m}. When M_ψ(U^p)_m lies in the block B_m, M_ψ(U^p)_m ≅ m ⊗̂_{E_{B_m}} P_{B_m}.
hypotheses: Blocks and projective envelopes are Paškūnas’s theory for GL_2(Q_p) (Pan §3.4), requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.5; p = 3 has a block (containing δ∘det) excluded in Theorem 3.5.5.
The normalisation of Colmez’s functor in Paškūnas’s papers introduces the cyclotomic twist between ρ̄_m|G_{F_v} and the block (Pan Remark 3.5.3).
proofSteps: The category C_{D_p^×,ψ}(O) is a product over v | p of Paškūnas’s categories for GL_2(Q_p) with central character (Pan Lemma 3.4.10–3.4.11, Corollary 3.4.12); blocks containing an absolutely irreducible object have projective envelopes P_B with E_B finite over its centre ≅ R^{ps}_B (Paškūnas, Theorems 3.4.5–3.4.6 of Pan).

M_ψ(U^p)_m is a compact O[[K_p]]-module with central character ψ^{-1} (R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure(c)) and a compatible D_p^×-action, so it is an object of C_{D_p^×,ψ}(O); Hom from P_{B_m} is exact on the B_m-component.

τ_Gal: T_ψ(U^p)_m acts on M_ψ(U^p)_m commuting with D_p^×, hence on m; the Hecke pseudo-representation restricted to G_{F_v} gives R_v^{ps} → T_ψ(U^p)_m (Pan 3.3 last paragraph). τ_Aut: the centre of E_{B_m} acts on P_{B_m}, hence on m (Pan 3.5.4).

sources.match: Paškūnas’s blocks, projective envelopes and their endomorphism rings for GL_2(Q_p), and the product version for D_p^× = ∏ GL_2(Q_p) with the identification of the centre with R_p^{ps}.
The block B_m attached to m, the module m = Hom(P_{B_m}, M_ψ(U^p)_m), and the two actions τ_Gal and τ_Aut of R_p^{ps}.

acceptance: For ρ̄_m|G_{F_v} absolutely irreducible at every v | p, each B_{m,v} contains a single supersingular representation and E_{B_m} is commutative, equal to R_p^{ps}.
m/mm is finite-dimensional over k (Pan Corollary 3.5.11 proof).

uses.how: Local–global compatibility is the equality τ_Gal = τ_Aut on m.
m is finite faithful over T_ψ(U^p)_m and is the module patched at a one-dimensional prime.
The block multiplicity module, finite and faithful over the completed Hecke algebra (input CC3).

nodes.title: Pan’s semisimple local–global compatibility
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.4/block-multiplicity-module, if p = 3 assume δ∘det ∉ B_{m,v} for every v | p. Then: (1) M_ψ(U^p)_m lies in the block B_m; (2) the two actions τ_Gal and τ_Aut of R_p^{ps,ψε^{-1}} on m coincide (Pan’s Theorem 3.5.5); (3) m is a faithful, finitely generated T_ψ(U^p)_m-module and T_ψ(U^p)_m is a finite R_p^{ps,ψε^{-1}}-algebra (Corollary 3.5.10); (4) S_ψ(U^p, k)[m] is a D_p^×-representation of finite length (Corollary 3.5.11); (5) if 𝔭 is a maximal ideal of T_ψ(U^p)_m[1/p] such that for every v | p, ρ(𝔭)|G_{F_v} is absolutely irreducible and de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights (ρ(𝔭) the semisimple representation with trace the Hecke pseudo-representation mod 𝔭), then 𝔭 is the pullback of a maximal ideal of a classical Hecke algebra T_{(k,w),ψ}(U^pU_p)[1/p] for some weight (k, w) and U_p ⊂ K_p, i.e. comes from a classical automorphic representation of (D ⊗ A_F^∞)^× and, by Jacquet–Langlands, from a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_F) (Corollary 3.5.12); (6) every irreducible component of T_ψ(U^p)_m has characteristic zero and dimension at least 1 + 2[F : Q] (Theorem 3.6.1).
hypotheses: Pan’s §3 hypotheses; the p = 3 exclusion concerns the block containing δ∘det.

The proof relies on the semisimplicity of the Hecke action at finite levels and compares the two actions only on classical crystalline points; it does not need ρ̄_m irreducible (it covers the residually reducible case).
(5) uses the absolute irreducibility of ρ(𝔭) at every place above p; Paškūnas’s Theorem 1.10 (all irreducible subquotients of the specialisation are isomorphic) is the local input.
proofSteps: (1)–(2) follow Emerton: by the density result (R31.2/density-of-algebraic-vectors(c), Pan Proposition 3.2.9) it suffices to compare the actions at classical crystalline points, where Berger–Breuil and classical local–global compatibility at p identify them (Pan proof of Theorem 3.5.5, Lemmas 3.5.6–3.5.9; local inputs from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.4–R30.5).

(3): faithfulness from (1); finite generation over E_{B_m} by Paškūnas’s Proposition 4.17 (S_ψ(U^p, E/O) is admissible), E_{B_m} finite over R_p^{ps}, and τ_Gal = τ_Aut factors through T_ψ(U^p)_m (Pan Corollary 3.5.10).
(4): m/mm is finite-dimensional, hence of finite length over E_{B_m} (Pan Corollary 3.5.11).

(5): for 𝔭_v the pullback to R_v^{ps}, all irreducible subquotients of Hom^cont(P_{B_m,v}/𝔭_vP_{B_m,v}, E) are isomorphic to one Π_v (Paškūnas), whose locally algebraic vectors are nonzero for de Rham with distinct weights (Colmez); a nonzero map into S_ψ(U^p)_E[𝔭] produces locally algebraic vectors, which are classical by R31.2/definite-quaternionic-classical-forms (Pan proof of Corollary 3.5.12); Jacquet–Langlands is GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.3/global-jl.
(6): Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of M_ψ(U^p)_m/ϖ over F[[K]] equals 3[F : Q], and the dimension formula of Proposition 3.6.12 bounds the special fibre (Pan §3.6).

sources.locator: Theorem 3.5.5 and its proof, Lemmas 3.5.6–3.5.9, pp. 29–32; Corollaries 3.5.10–3.5.12, pp. 32–33
sources.match: Local–global compatibility for the definite quaternionic completed homology: it lies in the block and the Galois and automorphic actions of R_p^{ps} agree; finiteness and faithfulness of m; finite length of the m-torsion; classicality of de Rham points absolutely irreducible at every place above p.
Lower bound 1 + 2[F : Q] for the dimension of every irreducible component of the localised big Hecke algebra.

acceptance: For F = Q (where Pan’s even-degree assumption is dropped in §3) and m non-Eisenstein with ρ̄_m|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible, (2) recovers the R_p-linearity of DLB’s local–global compatibility (R31.4/definite-quaternionic-local-global-compatibility).
Non-example: (5) fails for a 𝔭 with ρ(𝔭)|G_{F_v} reducible at some v | p: such points need not be classical (ordinary or trianguline points of positive slope).

nodes.title: Scholze’s functor and the completed cohomology of Shimura curves
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.1/shimura-curve-completed-cohomology (E_0 totally real of even degree with p split, D_0 definite split at all finite places, D with invariants exchanged at 𝔭 and ∞_0, a globalising π as in CDN Proposition 4.5), let S_{ψ,λ,m} = Hom_{U^p_𝔭}(λ, S_ψ(U^p, L/O))_m be the λ-typical, m-localised definite quaternionic module of D_0 (R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module), an admissible injective GL_2(Q_p)-representation in the block of r̄^{ss} (CDN Propositions 4.7–4.8). (1) There is a natural isomorphism of T_S^{univ}[G_{Q_p} × D_𝔭^×]-modules S^1(S_{ψ,λ,m}) ≅ Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m}, where S^1 is Scholze’s functor from smooth admissible GL_2(Q_p)-representations to D_𝔭^× × G_{Q_p}-representations (the degree-one cohomology of the Lubin–Tate tower’s pro-étale torsor over P^1, with coefficients in the sheaf attached to the representation) (Paškūnas, Lemma 6.2, from Scholze). (2) ρ̄ deforms to ρ_m: G_{E_0,S} → GL_2(T(U^p)_m) with characteristic polynomial X^2 − T_vX + N(v)S_v at Frob_v (v ∉ S), and with N = Hom_{T(U^p)_m[G_{E_0,S}]}(ρ_m, Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O)_m) the evaluation map ρ_m ⊗_{T(U^p)_m} N → Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O)_m is an isomorphism (Carayol–Scholze isotypy). Together these turn a local question on S^1(π) into a question on completed cohomology.
hypotheses: Scholze’s functor S^i is not planned in the atlas: it is the subject of the pending design DESIGN-ScholzeFunctorAndModpCohomologyOfTheLubinTateTower (route of PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-23); this node is conditional on it (gap ‘Scholze’s functor’).

The Shimura curve here is attached to D, ramified at 𝔭; the definite algebra D_0 is split at 𝔭, and the two are related by the exchange of invariants at 𝔭 and ∞_0 (fixed isomorphism (4.6) away from p∞_0).
ρ̄ absolutely irreducible (SL_2(k) ⊂ Im ρ̄_π ⊂ GL_2(k) by the globalisation of CDN Proposition 4.5).
proofSteps: (1) is Scholze’s comparison of the completed cohomology of the Shimura curve for D with S^1 applied to the completed degree-zero module of D_0 in Paškūnas’s λ-typical, ψ-isotypic, m-localised form (CDN Proposition 4.11, citing [55, Lemma 6.2]); the definite-side module is R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module with R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure(d).

(2): the deformation ρ_m is R31.3/hecke-galois-determinant-and-representation(c) for the Shimura-curve Hecke algebra; isotypy combines Scholze’s Propositions 5.3, 5.4 and 5.8 (CDN Proposition 4.12), with the finite-level Eichler–Shimura relation for Shimura curves, which is Carayol’s construction of the Galois representations on their cohomology (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.2/carayol-sigma-lambda-construction), the eigenspace decomposition being HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.4/cohomological-eigenspaces.
The duality (Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m})^∨ ≅ Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O)_m^d of R31.1/shimura-curve-completed-cohomology transports (1) to the integral completed cohomology.

sources.locator: Propositions 4.7–4.8 and Remark 4.9, p. 49; Proposition 4.11, Proposition 4.12, p. 51
sources.match: S_{ψ,λ,m} is admissible and injective in the block of r̄^{ss}; Paškūnas’s Lemma 6.2 (after Scholze) gives S^1(S_{ψ,λ,m}) ≅ Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m}; ρ̄ deforms to ρ_m over T(U^p)_m and Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p, O)_m ≅ ρ_m ⊗ N.
Recollection of Scholze’s functor S^i and his finiteness theorem.

acceptance: CDN use (1)–(2) to show that S^1(π) for a supersingular π has G_{Q_p}-action through ρ̄-isotypic pieces (their §4.1.5).

Non-example: replacing S_{ψ,λ,m} by the modular-curve object of R31.1/the-object-the-conjecture-is-about is wrong: Scholze’s functor relates the definite algebra split at p to the Shimura curve ramified at p, not the modular curve to itself.

nodes.title: The patched module M∞
nodes.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite, n ≥ 1 with p ∤ 2n, and r̄: G_F → GL_n(k) continuous admitting a potentially crystalline, potentially diagonalisable lift of regular weight (automatic after extending scalars if n = 2 or r̄ is semisimple). Choose a suitable globalisation (F̃/F̃^+ CM with each place v | p of F̃^+ split and F̃^+_v ≅ F, ρ̄: G_{F̃^+} → 𝒢_n(k) automorphic, irreducible on G_{F̃}, with adequate image on G_{F̃(ζ_p)}, restricting to r̄ at chosen ṽ | p), a definite unitary group G̃ over F̃^+, a tame level U^p, the localised completed cohomology S̃_{ξ,τ}(U^p, O)_m of G̃ with fixed types ξ, τ away from p, and Taylor–Wiles data Q_N. With R^loc = R^□_{r̄} ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v ∈ S∖{p}} R^{ξ,τ}_{ṽ} (the framed local ring at p unrestricted), R_∞ = R^loc[[x_1, …, x_{q−[F̃^+:Q]n(n−1)/2}]], S_∞ = O[[z_1, …, z_{n^2#T}, y_1, …, y_q]], K = GL_n(O_F) and G = GL_n(F), the patching construction produces a compact O-module M_∞ with commuting actions of R_∞ and G (and of S_∞ through a map S_∞ → R_∞), such that: (1) M_∞ is finitely generated and projective over S_∞[[K]], hence finitely generated over R_∞[[K]]; (2) with a = (z_i, y_j) ⊂ S_∞, there is a G-equivariant isomorphism M_∞/aM_∞ ≅ S̃_{ξ,τ}(U^p, O)^d_m compatible with the R^loc-action; (3) M_∞ is projective in the category of pseudo-compact Λ[[K]]-modules (Λ the completed group ring of the centre at the determinant), and M_∞ ⊗̂_{Λ_Z,x} O is a nonzero projective object of the category C(O) with fixed central character. Put Π_∞ = Hom^cont_O(M_∞, E) with the maximum norm, a unitary Banach representation of G with an R_∞-action; for y: R_∞ → O extending a point x of R^□_{r̄}, V(r_x) = (M_∞ ⊗_{R_∞,y} O)^d[1/p] = Π_∞[𝔪_y] is an admissible unitary Banach representation of G. For n = 2 and F = Q_p this is the patched module of Tung’s odd-p work and of Emerton–Paškūnas.
hypotheses: p ∤ 2n; r̄ has a potentially diagonalisable regular-weight potentially crystalline lift (CEGGPS §2.1, Lemma 2.2).
M_∞ depends on the global choices (globalisation, U^p, Q_N, ultrafilter or diagonal subsequence); V(r) is not known to be independent of them or nonzero in general (CEGGPS Remark 2.14).
The globalisation uses Emerton–Gee Corollary A.7 and potential automorphy (BLGGT); these are globalisation inputs audited in R31.6/globalisation-dependence-audit (CC5).
proofSteps: Globalise r̄ (EG14 Corollary A.7) and set up the definite unitary group, its algebraic modular forms and Hecke algebras (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII:PL.2/definite-unitary-group, PL.2/unitary-algebraic-modular-forms, PL.2/unitary-hecke-algebra) and the polarized global deformation problem with its universal ring R^{univ}_S and Taylor–Wiles primes (GlobalGaloisDeformations:G7/polarized-deformation-problem, G7/polarized-representability, G7/enormous-taylor-wiles-primes); the local framed rings are LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.1/local-lifting-ring (CEGGPS §§2.1–2.6).

Define M_{1,Q_N} as the Pontryagin dual of the projected localised forms at level U_1(Q_N)_{2N} with O/ϖ^N coefficients; each is a finite projective (O/ϖ^N)[Δ_{Q_N}][Γ_{2N}]-module with partial G-actions α_N: M_{1,Q_N} → Ind^{G_N}_{KZ}((M_{1,Q_N})_{K_N}) (CEGGPS §2.8, Remark 2.9).

Patch by the Taylor–Wiles–Kisin method (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5/patched-module, R03.5/patched-ring-action, R03.5/patching-extraction): pass to the limit along a compatible subsystem to get M_∞ with R_∞- and S_∞[[K]]-actions and α_∞: M_∞ → Ind^G_{KZ} M_∞; Proposition 2.10 shows M_∞ is finite projective over S_∞[[K]] (splitting a surjection from S_∞[[K]]^r using projectivity at each finite level), α_∞ is injective with G-stable image, giving the G-action.

(2) is the limit of the level-N isomorphisms ψ (CEGGPS Corollary 2.11), whose G-equivariance uses the analogue of Proposition 2.10 for completed cohomology (the degree-zero identification of CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8/definite-unitary-degree-zero, stated there for LLHLM’s definite GL_3; its extension to the rank-n definite unitary groups of CHT/Thorne type is requested from CC.8); (3) is Proposition 4.23 (pro-free over Λ[[P]] for a pro-p Sylow P) and Corollary 4.26.
Admissibility of V(r): (M_∞ ⊗_{R_∞,y} F)^{K_N} is finite-dimensional because M_∞ is finite over S_∞[[K]] and ker y induces an open ideal of S_∞ (CEGGPS Proposition 2.13).

sources.locator: §2.1, Lemma 2.2, pp. 15–17; §2.8 and Remark 2.9, pp. 24–26; definitions of R_∞ and S_∞, p. 27
sources.match: The globalisation of r̄, the finite-level modules M_{1,Q_N} with partial G-actions, and the patching rings R_∞ = R^loc[[x]] and S_∞ = O[[z, y]].

sources.locator: Proposition 2.10, p. 30; Corollary 2.11, p. 33; §2.12 and Proposition 2.13, Remark 2.14, pp. 33–34
sources.match: M_∞ is finitely generated projective over S_∞[[K]] with a G-action; M_∞/aM_∞ recovers the dual of localised completed cohomology; V(r) is admissible unitary.
M_∞ is projective among pseudo-compact Λ[[K]]-modules, and its specialisation at a central character is a nonzero projective object of C(O).
Π_∞ := Hom^cont(M_∞, E) with the maximum norm is a unitary Banach representation of GL_n(K) with an action of R_∞ ≅ R^□_ρ̄ ⊗̂ R^℘_∞.

sources.locator: §3, Definition 3.2 and the definition of Π_∞, Π_y, pp. 9–10
sources.match: For n = 2, F = Q_p: Π_y = Π_∞[𝔪_y] is admissible unitary (CEGGPS Proposition 2.13); the support of M_∞(σ) defines the automorphic components.

acceptance: For n = 1 the construction degenerates to local class field theory: M_∞ is free of rank one over R_∞[[K]]-coinvariant data and V(r) is the character attached to r by local reciprocity.
