nodes.title: Type-specialised patched modules and their support
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.5/ceggps-patched-module, for a K-stable O-lattice σ° in a locally algebraic type σ = σ^{(cr)}(λ, τ) (algebraic of highest weight λ tensored with the K-type attached to an inertial type τ by the inertial local Langlands correspondence), put M_∞(σ°) = (Hom^cont_{O[[K]]}(M_∞, (σ°)^d))^d ≅ lim_n Hom^cont_{O[[K]]}(M_∞, (σ°/ϖ^n)^∨)^∨. Let R_∞(σ)′ = R_∞ ⊗_{R^□_{r̄}} R^□_{r̄}(σ) (potentially crystalline ring of type σ) and R_∞(σ) the quotient acting faithfully on M_∞(σ°). Then: (1) R_∞(σ) is a reduced O-torsion-free quotient of R_∞(σ)′; (2) M_∞(σ°) is finitely generated over R_∞(σ) and Cohen–Macaulay, M_∞(σ°)[1/p] is locally free of rank one over R_∞(σ)[1/p] (in the potentially crystalline case; over the regular locus of the support in Tung’s potentially semistable variant), and the topology is the m-adic one; (3) the support of M_∞(σ°) in Spec R_∞(σ)′ is a union of irreducible components (its automorphic components); (4) the Hecke algebra H(σ) = End_G(c-Ind^G_K σ) acts on M_∞(σ°)[1/p] through the map H(σ) → R^□_{r̄}(σ)[1/p] interpolating the Bernstein-centre local Langlands correspondence (local–global compatibility at p); (5) if x is a closed point of Spec R_∞(σ)[1/p] with π_sm(r_x) generic, then V(r_x)_{l.alg} ≅ π_sm(r_x) ⊗ π_alg(r_x), the Breuil–Schneider representation.
hypotheses: σ potentially crystalline (σ^{cr}) in CEGGPS; Tung’s and Pyvovarov’s potentially semistable variants σ(λ, τ) give the same statements with ‘regular locus of the support’ in (2).
Genericity of π_sm(r_x) is needed in (5).
proofSteps: M_∞(σ°) is finite projective (free) over S_∞, being a direct summand of Hom(S_∞[[K]]^r, (σ°)^d)^d (CEGGPS proof of Lemma 4.18); the comparison with completed homology modulo a is R31.2/type-specialised-quaternionic-modules’ unitary analogue (CEGGPS Lemma 4.14, Remark 4.16).

(1)–(3): classical local–global compatibility at ṽ | p at finite auxiliary levels shows the R_∞-action factors through R_∞(σ)′; Cohen–Macaulayness from freeness over S_∞ and dim R_∞(σ) = dim S_∞; support a union of components by depth (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.6/supported-on-components; CEGGPS Lemmas 4.17–4.18).

(4) is CEGGPS Theorem 4.1 and Theorem 4.19 (the map η: H(σ) → R^□(σ)[1/p] of Theorem 4.1, with its integrality Lemma 4.17(2)), using Bernstein-centre local Langlands (CEGGPS §3, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5 integral Bernstein blocks).

(5): x is a smooth point of Spec R_∞(σ), so M_∞(σ°) is locally free of rank one there; Propositions 4.33–4.34 compute V(r_x)_{l.alg} ≅ π ⊗ π_alg(r_x) with π in the Bernstein component Ω and identify π with π_sm(r_x) when generic (CEGGPS Theorem 4.35).

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1, p. 51; Lemma 4.14, Remark 4.16, Lemma 4.17, Lemma 4.18, Theorem 4.19, pp. 60–66
sources.match: The patched modules M_∞(σ°), the reduced quotient R_∞(σ), Cohen–Macaulayness and rank-one local freeness, support a union of irreducible components, and compatibility of the Hecke algebra H(σ) with the Bernstein-centre map to the potentially crystalline ring.
Locally algebraic vectors of V(r_x) are π_sm(r_x) ⊗ π_alg(r_x) for generic π_sm(r_x).
The same statements for the quaternionic patched module in Tung’s 2-adic setting, with potentially semistable types.

acceptance: For σ = the trivial type of weight λ = (1, 0) (Barsotti–Tate, τ trivial), R^□(σ) is the crystalline Barsotti–Tate ring and M_∞(σ°) is the classical patched module of Kisin’s method.
Non-example: support on a union of components is not full support; Cohen–Macaulayness alone does not give support on every component (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6).

nodes.title: Support of the patched module (Emerton–Paškūnas)
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.5/ceggps-patched-module with R^□_{r̄} the unrestricted framed ring: (1) the support of M_∞ in Spec R_∞, defined as V(Ann_{R_∞} M_∞) (M_∞ being finitely generated over R_∞[[K]] rather than over R_∞), is a union of irreducible components of Spec R_∞; (2) the Zariski closure in (Spf R_∞)^{rig} of the crystalline points in the support is a union of irreducible components; (3) consequently, if Spf R^□_{r̄} is irreducible (for instance formally smooth), M_∞ has full support and R_∞ acts faithfully on it; (4) for n = 2, F = Q_p and r̄ not of the form (1 ∗; 0 ω) ⊗ χ nor (for p = 3) a twist of ω_2^2 ⊕ ω_2^6 on inertia, R_∞^ψ acts faithfully on V̌(M_∞^ψ) (Colmez’s functor applied to the fixed-central-character specialisation). Full support on every component is not asserted in general: (1) gives a union of components only.
hypotheses: For a finitely generated A[[K]]-module, Supp_A is V(annihilator); generators over A[[K]] generate an A-submodule with the same support (EP Lemma 6.2).
(4) uses that Spec R^□_{r̄} is irreducible and reduced in the stated cases (Paškūnas, Böckle).
proofSteps: (1): algebraic representations of K capture every projective object (EP Proposition 3.1), so the support of M_∞ is the closure of the union of supports of the M_∞(ξ) for algebraic ξ; each is reduced (CEGGPS Lemma 4.17), and by (2) the support of M_∞[1/p] is a union of components; p-torsion-freeness passes this to Spec R_∞ (EP Theorem 6.3).
(2) follows the infinite-fern approach of Chenevier and Nakamura, with Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen’s patched Jacquet module to make the argument sensitive to the support of M_∞ (EP Theorem 6.5).

(3) from (1) and irreducibility (EP Remark 6.4, Corollary 5.5); faithfulness is read off directly from the annihilator definition of the support, since M_∞ is finite over R_∞[[K]] but not over R_∞ (the finite-module criterion of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6 applies to the typed modules M_∞(σ°), not to M_∞).

(4): R_∞ ≅ R_∞^ψ ⊗̂ Λ_Z; apply (1) to M_∞^ψ ⊗̂ Λ_Z, which carries an arithmetic action, and use irreducibility and reducedness of Spec R^□_{r̄}; then V̌ preserves faithfulness through the Cayley–Hamilton quotient (TUNG-P3 Proposition 3.9, with Theorem 3.7 and Corollary 3.8).

sources.locator: Definition 6.1, Lemma 6.2, Theorem 6.3, Remark 6.4, Theorem 6.5, pp. 25–26; Theorem 1.8, p. 3
sources.match: The support of M_∞ in Spec R_∞ is a union of irreducible components, via density of crystalline points in the support; full support follows when the framed ring is irreducible.
For GL_2(Q_p): M_∞^ψ carries an arithmetic action, V̌(M_∞^ψ) is finitely generated over R_∞^ψ, and R_∞^ψ acts faithfully on V̌(M_∞^ψ) when Spec R^□_{r̄} is irreducible and reduced.

acceptance: For r̄ absolutely irreducible with End(r̄) = k and p ≥ 5, R^□_{r̄} is formally smooth, so M_∞ has full support.
CC5 caveat (GL2ModularityLifting supplier contract): Theorem 6.3 gives support on a union of components, so Tung’s Proposition 3.9 keeps its irreducibility, reducedness and density inputs.

nodes.title: Full support of patched modules for GL₂(Q_p), p odd (Tung)
nodes.statement: Let p > 2, F = Q_p, n = 2 in R31.5/ceggps-patched-module, and fix a determinant ψ. (1) For every closed point y ∈ Spec R_∞[1/p] whose Galois representation r_x is absolutely irreducible, V̌(Π_y) ≅ r_x^{⊕n_y} for some n_y ≥ 1, where V̌ is Colmez’s functor in Paškūnas’s normalisation and Π_y = Π_∞[𝔪_y] (in particular Π_y ≠ 0 for every y); hence M_∞(σ°)[1/p] is supported on every component of R_∞(σ)[1/p] that is non-ordinary at p, for every locally algebraic type σ (Tung Theorem 4.1). (2) If moreover r_x is potentially semistable with π_sm(r_x) generic, then V̌(Π_y) ≅ r_x, so n_y = 1 on an open dense set of closed points (Corollary 4.3). (3) For σ = σ(λ, τ) or σ^{cr}(λ, τ), every irreducible component of R^□_{r̄}(σ)[1/p] is automorphic (meets the support of M_∞(σ°)), except possibly the semistable non-crystalline component when r̄ ≅ (ω ∗; 0 1) ⊗ χ, λ = (a + 1, a) and τ = η ⊕ η (Proposition 4.4). (4) Breuil–Mézard: for each smooth irreducible k-representation σ̄ of GL_2(Z_p) there is a four-dimensional cycle C_σ̄(r̄) of R^{□,ψ}_{r̄}, independent of λ and τ, with Z(R^{□,ψ}_{r̄}(λ, τ)/ϖ) = Σ_σ̄ m_σ̄(λ, τ) C_σ̄(r̄) and the analogous identity for the potentially crystalline rings (Theorem 1.2); consequently every component of R^□_{r̄}(σ)[1/p] is automorphic, the exception of (3) included (Corollary 4.6, through Emerton–Gee’s Theorem 5.5.2). (5) Global consequence (Theorem 4.7): for F a totally real field in which p splits completely and ρ: G_{F,S} → GL_2(O) continuous with ρ̄ modular, ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible and ρ|G_{F_v} potentially semistable with distinct Hodge–Tate weights for each v | p, ρ comes up to twist from a Hilbert modular form.
hypotheses: p > 2. (5) assumes ρ̄ modular (residual modularity); the globalisations inside the proofs (Tung Lemmas 4.3.3–4.3.4 in the dyadic paper, CEGGPS’s potential automorphy, Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty Theorem A.4.1 on the reducible locus) are audited for independence from Serre’s conjecture in R31.6/globalisation-dependence-audit (CC5).
Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty’s Theorem A.4.1 assumes a potentially automorphic residual seed (recorded in the audit).

The local consequence (4) is a statement about local deformation rings proved through global patching; consumers cite it from this node (the PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.6 request explains why R30.6 cannot import it).
proofSteps: (1): V̌(M_∞) is finitely generated over R_∞ (Tung Corollary 3.8) and R_∞ acts faithfully (R31.5/patched-support-is-a-union-of-components(4)); for absolutely irreducible r_x the action of R_∞[[G_{Q_p}]] ⊗ κ(y) on V̌(Π_y) factors through the Cayley–Hamilton quotient g^2 − tr r_x(g) g + det r_x(g) (Theorem 3.7), so V̌(Π_y) ≅ r_x^{⊕n_y} by Boston–Lenstra–Ribet, and n_y ≥ 1 since V̌(Π_y) ≠ 0 (Corollary 3.10) (TUNG-P3 Theorem 4.1); Colmez’s functor and Paškūnas’s theory are requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.3 and R30.5.

(2): an absolutely irreducible subrepresentation Π of Π_y has no SL_2(Q_p)-invariants (Lemma 4.2), so V̌(Π) ≅ r_x, and a multiplicity computation through Paškūnas’s category gives V̌(Π_y) ≅ r_x (TUNG-P3 Corollary 4.3).

(3): by (1) only the components in the reducible locus remain; their points are extensions of de Rham characters, treated through Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty Theorem A.4.1 except in the stated semistable case (TUNG-P3 Proposition 4.4).

(4): from (3) and the Paškūnas/Emerton–Gee equivalence between automorphy of all components and the cycle identities, applied type by type (TUNG-P3 Theorem 1.2), then Emerton–Gee’s Theorem 5.5.2 for the remaining component (Corollary 4.6).
(5): the Taylor–Wiles–Kisin argument of Kisin’s Theorem 2.2.18 and Hu–Tan’s Theorem 6.3 with all components automorphic (TUNG-P3 Theorem 4.7).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.2, p. 4; Corollary 3.8, Corollary 3.10, pp. 11–12; Theorem 4.1, Lemma 4.2, Corollary 4.3, pp. 12–13; Proposition 4.4, Corollary 4.6, Theorem 4.7, pp. 14–16
sources.match: For p > 2: V̌(Π_y) ≅ r_x^{⊕n_y} at absolutely irreducible points (n_y = 1 at generic potentially semistable points); automorphy of every component of the potentially semistable rings except one semistable case, then of all of them after the Breuil–Mézard identities; and the totally real automorphy theorem under residual modularity.

acceptance: For r̄ absolutely irreducible and σ crystalline of weight (k−1, 0) with 2 ≤ k ≤ p, (3) recovers the automorphy of the (formally smooth, irreducible) crystalline ring.
Non-example: (3) does not follow from a union-of-components support statement alone; it uses the p-adic local Langlands input of (1).

nodes.title: Patched completed homology of a definite quaternion algebra
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module (F totally real, p split, D definite and split above p) with a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal m of T^S_ψ(U^p), a global deformation problem S for ρ̄_m (local conditions D_{v,ψ} at v | p, odd conditions at real places, Steinberg conditions at Σ, an auxiliary place v_1) and Taylor–Wiles data (Q_N, {α_v}), the patching of the completed homology modules M_ψ(U^p_{Q_N})_m produces: a pseudo-compact O_∞[[K_p]]-module M̃_∞ with compatible G_p = ∏_{v|p}GL_2(F_v)-action, a patched deformation ring R̃_∞ (a power series ring over R^loc = ⊗̂_{v∈S} R_v) acting on it, and an ideal a ⊂ O_∞ = O[[y_1, …, y_q]] (with framing variables) such that M̃_∞/aM̃_∞ ≅ M_ψ(U^p)_m G_p- and R^S_ψ-equivariantly. For an open ideal J and U_p ⊂ K_p the specialisations O_∞/J ⊗ M̃_∞ recover patched finite-level modules; M̃_∞ is projective in the category of pseudo-compact O_∞[[K_p]]-modules with central character. Pan’s variant at a one-dimensional prime patches the localisation at a prime q of the pseudo-deformation ring instead (patched completed homology, Pan Definition 4.5.6).
hypotheses: Tung’s 2-adic setting: 2 splits completely in F, v_1 chosen so that U^pU_p is sufficiently small; Pan’s residually irreducible §8: p > 2, F with p completely split.

This is the quaternionic analogue of R31.5/ceggps-patched-module (definite quaternion algebra instead of definite unitary group); the general patching formalism is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5.
proofSteps: Completed homology at auxiliary levels: M_ψ(U^p_{Q_N}) is flat over O[Δ_{Q_N}] and its Δ_{Q_N}-coinvariants recover M_ψ(U^p) (Pan Lemma 4.4.2, Corollary 4.4.3; Tung-2 §4.5).
Taylor–Wiles primes for the quaternionic problem (Tung-2 Lemma 4.4.1; Pan §4.3 at a one-dimensional prime) from GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5.

Patch by ultraproducts or compatible subsequences (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5/patched-module, R03.5/patched-ring-action) to get M̃_∞, R̃_∞ and a with M̃_∞/aM̃_∞ ≅ M_ψ(U^p)_m (Tung-2 Propositions 4.6.5–4.6.6; Pan Definition 4.5.6, Proposition 4.5.8; Pan §8.3).

Projectivity: each finite-level module is projective over O/ϖ^n[Δ][K_p/U_p] by R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure(c), and projectivity passes to the patched limit (Tung-2 Corollary 4.2.2 and §4.6).

sources.locator: §4.2, Definition 4.2.1, Corollary 4.2.2, Lemma 4.2.4, Proposition 4.2.5, pp. 18–20; Lemma 4.4.1, p. 21; Propositions 4.6.5–4.6.6, pp. 25–26
sources.match: Completed homology M_ψ(U^p) of the definite quaternionic tower, its projectivity, the big Hecke algebra and ρ_m, Taylor–Wiles data, and the patched module M̃_∞ with M̃_∞/a ≅ M_ψ(U^p)_m.

sources.locator: §4.4, Lemma 4.4.2, Corollary 4.4.3; §4.5, Definition 4.5.6, Proposition 4.5.8, pp. 52–59; §8.2–8.3, pp. 126–129
sources.match: Completed homology with auxiliary levels, patched completed homology at a one-dimensional prime, and patching of completed homology in the residually irreducible case.

acceptance: Specialising M̃_∞ at the augmentation ideal and at a locally algebraic type σ gives the type-specialised module of R31.2/type-specialised-quaternionic-modules.
Gee–Newton’s patched complex (CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.4/patched-perfect-model-import) is the higher-degree analogue; in degree zero the complex is the module M̃_∞.

Full support of the patched completed homology at a nice prime, resp. in the residually irreducible case.

nodes.title: Full support at p = 2 (Tung)
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.5/quaternionic-patched-completed-homology with p = 2 splitting completely in F (F_v ≅ Q_2 for v | 2), ρ̄ modular with non-solvable image, totally odd fixed determinant ψε, odd deformation conditions at the real places, Steinberg conditions at Σ and the auxiliary place v_1: (1) (Lemma 5.3.2) for a locally algebraic type σ the following are equivalent: (a) the support of M̃_∞(σ°)[1/2] meets every irreducible component of Spec R^loc(σ)[1/2]; (b) M̃_∞(σ°)[1/2] is a faithful R̃_∞(σ)[1/2]-module, locally free of rank one over the regular locus of its support; (c) R^S_ψ(σ) is a finite O-algebra and M(σ)[1/2] is a faithful R^S_ψ(σ)[1/2]-module (M(σ) the type-specialised finite-level module of R31.2/type-specialised-quaternionic-modules); (d)–(e) the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity, resp. cycle, of R̃_∞^{inv}(σ)/ϖ equals Σ_a m_a μ′_a(ρ̄), resp. Σ_a m_a Z′_a(ρ̄), over Serre weights a with multiplicities m_a in σ̄; (2) (Theorem 6.3.7) for y with r_x absolutely irreducible, V̌(Π_y) ≅ r_x^{⊕n_y}, so M̃_∞(σ°)[1/2] is supported on every non-ordinary component of R̃_∞(σ)[1/2]; (3) (Theorem 7.3.1) ordinary components are reached by an ordinary R = T theorem constructing automorphic ordinary lifts; (4) (Theorem 8.0.1) for every locally algebraic type σ, the support of M̃_∞(σ°)[1/2] meets every irreducible component of R̃_∞(σ)[1/2]; consequently the 2-adic Breuil–Mézard conjecture holds for every ρ̄: G_{Q_2} → GL_2(k) (Corollary 8.0.2, the local consequence owned by PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.6), new when ρ̄ ≅ (χ ∗; 0 χ).
hypotheses: p = 2 splits completely in F; ρ̄ automorphic with non-solvable image; the conditions at real places are the odd deformation conditions; the globalisation of a given local ρ̄ (Tung-2 Lemma 4.3.3) cites Calegari Proposition 3.2, Snowden Proposition 8.2.1 and the dyadic construction of Khare–Wintenberger II Theorem 6.1, and Lemma 4.3.4 cites Paškūnas Lemma 3.29 and KW II Lemma 3.5 — audited in R31.6/globalisation-dependence-audit (CC5).

The equivalences in (1) are analogues of Paškūnas’s Proposition 3.17 and Emerton–Gee’s Lemma 5.5.1; (d)–(e) use the Hilbert–Samuel and cycle formalism of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3/R03.6.
proofSteps: (1): standard comparison of support, faithfulness and multiplicities for Cohen–Macaulay patched modules of rank one (TUNG-2 Lemma 5.3.2, after Kisin Lemma 2.2.11, Gee–Kisin Lemma 4.3.9, Emerton–Gee Lemma 5.5.1, Paškūnas Proposition 3.17; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.6/cycle-specialization-multiplicity).

(2): same argument as R31.5/full-support-odd-p(1) using the 2-adic Colmez functor and Paškūnas’s 2-adic blocks (TUNG-2 Theorem 6.3.7, Corollary 6.3.6), local inputs requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.3, R30.5.

(3): ordinary Hida-theoretic R = T on the definite quaternion algebra (the quaternionic nearly ordinary Hecke algebra and its Galois representation, OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1, R21.3) gives automorphic ordinary lifts with prescribed local data (TUNG-2 Theorem 7.3.1, Propositions 7.1.6, 7.2.1, Corollaries 7.2.2–7.2.3).
(4): for each component C pick, place by place, a point of C reached by (2) or (3) (TUNG-2 Theorem 8.0.1); (1) and Theorem 5.3.3 give the cycle identity (Corollary 8.0.2).

sources.locator: Lemma 5.3.2, Theorem 5.3.3, p. 28; Proposition 5.4.1, p. 29; Corollary 6.3.6, Theorem 6.3.7, p. 33; Theorem 7.3.1, p. 37; Theorem 8.0.1, Corollary 8.0.2, p. 38
sources.match: Equivalent forms of full support, the non-ordinary components through 2-adic local Langlands, ordinary components through an ordinary R = T theorem, and full support on every component for p = 2, giving Breuil–Mézard for G_{Q_2}.

acceptance: For ρ̄|G_{Q_2} ≅ (χ ∗; 0 χ), Corollary 8.0.2 is new (not covered by Paškūnas 2016).
Non-example: (2) alone gives only the non-ordinary components; ordinary components need (3).

nodes.title: Pan’s patching at a nice prime
nodes.statement: In the setting of R31.3/eisenstein-localisation-and-pro-modular-primes (p odd, F of even degree with p split, residual pseudo-representation 1 + χ̄ with χ totally odd, the Eisenstein maximal ideal m of the variant Hecke algebra T_m), call a prime q ⊂ T_m nice if (i) p ∈ q and dim T_m/q = 1; (ii) with A the normalisation of T_m/q in k(q), there is a lattice ρ(q)°: G_{F,S} → GL_2(A) with ρ(q)° ⊗ k(q) ≅ ρ(q) irreducible; (iii) its reduction mod m_A is a non-split extension (∗ ∗; 0 ∗) of the two residual characters; (iv) if ρ(q) is induced from a character of G_L for a quadratic L/F then L ∩ F(ζ_p) = F; (v) for every v ∈ S∖Σ_p, ρ(q)°|G_{F_v} is the constant lift of its reduction. If p = 3 assume χ̄|G_{F_v} ≠ ω^{±1} for v | p. Then for a nice q with q^{ps} = q ∩ R^{ps,{ξ_v}}, the surjection (R^{ps,{ξ_v}})_{q^{ps}} → T_q has nilpotent kernel (Pan’s Theorem 4.1.7). Consequently (Corollary 4.1.8): if 𝔭 is a maximal ideal of R^{ps,{ξ_v}}[1/p] with ρ(𝔭)|G_{F_v} irreducible and de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights for every v | p, and some irreducible component of R^{ps,{ξ_v}} contains both 𝔭 and a nice prime, then ρ(𝔭) arises from a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_F).
hypotheses: The nice-prime conditions are stated inline here; GL2ModularityLifting:R32.4/nice-prime restates the same definition for its consumers, and should import this statement.
p = 3 needs χ̄|G_{F_v} ≠ ω^{±1}; the ordinary/residual analysis that produces nice primes on a component (Pan §§5–7) belongs to the consumer GL2ModularityLifting R32.4.
proofSteps: Local and global framed deformation rings at q (Pan §4.2: completions at the constant lift at v ∈ S∖Σ_p are ordinary local deformation rings, by condition (v)), Taylor–Wiles primes at a one-dimensional prime (Pan §4.3, Proposition 4.3.2, Lemmas 4.3.4–4.3.11, using condition (iv) and the irreducible lattice ρ(q)°; GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 treats an absolutely irreducible residual representation and does not cover this case, so the construction is part of this node’s proof), completed homology with auxiliary levels (§4.4).

Patch the completed homology and the deformation rings at q (Pan §§4.5–4.6, R31.5/quaternionic-patched-completed-homology in Pan’s variant; patched pseudo-deformation and representation rings, Definition 4.6.3, Proposition 4.6.16).

Apply Paškūnas’s theory and the local–global compatibility of R31.4/pan-semisimple-local-global-compatibility to the patched block multiplicity module m_∞ (Pan §4.7, Proposition 4.7.7): it is finitely generated over the localised patched ring and of the expected dimension, by the dimension bound Theorem 3.6.1.

Full support: dim(R^{(ξ_v)})′(m_∞) ≥ 4|P| − 1 + r + 2[F : Q] (Lemma 4.8.2) and equidimensionality of the local rings (Proposition 4.2.4) give full support (Lemma 4.8.5, Corollary 4.8.4), hence nilpotent kernel (Pan §4.8).
Corollary 4.1.8 combines the theorem (the component through q lies in the closed image of Spec T_m, so 𝔭 is pro-modular) with classicality, R31.4/pan-semisimple-local-global-compatibility(5).

sources.match: Nice primes of T_m, nilpotence of the kernel of (R^{ps,{ξ_v}})_{q^{ps}} → T_q at a nice prime, and automorphy of de Rham points on a component through a nice prime.

sources.locator: §§4.2–4.8, Proposition 4.2.4, Definition 4.5.6, Proposition 4.6.16, Proposition 4.7.7, Lemmas 4.8.2–4.8.5, pp. 40–70
sources.match: Patching at a one-dimensional prime: local and global deformation rings, Taylor–Wiles primes, patched completed homology, patched rings, the application of Paškūnas’s theory and the full-support argument.

acceptance: Corollary 4.1.8 is the input of GL2ModularityLifting:R32.4/nice-prime-component-bridge (input CC4).
Non-example: for a one-dimensional prime with ρ(q)° residually split (condition (iii) fails), Pan’s local analysis at the constant lift does not apply.

planet.name: Pan’s patching at a nice prime

nodes.title: Pan’s patching in the residually irreducible case
nodes.statement: Let p > 2, F totally real with p split completely, and ρ: G_F → GL_2(O) continuous irreducible with (1) finitely many ramified places, (2) ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible, (3) ρ|G_{F_v} absolutely irreducible and de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights for every v | p, and if p = 3, ρ̄|G_{F_v} not of the form (η ∗; 0 ηω) or (ηω ∗; 0 η), (4) det ρ(c) = −1 for every complex conjugation c, (5) ρ̄ arises from a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π_0 of GL_2(A_F). Then ρ arises from a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_F) (Pan’s Theorem 8.0.1). The proof shows that the patched completed homology m_∞ has full support on Spec R^v_∞ (Proposition 8.4.9) and hence the kernel of R^{(ξ_v)} → T_m is nilpotent (Corollary 8.4.10). When F = Q, hypothesis (5) follows from Serre’s conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger), which gives Pan’s unconditional Theorem 1.0.4 (Remark 8.0.4); that route is a full-Serre consequence and is excluded from any independent proof of Serre’s conjecture.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (5), residual modularity, is retained; replacing it by Serre’s conjecture for F = Q (Remark 8.0.4) uses the full Serre theorem.
Tung’s thesis removes Pan’s extra p = 3 restriction (Pan Remark 8.0.2); that strengthening is not planned here.
proofSteps: Standard reductions by solvable base change: unipotent inertia away from p, N(v) ≡ 1 mod p at ramified v ∤ p with ρ̄ trivial there, [F : Q] even, π_0 unramified outside p (Pan 8.0.5).
Galois deformation rings and completed homology with auxiliary levels (Pan §§8.1–8.2), patching (§8.3, R31.5/quaternionic-patched-completed-homology).

Apply Paškūnas’s theory and local–global compatibility (R31.4/pan-semisimple-local-global-compatibility) to the patched block module: full support (Proposition 8.4.9) and nilpotent kernel (Corollary 8.4.10) (Pan §8.4).
Conclude with classicality of points absolutely irreducible and de Rham at every v | p (R31.4/pan-semisimple-local-global-compatibility(5)) and Jacquet–Langlands.

sources.locator: Theorem 8.0.1, p. 124; Remarks 8.0.2–8.0.4 and 8.0.5, p. 125; Proposition 8.4.9, Corollary 8.4.10, p. 132
sources.match: Fontaine–Mazur in the residually irreducible case under residual modularity, via full support of patched completed homology; Remark 8.0.4 records that for F = Q residual modularity follows from Khare–Wintenberger.
The unconditional consequence for F = Q obtained through Serre’s conjecture.

acceptance: Applied with F = Q and ρ̄ residually modular by hypothesis, the theorem is the residually irreducible Fontaine–Mazur theorem in the form GL2ModularityLifting:R32.4/pan-residually-irreducible-fontaine-mazur consumes (input CC4).
Non-example: dropping (5) and invoking Theorem 1.0.4 instead is not admissible in an independent proof of Serre’s conjecture.

nodes.title: Promodularity and the Fontaine–Mazur and Kisin consequences
nodes.statement: (Corollary 1.2.2) Let V be promodular, continuous, irreducible, two-dimensional over E, unramified outside finitely many primes, with V̄ absolutely irreducible and V̄|G_{Q_p} ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε̄). (1) If V|G_{Q_p} is trianguline, V is a twist of the Galois representation of an overconvergent p-adic cuspidal eigenform of finite slope. (2) If V|G_{Q_p} is de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and is not the direct sum of two characters with isomorphic reductions, V is a twist of the Galois representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform of weight k ≥ 2. (Theorem 1.2.3, Böckle, Diamond–Flach–Guo, Khare–Wintenberger, Kisin) If V is continuous, irreducible, odd, two-dimensional over E, unramified outside a finite Σ, and (a) p > 2, (b) V̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible, (c) V̄|G_{Q_p} ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 1) and ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε̄) for every k-valued χ, then V is promodular of tame level divisible only by the primes in Σ∖{p}. (Theorem 1.2.4) Under (a)–(c), the conclusions of Corollary 1.2.2 hold without assuming promodularity: Kisin’s conjecture in the trianguline case and the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture in the de Rham case.
hypotheses: Corollary 1.2.2 uses the promodularity hypothesis; Theorem 1.2.3 supplies it, but its proof uses Serre’s conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger, Kisin) to know that V̄ is modular (EM11 §7.3), so Theorem 1.2.4 inherits that dependence (R31.6/globalisation-dependence-audit).

Corollary 1.2.2(2) has an extra hypothesis absent from Theorem 1.2.4; under (c) a sum of two characters with isomorphic reductions has V̄|G_{Q_p} a twist of 1 ⊕ 1, which (c) excludes (a deduction, not stated in the source).
Kisin’s parallel result replaces (c) by V̄|G_{Q_p} ≇ χ ⊗ (ε̄ ∗; 0 1) (Emerton Remark 1.2.5); the two are different statements.
Conclusions are up to twist; (1) relies on the proof of EM-PAMQ Theorem 7.5.8, which is only sketched there, and Emerton replaces it by an equidimensionality argument (EM11 §7.2).
proofSteps: Corollary 1.2.2(2) (EM11 Theorem 7.1.1): Theorem 1.2.1(1) embeds B(V|G_{Q_p}) into Hom(V, Ĥ^1_E); by Colmez (EM11 Theorem 3.3.21, requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.4) B(V|G_{Q_p})_{l.alg} ≠ 0, so Hom(V, (Ĥ^1_E)_{l.alg}) ≠ 0 and R31.2/locally-algebraic-vectors-of-completed-cohomology gives a classical form.

Corollary 1.2.2(1) (EM11 Theorem 7.2.1): pass to locally analytic Jacquet modules J_B; for trianguline V each Jordan–Hölder factor of B(V)^{an} has nonzero Jacquet module, so the eigensystem of V appears in Spec A(K^p)_ρ̄, which is equidimensional of dimension two by R31.1/non-eisenstein-boundary-and-injectivity(d) and Emerton’s Jacquet-module dimension result; hence V is a twist of a finite-slope overconvergent eigenform (the Jacquet functor is requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.2).

Theorem 1.2.3 (EM11 §7.3): Serre’s conjecture gives V̄ modular; Böckle’s Corollary 3.8 handles V̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely reducible and the finite flat case; Diamond–Flach–Guo’s extensions of Wiles–Taylor–Wiles–Diamond and Ramakrishna to arbitrary absolutely irreducible V̄|G_{Q_p} give the rest; the p-adic Langlands correspondence plays no role.
Theorem 1.2.4 combines Theorem 1.2.3 with Corollary 1.2.2.

sources.match: The Fontaine–Mazur and Kisin consequences for promodular V, the promodularity theorem with hypotheses (a)–(c), and their combination.

sources.locator: Theorems 7.1.1 and 7.2.1 with proofs, pp. 94–95; §7.3, pp. 95–96
sources.match: Proofs of the two parts of Corollary 1.2.2 from Theorem 1.2.1, Colmez’s non-vanishing of locally algebraic vectors and Jacquet modules; the proof of Theorem 1.2.3 from Serre’s conjecture, Böckle and Diamond–Flach–Guo.

acceptance: For V = V_f ⊗ ψ with f classical and ψ a finite-order character, all hypotheses can be checked and the conclusion recovers f up to twist.
Non-example: for p = 2 Theorem 1.2.3 is not available, so Theorem 1.2.4 gives nothing at p = 2.

nodes.title: Böckle’s R = T for the completed Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) be absolutely irreducible, odd and modular, unramified outside Σ = Σ_0 ∪ {p}. Assume (1) p ≥ 3, (2) ρ̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible, (3) ρ̄|G_{Q_p} is neither χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 1) nor χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε̄) for any k-valued χ. Then the surjection φ_Σ: R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T_{ρ̄,Σ} of R31.3/deformation-to-hecke-surjection is an isomorphism. In particular every deformation of ρ̄ unramified outside Σ is promodular, and T_{ρ̄,Σ} is a complete intersection of relative dimension three over O when R_{ρ̄,Σ} is unobstructed.
hypotheses: ρ̄ modular is a hypothesis; replacing it by ρ̄ odd uses Serre’s conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger, Kisin).
The relative-dimension remark holds only in the unobstructed case (H^2(G_{Q,Σ}, ad ρ̄) = 0); it is not used elsewhere.
proofSteps: Böckle’s Corollary 3.8 (with Diamond–Flach–Guo in the case ρ̄|G_{Q_p} absolutely irreducible): R_{ρ̄,Σ} is shown to be generated by its classical points of weight two and finite flat type, which are modular by Wiles–Taylor–Wiles–Diamond, using that the finite-flat (weight-two crystalline) local ring with fixed determinant is formally smooth of relative dimension one for irreducible ρ̄|G_{Q_p} (Ramakrishna; LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6/export-fontaine-laffaille-irreducible) and a dimension count; the details are EM11 §7.3 and NAK Theorem 2.1.

Since φ_Σ is surjective (R31.3/deformation-to-hecke-surjection) and both rings have the same reduced quotient with dense classical points (R31.3/classical-points-and-zariski-density), the identification of the classical points on both sides gives injectivity once R_{ρ̄,Σ} is reduced, which is part of Böckle’s result.

sources.match: Under p ≥ 3, ρ̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible and the two local exclusions, φ_Σ: R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T_{ρ̄,Σ} is an isomorphism (Böckle Corollary 3.8 and the proof of Emerton’s Theorem 1.2.3).
The proof of Theorem 1.2.3 through Böckle’s deformation-theoretic method and Diamond–Flach–Guo.

acceptance: Nakamura uses this to transfer his zeta morphisms from T_{ρ̄,Σ} to R_{ρ̄,Σ} (his Theorem 1.1).
Non-example: for ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≅ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε̄) the theorem is not asserted; this is the case excluded by Emerton’s Remark 1.1.2 and Assumption 3.3.1.

nodes.title: Locally algebraic vectors of B(V) by a global argument
nodes.statement: Let V_E be a continuous two-dimensional representation of G_{Q_p} over E, de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights a > b. Then B(V_E)_{l.alg} ≅ Sym^{a−b−1}E^2 ⊗ det^{b+1} ⊗ π_p(V_E), G-equivariantly, where π_p(V_E) is the smooth representation attached by classical local Langlands to the Weil–Deligne representation of V_E (Emerton’s Theorem 3.3.22). For V_E crystabelline or a twist of semistable this is Colmez’s Theorem VI.6.50; for V_E potentially crystalline but not crystabelline Emerton’s proof is global: realise V_E (up to unramified twist and extension of scalars) as the local component at p of a classical eigenform whose automorphic representation has a type σ of V_E at p, and compare the locally algebraic vectors of Ĥ^1(K_1^p(N))_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭] computed by EM-PAMQ Theorem 7.4.2 with those of ρ(𝔭) ⊗ B(ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p}) given by Theorem 1.2.1. Only a nonzero G_Q × G-map ρ(𝔭) ⊗ B(ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p}) → Ĥ^1[𝔭] is needed (Emerton’s Remark 7.4.2).
hypotheses: The global proof is placed here, downstream of R31.4, and is exported to consumers of Kisin’s Hypothesis (1.2.6) (input LL3 of GL2ModularityLifting); the local owner PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.4 states Colmez’s cases and must not import this node, or the stages R30 and R31 would form a cycle.
Colmez’s non-vanishing B(V_E)_{l.alg} ≠ 0 (Theorem VI.6.18) and the irreducibility of B for irreducible V_E (Emerton Proposition 3.3.24) are local inputs (R30.4).

The global realisation uses an auxiliary modular ρ̄ with ρ̄|G_{Q_p} irreducible (the reduction of the induction of a Grössencharacter of an imaginary quadratic field in which p is inert) having a chosen Serre weight W, and the weight part of Serre’s conjecture for that ρ̄ (Emerton Remark 5.7.4 notes this is its only use in the paper); it does not invoke Khare–Wintenberger for the representation under study.
proofSteps: By Colmez (Theorem VI.6.42) B(V_E)_{l.alg} depends only on π_p(V_E) and the weights, so it suffices to treat one V′_E with the same π_p and weights; π_p(V_E) is cuspidal since V_E is potentially crystalline and not crystabelline (EM11 §7.4, p. 97).

Let σ be the minimal type of π_p(V_E), τ_0 = Sym^{a−b−1}O^2 ⊗ det^b ⊗ σ_0 and W a constituent of τ_0/ϖ; choose a modular ρ̄ with ρ̄|G_{Q_p} irreducible and W ∈ W(ρ̄) (a CM-induced ρ̄); choosing ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≅ Ind ω_2^{r+1} up to twist when W = Sym^r ⊗ det^b makes W the weight of Serre’s k(ρ̄) = r + 2, so Edixhoven’s weight theorem (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3/edixhoven-weight-theorem, which concerns the minimal weight) suffices to embed W into H^1(K_{Σ_0})_{k,ρ̄,Σ}[m] at an allowable neat level K_{Σ_0} (Emerton invokes the full weight part, Remark 5.7.4, which this choice avoids); lift to τ_0 → Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{O,ρ̄,Σ} by injectivity (R31.1/non-eisenstein-boundary-and-injectivity(c)) and pick 𝔭 with Hom_{GL_2(Z_p)}(τ, Ĥ^1(K_{Σ_0})_{E,ρ̄,Σ})[𝔭] ≠ 0 (EM11 (7.4.1)).

𝔭 is classical (the vectors are locally algebraic of weight Sym^{a−b−1} ⊗ det^b) and its automorphic representation has π_p ≅ π_p(V_E) up to unramified twist by the theory of types (CEGGPS §3, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5).

By R31.2/classical-eigensystems-in-completed-cohomology, Ĥ^1(K_1^p(N))_{E,ρ̄,Σ}[𝔭]_{l.alg} ≅ ρ(𝔭) ⊗ Sym^{a−b−1} ⊗ det^b ⊗ π_p(V_E); by R31.4/multiplicity-module (Remark 6.4.3) there is a nonzero, hence injective (irreducibility of B), map ρ(𝔭) ⊗ B(ρ(𝔭)|G_{Q_p}) → Ĥ^1[𝔭]; taking locally algebraic vectors gives an embedding of a nonzero space into an irreducible one, hence an isomorphism (EM11 §7.4, Remark 7.4.2).

sources.locator: Theorems 3.3.21–3.3.22 and Remark 3.3.23, pp. 27–28; §7.4 with (7.4.1) and Remark 7.4.2, pp. 96–98
sources.match: B(V_E)_{l.alg} ≅ Sym^{a−b−1} ⊗ det^{b+1} ⊗ π_p(V_E) for de Rham V_E with distinct weights; Colmez proves the crystabelline and semistable cases and Emerton the remaining potentially crystalline case by the global comparison.

acceptance: For V_E = V_f|G_{Q_p} with f of weight k and level prime to p, B(V_E)_{l.alg} ≅ Sym^{k−2} ⊗ π_p(f) up to the determinant twist, the Breuil–Schneider representation.
Non-example: for V_E de Rham with equal Hodge–Tate weights, B(V_E)_{l.alg} = 0 (Colmez’s converse); the theorem needs distinct weights.

nodes.title: Globalising a supercuspidal π on a definite quaternion algebra
nodes.statement: Let π be an irreducible supercuspidal smooth representation of GL_2(Q_p) over L (with trivial central character on a fixed uniformiser up to twist), B̄ the definite quaternion algebra over Q of discriminant ℓ (ℓ ≠ p, ramified at ℓ and ∞), and Σ, K^p as in R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module. Then there is a quaternionic modular form f of weight 2 for B̄^* such that, with π(f) its automorphic representation, π(f)_p ≅ π ⊗ (ξ∘det) for an unramified character ξ, and r̄_f: G_Q → GL_2(F̄_p) is absolutely irreducible on G_{Q_p} (Dospinescu–Le Bras Theorem 5.5). The proof uses: (Lemma 5.6) for a minimal GL_2(Z_p)-type σ of π, a GL_2(Z_p)-stable lattice σ_0 and a Serre weight W in the socle of σ̄_0, there is a quaternionic form g whose residual r̄_p is absolutely irreducible with W in the GL_2(Z_p)-socle of the mod p local Langlands π̄ of r̄_p, obtained as the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of the weight-two CM form attached to a Hecke character of an imaginary quadratic F in which p and ℓ are inert; and (Hecke) the automorphic induction of a Hecke character χ of F with χ_∞(z) = z^{-1}, not factoring through the norm, is a weight-two cusp form whose component at an inert prime is the local automorphic induction and whose p-adic Galois representation is the induction of the Galois character of χ.
hypotheses: The CM form is constructed from a Hecke character with prescribed reduction at p and supercuspidal local induction at ℓ; this globalisation uses class field theory and automorphic induction only, not Serre’s conjecture.
DLB’s proof of Lemma 5.6 prints η̄_p where the condition is on the Galois character attached to χ (sourceIssues); the node uses the corrected condition.
proofSteps: Reduce to W = Sym^r F_p^2 (0 ≤ r ≤ p − 1); by the explicit mod p local Langlands correspondence it suffices that r̄_p ≅ Ind_{Q_{p^2}}^{Q_p} ω_2^{r+1} up to unramified twist (requested from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.3).

Choose F imaginary quadratic with p and ℓ inert and a Hecke character χ with χ_∞(z) = z^{-1}, Galois character reducing to ω_2^{r+1} at p up to unramified twist, and χ_ℓ with supercuspidal local induction; its automorphic induction is a weight-two cusp form (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.5/prescribed-local-induction, applied over Q with the prescribed place p, L_p = Q_{p^2}, and with v = ℓ where L/Q is not split and ξ_ℓ does not factor through the norm, so the component at ℓ is supercuspidal), discrete series at ℓ, which transfers to B̄^* by global Jacquet–Langlands (R17.3/global-jl) (DLB Lemme 5.6).

From g, use R31.4/definite-quaternionic-local-global-compatibility (or its weak form Proposition 13.5), exactness of Hom_{GL_2(Z_p)}(−, C^0(X(K^p), O/ϖ^n)_m) (R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure(b)) and Henniart’s unicity of types to produce f with π(f)_p ≅ π ⊗ ξ∘det (DLB Théorème 5.5 and its proof, after Emerton and Breuil–Emerton Theorem 5.1).

GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.3/supercuspidal-globalization states an analogous globalisation in CDN’s setting (B̌ ramified at 𝔭, existence left as a gap there); it is not used: for B̄ over Q with weight two the construction above is self-contained.

sources.locator: Théorème 5.5 and its proof with Lemme 5.6, pp. 26–27
sources.match: A weight-two quaternionic form with p-component π up to unramified twist and residual representation absolutely irreducible at p, built from a CM form with a prescribed Serre weight and Emerton’s local–global compatibility for B̄.

acceptance: For π the supercuspidal of conductor p^2 attached to a regular character of Q_{p^2}^×, the CM form of Lemma 5.6 can be taken with χ of conductor p at the inert prime p.
Non-example: for π a principal series the theorem is not needed; a global form with given principal series at p exists by Hida/eigencurve arguments and has reducible r̄_p in general.

nodes.title: Audit of globalisation inputs and dependence on Serre’s conjecture
nodes.statement: Record, for each result of this roadmap consumed by the lifting theorems, which globalisations it uses and whether any invokes the full Serre conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger, Kisin): (i) Theorem 1.2.1 and Corollary 1.2.2 (R31.4/the-main-local-global-theorem-with-its-two-residual-hypotheses, R31.6/promodularity-…) assume V promodular and ρ̄ modular; they invoke no globalisation beyond that hypothesis, and Theorem 6.2.4 is proved by Mazur’s principle, not by Theorem 1.2.3; (ii) Emerton’s Remark 5.2.3 (allowable levels at the Artin conductor) cites the proof of Serre’s conjecture but, for p > 2, only needs the earlier weak-to-strong Serre theorem; (iii) Theorem 1.2.3 (promodularity) and hence Theorem 1.2.4 use Serre’s conjecture explicitly (EM11 §7.3) — excluded from any independent proof of Serre; (iv) Theorem 1.2.6’s hypothesis ‘modular (equivalently odd)’ — the equivalence is Serre’s conjecture; with ‘modular’ as hypothesis it is independent; (v) Emerton’s §7.4 (R31.6/global-proof-of-locally-algebraic-vectors) uses an auxiliary CM-induced modular ρ̄ and the weight part of Serre’s conjecture for it (EM11 p. 97, Remark 5.7.4), not Khare–Wintenberger for the representation studied; (vi) Dospinescu–Le Bras Theorem 5.5 uses CM forms and Jacquet–Langlands only; (vii) CEGGPS’s patched module uses Emerton–Gee Corollary A.7 (suitable globalisation via potential automorphy, BLGGT) and Proposition A.2, independent of Serre; (viii) Tung (odd p): Lemma 4.3.3 globalises r̄ through Calegari Proposition 3.2 (Moret-Bailly), Snowden Proposition 8.2.1 and, at p = 2, Khare–Wintenberger II Theorem 6.1’s construction (dyadic Hilbert–Blumenthal abelian varieties); Lemma 4.3.4 cites Paškūnas Lemma 3.29 (which keeps a given-automorphic hypothesis) and KW II Lemma 3.5; (ix) Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty Theorem A.4.1 (reducible locus) assumes a potentially automorphic residual seed in addition to adequacy and potentially diagonalisable regular local lifts; (x) Emerton–Paškūnas Theorem 6.3 gives support on a union of components, not full support, so Tung’s Proposition 3.9 keeps its irreducibility, reducedness and density inputs; (xi) Pan’s Theorem 8.0.1 keeps residual modularity as hypothesis (5), while his Theorem 1.0.4 (via Remark 8.0.4) and Emerton’s §7.3 are full-Serre consequences and are excluded; (xii) Pan’s residually reducible Theorem 4.1.7 needs no residual modularity. The audit records what the sources state and what their immediate cited proofs use; it certifies leaves only where those proofs were read, and lists the uninspected leaves as gaps.
hypotheses: The audit is a record of dependencies, not a claim that they are unavoidable; promodularity and residual modularity are hypotheses that can be verified independently.

Leaves read for this audit: EM11 §§6.2, 7.3, 7.4 (pp. 71–98); DLB §5.1 (pp. 25–27); CEGGPS §2.1 (pp. 15–17); TUNG-P3 §§3–4; TUNG-2 §§4.3, 8 (pp. 21, 38); EP §6 (p. 26); PAN Theorem 8.0.1 and Remark 8.0.4 (pp. 124–125). Calegari Proposition 3.2, Snowden Proposition 8.2.1, KW II Theorem 6.1 and Lemma 3.5, Paškūnas Lemma 3.29, EG14 Proposition A.2/Corollary A.7 and BLGG13 Theorem A.4.1 were not re-read in this job; GL2ModularityLifting:R32.6 records the reading of several of them (its request text).
proofSteps: Read each consumed theorem’s proof for its global inputs (leaves listed in the hypotheses) and classify each input as hypothesis, independent globalisation, or full-Serre consequence.
Emerton: §7.3 opens by invoking Serre’s conjecture for V̄; §6.2’s proofs use only the modular-ρ̄ hypothesis and Mazur’s principle; §7.4 uses completed cohomology at an allowable level.
Tung/CEGGPS/BLGG/EP/Pan: as listed in the statement, with the Serre-free status certified only for the leaves read; the rest are recorded in the gap ‘Uninspected globalisation leaves’.
Supply this record to GL2ModularityLifting:R32.6/globalisation-dependency-audit (the existing owner of the lifting-side audit), not a second audit there.

nodes.statement: The exact statements this roadmap exports, by consumer branch: (CC1) type-specialised quaternionic modules and their faithful algebraic module (R31.2/type-specialised-quaternionic-modules), with Pan’s classicality (R31.4/pan-semisimple-local-global-compatibility(5)); (CC2) Pan’s completed Hecke quotient, determinant-fixed pseudo-character with p-power tame characters, pro-modular primes as kernel containment closed under specialisation (R31.3/eisenstein-localisation-and-pro-modular-primes), Tung’s Hecke-valued representation with determinant ψε (R31.3/hecke-galois-determinant-and-representation(c)); (CC3) Pan’s Theorem 3.5.5, Corollaries 3.5.10 and 3.5.12 (R31.4/pan-semisimple-local-global-compatibility); (CC4) the CEGGPS patched module with projectivity (R31.5/ceggps-patched-module), Emerton–Paškūnas support and faithfulness (R31.5/patched-support-is-a-union-of-components), Tung’s full support at odd p (R31.5/full-support-odd-p) and at p = 2 with Lemma 5.3.2’s equivalences and Theorem 8.0.1 (R31.5/full-support-dyadic), Pan’s Theorem 4.1.7 with §§4.2–4.8 (R31.5/pan-patching-at-a-nice-prime) and §8 with its residual-modularity hypothesis (R31.5/pan-residually-irreducible-patching); (CC5) the globalisation audit (R31.6/globalisation-dependence-audit). Branches of GL2ModularityLifting R32: odd-prime residually modular de Rham lifting (Kisin/Emerton, then Paškūnas p ≥ 5 with End ρ̄_p = k, Hu–Tan for split non-scalar ρ̄_p, Tung for all odd p including p = 3) uses CC4–CC5 with the local Breuil–Mézard input LL1 from PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.6; the dyadic branch (Kisin’s 2-adic BT, Paškūnas 2016, Tung p = 2) uses CC1, CC4, CC5; Pan’s p ≥ 5 residually reducible branch uses CC2–CC4; Pan’s residually irreducible branch uses CC3–CC5. Other consumers: KatoEulerSystems L2 (R31.2/completed-homology-with-coefficients, Lemma 2.10 form); LocallyAnalyticCompletedCohomology LA.2/LA.5/LA.12 (R31.1/the-object-the-conjecture-is-about with R31.1/degree-zero-two-and-compact-support; R31.3/completed-hecke-algebra-of-the-modular-tower, R31.3/hecke-galois-determinant-and-representation, R31.3/galois-factorisation-of-completed-cohomology; R31.4/the-main-local-global-theorem-with-its-two-residual-hypotheses and R31.3/classical-points-and-zariski-density for the dense classical vectors with semisimple Hecke action; R31.6/promodularity-… for Emerton’s Theorem 1.2.3); AutomorphicCongruences L3 and TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.2 (through CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.8, not through this roadmap).
hypotheses: Every export keeps the hypotheses of its source theorem; no unqualified ‘p-adic local–global compatibility theorem’ is exported.

The local statements (Paškūnas, Hu–Tan, Tung’s Breuil–Mézard, Kisin’s (1.2.6)) are PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.6’s exports (inputs LL1–LL3), except the global proof of Emerton’s Theorem 3.3.22 (R31.6/global-proof-of-locally-algebraic-vectors).

requests.need: For G = GL_2(Q_p): (i) the categories of admissible G-representations on orthonormalizable modules over a complete local noetherian O-algebra A (Emerton lg §3.1, Definition 3.1.1), with the facts used for completed tensor products: Emerton lg Proposition 3.1.3 (a continuous equivariant map between admissible continuous representations has closed image), Lemmas 3.1.6, 3.1.16 (ϖ-adic separatedness of Π ⊗̂_A M for M^* finitely generated) and 3.1.17 (𝔭-parts of Π ⊗̂_A M), and Lemma B.6; (ii) Emerton’s ordinary-parts functor Ord_B on admissible representations with its adjunction Hom_G(Ind_B^G U, V) ≅ Hom_T(U, Ord_B V) (Emerton, Ordinary parts I, Theorem 4.4.6) and its compatibility with completed cohomology as used in lg Proposition 6.2.2 and Corollary 5.6.13; (iii) Emerton’s locally analytic Jacquet functor J_B with left exactness, as used in lg §7.2.

Colmez’s Montréal functor MF (and Paškūnas’s normalisation V̌) on admissible finite-length G-representations, exact and compatible with central characters; for ρ̄: G_{Q_p} → GL_2(k) not a twist of (1 ∗; 0 ε̄), Colmez’s π̄ with MF(π̄) ≅ ρ̄, central character det(ρ̄)ε̄, no finite-dimensional subquotient (Emerton lg Theorem 3.3.2); the explicit mod p correspondence for irreducible ρ̄ (supersingular π̄ attached to Ind ω_2^{r+1}, used in DLB Lemme 5.6 and in the socle description of Serre weights).

(i) Topological irreducibility of B(V) for absolutely irreducible V (Emerton lg Proposition 3.3.24; Colmez Theorem 0.17(ii)); (ii) Colmez’s non-vanishing of locally algebraic vectors for de Rham V with distinct Hodge–Tate weights (Theorem VI.6.18) and the description B(V)_{l.alg} ≅ Sym^{a−b−1} ⊗ det^{b+1} ⊗ π_p(V) in the crystabelline and semistable cases (Theorem VI.6.50) and its dependence only on π_p(V) and the weights (Theorem VI.6.42); (iii) Berger–Breuil: for crystalline absolutely irreducible V with weights a < b and π_p(V) unramified, B(V) is the universal unitary completion of π_p(V) ⊗ Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a, so Hom^cont_G(B(V), Π) = Hom_G(π_p(V) ⊗ Sym, Π) for unitary Banach Π; (iv) Colmez’s locally algebraic vectors for potentially semistable V in the form used by Tung (Corollary 4.3). The global case of Emerton lg Theorem 3.3.22 is not requested: it is R31.6/global-proof-of-locally-algebraic-vectors and must not be imported by R30.

(i) Kisin’s theorem (Emerton lg Theorem 3.3.13): Def^*(π̄) → Def(ρ̄) fully faithful, restricting to an equivalence Def^{crys}(π̄) ≅ Def^{crys}(ρ̄) (and Def^{crys} = Def under Assumption 3.3.1, Emerton Remark 3.3.14); (ii) the universal deformation π_p of π̄_p over R_p when End(ρ̄_p) = k, and for absolutely irreducible ρ̄_p the orthonormalizable admissible family Π^{univ} with Π^{univ} ⊗ k(𝔭) ≅ Π(𝔭) (DLB §13); (iii) Paškūnas’s blocks of the category of compact O[[GL_2(Z_p)]]-modules with G-action and central character, their projective envelopes P_B with E_B = End(P_B) finite over its centre ≅ R_B^{ps} (Pan Theorems 3.4.5–3.4.6, Corollary 3.4.12), the finite generation of Hom(P_B, M) over E_B for admissible duals (Paškūnas, Image of Colmez’s functor, Proposition 4.17), Theorem 1.10 of that paper (irreducible subquotients of a specialisation at an absolutely irreducible point are isomorphic), and the projective envelope P̃ of the dual of the socle of π̄_p with R_p ≅ End(P̃) and π_p^* ≅ P̃ (Nakamura Proposition B.26); (iv) the 2-adic versions used by Tung.

The purely local statements that the export table hands on, stated with their hypotheses: Breuil–Mézard in cycle form for p > 2 (Paškūnas 2015 Theorem 1.1 for p ≥ 5 with End ρ̄ = k; Hu–Tan for split non-scalar ρ̄; Tung Theorem 1.2 for all odd p) and for p = 2 (Tung Corollary 8.0.2), with the Hilbert–Samuel and cycle formalism of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. Tung’s proofs go through the global patched modules, which this roadmap plans (R31.5/full-support-odd-p part (4) and R31.5/full-support-dyadic part (4) state the resulting cycle identities); since the atlas orders R30.6 before R31.4, R30.6 must not import R31.5: it should state the local theorems with the global input marked as a supplier from R31.5, or the Breuil–Mézard statements proved by patching should be cited by consumers directly from R31.5.

Integral local Langlands in families for GL_2(Q_ℓ), ℓ ≠ p, over reduced complete local O-algebras: the co-Whittaker family π(ρ) attached to ρ: G_{Q_ℓ} → GL_2(A) (unique, A-torsion-free, generic fibres the contragredient local Langlands representations; Emerton–Helm), unconditionally for n = 2; Φ (top derivative) of a co-Whittaker family is free of rank one; End_{A[G]}(M ⊗ V) = End_A(M) for co-Whittaker V and any A-module M (Nakamura Lemma B.10); the mod p fibre statement for p > 2 used in Emerton lg Theorem 6.1.2; and the Bernstein-centre inertial local Langlands for types used in CEGGPS §3. The current Tau Ceti SR.5 states the family construction conditionally on Helm’s conjecture; the n = 2 case is requested unconditionally.

At a prime ℓ ≠ p where the level has Iwahori (Γ_0(ℓ)) structure and the curve has the semistable model of R13.5: (i) the Hecke algebra generated by T_q, S_q for q prime to the level acts on the component group Φ of the Néron model of the Jacobian through an Eisenstein quotient, so Φ_m = 0 for a non-Eisenstein m (Ribet, Invent. Math. 100 (1990), Corollary on p. 140, under the neatness of the level away from ℓ); (ii) geometric Frobenius at ℓ acts on the character group (torus) part of the special fibre by ℓ^{-1}U_ℓ (Ribet, Proposition 3.8). The current R14.6 nodes state the character-group and component sequences and the good-reduction Eichler–Shimura relation only.

Extend CC.8/definite-unitary-degree-zero (stated for LLHLM §5.3’s definite outer form of GL_3) to the definite unitary groups G̃ of rank n over a totally real F̃^+ used by CEGGPS §2.3 (Clozel–Harris–Taylor/Thorne type, quasi-split at finite places, compact at infinity): the completed degree-zero object lim_s colim_{U_p} S_{ξ,τ}(U_pU^p, O/ϖ^s) with its tame Hecke and GL_n(F̃^+_p)-actions is the CC.2 completed object of the finite discrete tower, with the same stabiliser caveat.

gaps.title: Eisenstein maximal ideal for the ordinary Hilbert Hecke algebra
gaps.detail: Pan’s Proposition 5.6.1 (generalising Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.18): under ord_ϖ L_p(F, −1, χ̃ω) > 0, ϖ and T_v − (1 + χ(Frob_v)) generate a maximal ideal of the ordinary Hecke algebra, via Eisenstein series and congruences of Hilbert modular forms. No accepted packet states it (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21 plans the Skinner–Wiles R = T theory but not this congruence, and the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function belongs to the p-adic L-function roadmaps). Here the maximal ideal is a hypothesis; part (e) of the node, nonvanishing of T_m, is conditional on this gap. Suggested owner: OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21 (Skinner–Wiles Eisenstein congruences).

sourceIssues.correction: The condition is on the p-adic Galois character η attached to χ: the reduction of η|G_{F_p} equals ω_2^{r+1} up to unramified twist (F_p = Q_{p^2}), so that r̄_p ≅ Ind_{Q_{p^2}}^{Q_p} of that reduction.
sourceIssues.reason: η is not defined in the proof; the required shape of r̄_p is a condition on the Galois character of χ, not on its local component χ_p. Recorded by PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17/E2.

upstreamNotes.note: Layer SR.5 states the integral local-Langlands family construction conditionally on Helm’s conjecture. For GL_2 the family π(ρ) over reduced complete local rings is used unconditionally by Emerton’s and Nakamura’s local–global compatibility (Emerton–Helm, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 47 (2014), Proposition 6.2.4 in the End(ρ̄_p) = k case); an unconditional n = 2 statement, with the mod p fibre for p > 2, would let CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.4 cite SR.5 without a conditional hypothesis.

Layer 3.2 states Mahler’s theorem on Z_p. The density arguments of Emerton (lg Proposition 5.4.1) and Dospinescu–Le Bras (Lemme 13.2) need it on compact open subsets of Z_p^d (GL_2(Z_p) ⊂ M_2(Z_p)), by tensor products of Mahler bases; a several-variable corollary would serve them.

findingsCoverage.disposition: Fix (a) as adopted by the accepted CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8 packet: the modular and Shimura-curve tower identifications are CC.8/arithmetic-tower-realisation (with CC.8/hilbert-finite-local-system-input for quaternionic Shimura curves), and this roadmap imports them in R31.1/the-object-the-conjecture-is-about and R31.1/shimura-curve-completed-cohomology instead of proving them again; R31.1 proves only the GL_2-specific degree, boundary and non-Eisenstein results.

CC.8 now plans the completed Hecke algebra as the inverse limit of IHG.2’s finite images (CC.8/completed-hecke-algebra), its semilocal product (CC.8/completed-semilocal-product, Gee–Newton 2.1.11/2.1.14) and the residual localisation (CC.8/residual-hecke-projector, CC.8/completed-residual-localisation). R31.3/completed-hecke-algebra-of-the-modular-tower specialises these to GL_2 and identifies them with Emerton’s T(K^p) and T_{ρ̄,Σ}; R31.3/definite-quaternionic-hecke-algebra specialises them to the quaternionic tower. No second construction.

The definite quaternionic tower is planned in full (space of p-adic automorphic forms, Hecke algebras and localisations, attached Galois representation and Banach representations, and Emerton’s local–global compatibility for it, proved by DLB’s §13 argument and in Pan’s generality), importing finite-level quaternionic forms from HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3 and Jacquet–Langlands from GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3; a sub-layer presentation is proposed (restructure entry 2).
